docs.title: Documentation Index
docs.text:
Truth class: current descriptive Last reality check: 2026-11-02 Verification: just docs-check

casa-rs is used from the Python package casars and from the task executables of the application catalog (such as calibrate gaincal ...), which Python also starts for its task calls (ADR-0017). All computation is in Rust, and the Python package is its interface (ADR-0018).

The published site is https://bglenden.github.io/casa-rs/, with the Rust API reference at https://bglenden.github.io/casa-rs/rustdoc/; both are built from main.

At the repository root, ARCHITECTURE.md describes the crates and their boundaries, TESTING.md the gates and evidence rules, and GLOSSARY.md the domain vocabulary.

This directory holds stable reference material. Open work, status and history live in GitHub issues and pull requests.

docs.title: CASA (C++) bugs
docs.text:
Notes on bugs or likely bugs observed while doing Rust/C++ parity work against CASA.

Known imaging parity defect: CASA Högbom niter off-by-one. CASA behaviours casa-rs follows for parity: AW-projection hand pairing, AW-projection prediction w, MatrixCleaner's stop iteration, exact peak comparisons, multi-term weight normalization, the Airy beam's blockage term, the EVLA's 11052 MHz fit, the simulator's and tclean's two mosaic machines, a moved pointing phased on its field, datacolumn='corrected' without CORRECTED_DATA, W projection's sectioned grid edge. CASA behaviours casa-rs does not follow: odd-size scale convolutions, MatrixCleaner's step residual, an unplaceable PB pointing, the cube density's two uvw frames, continuum briggsabs at robust 0 and noise 0, nsigma with fastnoise=False and no mask, single-precision Taylor weights, a mosaic's single-precision weight image, facets of an image size that does not divide, an unflagged non-finite sample, a tuned cube's frequency selection, a cube's fine frequency grid at a whole ratio, the .gridwt a cube leaves, tb.getcol of an int64 column, tb.putkeyword of an int beyond 32 bits, tb slices that abort the process, tb.putcell of an int beyond 32 bits, tb.putcell with several rows, tb.addrows with a negative count, tb.removerows and tb.addcols that fail part way, MSIter's receptor angles for a window without its own FEED row. Simulator behaviours casa-rs does not follow: TIME as TAI, shadowing the front antenna, relabelled spectral-window frames, unconvertible coordinate systems, quantities in the wrong units, calls before setconfig, a zero integration time, readantenna's observatory fallback, readantenna's names after blank lines, the measures tool's default frame, the model predict rewrites, models the simulator cannot read, setmosaicfield's off-centre grid, observemany's rows before an unknown field, W projection without planes, total power in cross-correlations, close after a mosaic predict, the beam on a moved pointing, scratch columns added at predict and corrupt, tsys-manual's stale and borrowed system temperatures, tsys-manual scaling every noise term, the noise term a refused tsys-manual leaves, tsys-atm's atmosphere half a band away, settrop's dispersive delay alone, settrop's atmosphere half a band away, settrop's anisotropic screen, settrop's solutions stamped halfway, gain screens read past their transform, gain screens sharing a seed, random gains about zero, the last antenna's unit gain or leakage, leakage for two windows only, a simulated term's table written when it is set. Measures behaviours casa-rs follows for parity: IAU 1980 sidereal time and obliquities under IAU 2000. Measures behaviours casa-rs does not follow: latitudes of unnormalized directions, IAU 2000 JMEAN to J2000, IAU 2000 GMST1. Simulator behaviours casa-rs follows: observemany's padded single name, one leakage per window for the whole run. Component-list behaviours casa-rs does not follow: a limb-darkened disk without an exponent, a negative component under the primary beam, a single spectral index, the beam's component spectrum frame, addcomponent's single-precision flux, the cl tool's record units. Component-list behaviours casa-rs follows: addcomponent's polarization, a shape addcomponent cannot make. Concatenation behaviours casa-rs does not follow: a merged source record's time, source equivalence decided by its last column, merged sources' numbering, observation IDs after removing duplicates, an input without states, writing into its inputs. ATM data errors casa-rs corrects (tools/atmosphere/atm-corrections.patch): HCN's misplaced line, sea-level air densities, the H2(17)O weight, the HDO weight. ATM behaviours casa-rs follows: HCN above 100 km, copied bottom pressures, unpadded ozone isotopologue layers, (16)O(17)O. ATM behaviours casa-rs does not follow: the averaged non-dispersive wet phase. Calibration behaviours casa-rs follows: a gain table's resolution and total bandwidth. Calibration behaviours casa-rs does not follow: a solve that fits exactly. simutil behaviours casa-rs does not follow: the ALMA tiling's default beam, noisetemp's receiver lookup, directions without an epoch, modifymodel's axis swaps, modifymodel's Stokes labels, incell as two cells, the component-only model's unset width, component spectra in another frame. Flagging behaviours casa-rs does not follow: a re-saved version's comment, a summary of correlations it cannot name. Coordinate behaviours casa-rs does not follow: a tabular coordinate's subimage, a FITS date's time scale, feather on a transposed image. MeasurementSet selection behaviours casa-rs follows: later timerange terms' defaults, FLAG_ROW beside other selections. MeasurementSet selection behaviours casa-rs does not follow: the state a refused bracketed range leaves.

docs.title: AW-projection pairs the partner hand's visibility with the conjugate-baseline cell
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs follows it for parity (#667, PR #668)
  • Affected code:
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines2/AWVisResampler.cc (getConvFunc_p, DataToGridImpl_p, GridToData)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: For a row with w ≤ 0, getConvFunc_p selects the conjugate-baseline cell of the outer correlation's Mueller element (conjMNdx, the partner hand: RR ↔ LL, RL ↔ LR), and DataToGridImpl_p then grids the visibility of the selected cell's hand (visVecElement = muellerElement % nDataPol), not the outer correlation's. The RR grid receives RR × conj(CF_RR) for w > 0 and LL × CF_LL for w ≤ 0; GridToData likewise reads the partner's model grid into the outer visibility. Stokes I of an unpolarized source is unaffected (the two hands are equal); per-hand grids of data whose hands differ, such as a circularly polarized source, mix the hands on the w ≤ 0 rows.

docs.title: Why this looks like a bug
docs.text: The Mueller element of a real power pattern has a Hermitian transform, so the RR kernel at −|w| is the conjugate of the kernel of the mirrored RR beam at +|w|; for the EVLA squint (R and L beams offset in opposite directions) the mirrored RR beam is the LL beam, which is why the partner cell stands in for the conjugate. The visibility being convolved is still the outer hand's. The index muellerElement % nDataPol returns the column of the selected cell's own element instead of the column of its position in the conjugate Mueller matrix.

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: On refim_mawproject (CASA 6.7.6.14, Stokes I, wbawp=True, conjbeams=True) the two pairings differ by 3.06e-3 normalised RMS in the dirty image. casa-rs compiles CASA's pairing (casa-imaging-operator, aw::routing into MuellerRouting) and agrees with CASA to 2e-7.

docs.title: AW-projection predicts with the unrotated w
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: CASA inconsistency between gridding and prediction; casa-rs follows it for parity (#667, PR #668)
  • Affected code: AWVisResampler.cc (GridToData reads vbs.vb_p->uvw()(2, irow); DataToGridImpl_p reads the rotated vbs.uvw_p)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: AWProjectFT hands the resampler the uvw rotated to the image phase centre and the phase shift (vbs.uvw_p, dphase_p) together with the VisBuffer (vbs.vb_p). GridToData selects its w-plane and tap conjugation from the VisBuffer's unrotated w while placing the sample at the rotated u, v with the rotated phasor; DataToGridImpl_p uses the rotated w for both. The two differ only where the rotation moves a w across a plane boundary or through zero. casa-rs carries the unrotated uvw per row (RowContext::original_uvw_m, ConvolutionFunctionSet::prediction_w) and keys the AW prediction on it.

docs.title: importvla stale VLACDA cache crash on old VLA export data
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-04-15
  • Status: likely CASA importvla bug
  • Affected code:
  • casatools/src/code/nrao/VLA/VLACDA.cc
  • casatools/src/code/nrao/VLA/VLABaselineRecord.cc
  • NRAO Archive file: AG189_1_46325.23029_46325.80807.exp (archive revision 11)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: importvla can abort on old VLA export data when a CDA is valid in one logical record and absent in the next. The immediate failure is the offset != 0 assertion in VLABaselineRecord::attach().

docs.title: Likely mechanism
docs.text: VLALogicalRecord::read() reattaches all four CDAs on every logical record. VLACDA caches baseline-record objects, so if a CDA was populated on one record and then becomes absent on the next, VLACDA::attach() can try to reattach cached baseline objects using offset 0, which triggers the assertion in VLABaselineRecord.

docs.title: Proposed fix
docs.text: In VLACDA::attach(), if the new CDA is invalid (itsOffset == 0, or equivalently no baseline data are present), clear the cached baseline objects and return before any reattach path runs.

docs.title: mstransform channel-mode transformed-grid inconsistency
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-04-10
  • Status: likely CASA mstransform bug or long-standing implementation quirk
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/mstransform/MSTransform/MSTransformRegridder.cc

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
In the transformed mode="channel" / regridQuant == "freq" path, CASA appears to anchor the output-grid start edge using transCHAN_WIDTH[firstChan], while it spaces the uniform output grid using transCHAN_WIDTH[0].

That is inconsistent once the frame transformation causes per-channel widths to vary slightly across the SPW. In the EVLA refim_Cband.G37line.ms repro case used during parity work, this produced an output-axis offset of about 0.046 Hz.

docs.title: Why this looks like a CASA bug, not a casacore bug
docs.text: Direct Rust-vs-casacore measures conversion for the relevant TOPO -> LSRK path matched to about 0.0015 Hz, so the underlying frame conversion itself does not appear to be the source of the discrepancy. The remaining offset is introduced later by CASA's transformed-grid construction policy in mstransform.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This is scientifically tiny in the observed repro, but it is semantically inconsistent.
  • The effect shows up in transformed channel-mode cubes where the transformed widths differ slightly across the SPW.

docs.title: Related references
docs.text:
• casacore PR #1464: Fix missing frame bias in IAU2000 JNAT<->APP conversions
  • casacore issue #1465: Unit mismatch in setMaximumCacheSize: bytes passed where MiB expected

Those casacore links are not the same bug, but they came out of the same cross-checking and parity work that surfaced this CASA-side issue.

docs.title: CASA Hogbom niter off-by-one bug
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-04-05
  • Status: likely CASA bug / legacy interface mismatch
  • Affected code:
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/ImagerObjects/SynthesisDeconvolver.cc
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/ImagerObjects/SDAlgorithmHogbomClean.cc
  • casatools/casacore/scimath_f/hclean.f

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
In the current CASA tclean(..., deconvolver='hogbom') path, niter=1 appears able to commit two clean components inside a single minor cycle while still reporting iterdone = 1.

Since provider contract 31 (owner approved 2026-10-31), casa-rs defaults its extra hogbom_iteration_mode option to casa-inclusive to reproduce this behavior. Explicit strict limits physical updates to the requested budget. Migrating an older profile warns when that option was omitted and adopts the inclusive default; explicit values are preserved. CASA's 92 parameter defaults are unchanged.

The effect is not limited to the top-level niter=1 case. Any CASA Hogbom minor-cycle call that enters hclean with a positive cycleNiter may commit one more component than the reported minor-cycle count. In a Cotton-Schwab run, that means the model, residual, restored image, and controller stop/refresh decisions can shift by up to one extra component per Hogbom minor-cycle block.

The first repro used:

  • dataset: .../casatestdata/measurementset/vla/sim_data_VLA_jet.ms
  • setup: imsize=512, cell='12arcsec', specmode='mfs', weighting='natural', gain=0.1, threshold='0Jy', niter=1
  • observed result: CASA reported iterdone = 1, but the output .model image contained two nonzero clean components

docs.title: Likely mechanism
docs.text:
An off-by-one caller/kernel mismatch:

  1. SDAlgorithmHogbomClean::takeOneStep seeds starting_iteration = 0
  2. the Fortran hclean kernel iterates over an inclusive do iter = siter, niter
  3. the returned count is then clamped back down to niter

With siter = 0 and niter = 1, that inclusive loop permits two update opportunities, which matches the observed behavior.

docs.title: Repro detail
docs.text:
The output .model image contained two nonzero pixels:

  1. (264, 331) = 0.6685306429862976
  2. (265, 331) = 0.6019284129142761

Their sum matched the reported modelFlux, which makes this look like an actual extra component update rather than a display or reporting artifact.

A second trace on the ALMA TW Hydra tutorial data used tclean(..., deconvolver='hogbom', niter=1, cycleniter=1, weighting='briggs', robust=0.5, imsize=250, cell='0.1arcsec'). CASA reported one minor iteration, but the model flux was 0.0569704 Jy; the dirty-image peak was 0.299844 Jy/beam, so one strict-gain component at gain=0.1 would account for only about 0.0299844 Jy. The reported model flux is therefore consistent with two committed Hogbom components in that minor-cycle call.

docs.title: Benchmark repro
docs.text:
The same behavior appeared on a medium standard-MFS VLA benchmark dataset:

  • setup: specmode='mfs', gridder='standard', deconvolver='hogbom', imsize=1024, cell='0.25arcsec', spw='0:0~63', Briggs robust=0.5, gain=0.1, threshold='0Jy', niter=1, cycleniter=1
  • observed result: CASA reported iterdone = 1, but the output .model image contained two nonzero clean components:
  • (510, 510) = 9.177456855773926
  • (508, 507) = 8.556220054626465

In a strict one-component casa-rs comparison this made the one-cycle residual RMS difference jump to 3.65e-2. Running casa-rs with its CASA-compatible Hogbom accounting (HogbomIterationAccounting::CasaInclusive) reproduced both components and reduced the residual RMS difference to 7.64e-5, matching the dirty gridding numerical floor. On the full niter=500, cycleniter=50 heavy row, the same CASA-compatible mode reduced the CASA/casa-rs product differences to .model RMS 1.71e-7, .residual RMS 5.68e-5, and .image RMS 5.87e-5.

docs.title: MatrixCleaner counts the iteration that stops it
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: CASA accounting quirk; casa-rs follows it for parity (IF-5, #654)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/MatrixCleaner.cc (MatrixCleaner::clean), read by SDAlgorithmMSClean::takeOneStep

clean increments itsIteration at the top of each pass and only then tests the threshold (abs(strength) < threshold()) and the 50% divergence rule, so a step that stops on either reports one more iteration (numberIterations()) than it cleaned components. Multiscale iterdone, the niter budget and the per-cycle summaryminor counts include it; on refim_point with scales [0, 6, 10] CASA reports [22, 3, 25, 3, 47] for [21, 2, 24, 2, 51] components when the extra iteration is not charged. casa-rs charges it (Solver::charges_stop).

docs.title: Multiscale and multi-term scale convolutions shift by a pixel on odd image sizes
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (IF-5, #654)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/MatrixCleaner.cc (makeScale, makePsfScales, makeDirtyScales), MultiTermMatrixCleaner.cc (computeRHS, computeHessianPeak)

Scale functions are centred at (nx/2, ny/2) and convolved by FFT without moving that centre to the origin. Single convolutions are re-centred with FFTServer::flip, which rotates by ceil(n/2); double convolutions (PSF ⊛ scale ⊛ scale) are not flipped, relying on the two n/2 shifts cancelling. Both are exact only for even n: on an odd axis the scale- convolved residual is one pixel off its residual and the PSF cross terms one pixel off the PSF peak. casa-rs convolves with the scale centred at the origin, which agrees with CASA on every even axis.

docs.title: MatrixCleaner's step residual forgets earlier steps
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (IF-5, #654)
  • Affected code: synthesis/ImagerObjects/SDAlgorithmMSClean.cc (takeOneStep), SDAlgorithmBase.cc (deconvolve)

With cycleniter ≥ 5000 a plane's minor cycle runs in 2000-iteration takeOneStep calls. Each call sets the residual to itsDirty − PSF ⊛ (model − prevModel), where itsDirty is the residual at the plane's first step and model − prevModel only this step's components, so from the second step on the reported peak residual omits the earlier steps' subtraction. That peak drives the minor-cycle stop codes 2 and 4. casa-rs carries each step's residual into the next.

docs.title: Peak searches let rounding choose between equal pixels
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-09
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows (exact comparisons); it makes parity rows on exactly symmetric skies rounding-dependent (IF-5, #654)
  • Affected code: casacore/scimath_f/hclean.f, casacore minMax as read by MatrixCleaner::findMaxAbsMask and MultiTermMatrixCleaner (chooseComponent), Clark's ABSMAXF

Every CASA peak search compares exactly and keeps the first extreme in its scan order; casa-rs does the same. On a point-symmetric sky such as refim_point, mirror pixels are equal in exact arithmetic (CASA's dirty and PSF images are exactly point-symmetric even in float32), and the scale convolutions and subtractions of the minor cycle break the tie by an ulp or two, so rounding, not the data, picks the component. On refim_point CASA's rounding went both ways: MatrixCleaner took the first mirror in scan order, and the multi-term cleaner the later one (one tie, at [50,47] / [50,53], value 4.9e-5, in the last cycle). casa-rs's FFTW plans are chosen by timing, so its refim_point multiscale row comes out at 5.4e-6 or 4.5e-2 NRMS from run to run; its MT-MFS row is 3.4e-4 when the tie goes CASA's way and 3.1e-2 when it does not (as on main). Both outcomes are equally valid cleans; such rows cannot measure parity, so IF-5's multiscale and MT-MFS acceptance uses skies without the symmetry (refim_twopoints_twochan, refim_eptwochan).

docs.title: The multi-term weight normalization override is never called
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-11
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs follows it for parity (#704, PR #707)
  • Affected code: synthesis/ImagerObjects/SIImageStore.h, SIImageStoreMultiTerm.h, SynthesisNormalizer.cc (divideWeightBySumWt)

SIImageStore declares virtual void divideWeightBySumwt() (lower-case wt). SIImageStoreMultiTerm declares void divideWeightBySumWt() (upper case W), a different name, so it overrides nothing; its loop that divides every Taylor weight image by the principal sum of weights is never called. SynthesisNormalizer::divideWeightBySumWt calls itsImages->divideWeightBySumwt(), which reaches the base body and divides weight(), term 0, alone. MultiTermFTNew::finalizeToSkyNew writes each term's raw getWeightImage moment, so .weight.tt1 and .weight.tt2 stay the raw Σ W·s^N while .weight.tt0 is normalized. CASA 6.7.6.14 on refim_alma_mosaic (mosaic, nterms=2) agrees: weight.ttN / sumwt.ttN is 0.6913 for N = 0, 1 and 2. casa-rs publishes the same.

docs.title: The analytic PB ignores a failed toPixel
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-11
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#702, PR #707)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines/PBMath1D.cc (apply)

PBMath1D::apply converts the pointing to a pixel with the image's direction coordinate (toPixel) and ignores the call's result, so a pointing the projection cannot place, such as one 90° or more from the image centre under SIN, is centred on whatever pixel the failed call left. casa-rs adds no beam for a pointing 90° or more from an image domain's centre and refuses any other projection failure.

docs.title: The cube Briggs weightor grids and looks up its density in different uvw frames
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-15
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#712 review by Fable and Astra)
  • Affected code (CASA 6.7.5.18 and 6.7.6.14):
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines2/BriggsCubeWeightor.cc (weightUniform, getWeightUniform)
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines2/GridFT.cc (put)

BriggsCubeWeightor, which weighs cubes under uniform and Briggs weighting (perchanweightdensity), fills its density grid through GridFT::put, which rotates each row's uvw to the image phase centre (rotateUVW, GridFT.cc:778). It then looks each row up, and tapers it, at vb.uvw(), the unrotated MeasurementSet uvw (BriggsCubeWeightor.cc:826, 860-861). The grid and the lookup use different frames. When the phase centre is the field centre the rotation is the identity and nothing changes; for a cube with a phase centre away from the field centre, or a multi-field cube, a row reads the density of a different cell from the one its own sample was counted in, so its weight no longer follows the local density. The MFS weightor (VisImagingWeight) accumulates and looks up in one frame, the MeasurementSet uvw.

casa-rs bins and looks up the cube rule at the rotated uvw, one frame for both (the_cube_density_bins_and_looks_up_the_rotated_uvw), and the standard (MFS) rule at the MeasurementSet uvw, as VisImagingWeight does (the_standard_density_bins_the_measurement_set_uvw). Cubes imaged at their own field centre agree with CASA either way; off-centre and multi-field cubes under a density weighting differ from CASA's weights by this mechanism.

Measured on a mosaic (2026-11-03, #818, CASA 6.7.6.14, CPU f64). On a mosaic a row's uvw is MosaicFT's reprojection (girarUVW, in which w does not reach u and v), so casa-rs bins and looks up a mosaic cube's density there, while CASA bins at GridFT's rotation and looks up at the MeasurementSet uvw. On refim_alma_mosaic.ms (three fields 7.5″ apart, three channels, 350×280 at 0.06″, mosweight=True, where each field's density is its own, BriggsCubeWeightor's multiField):

  • one field imaged at its own centre agrees with CASA on every product, the PSF to 1e-7 and .sumwt exactly, under uniform and Briggs weighting;
  • the same field imaged at its neighbour's centre differs, uniform weighting PSF NRMS 2.6e-2 and .sumwt 4.1e-4: 4,135 of its 130,032 (row, channel) weights differ from CASA's IMAGING_WEIGHT;
  • an evidence-only build that grids the density at GridFT's rotation of the MeasurementSet uvw and looks it up at the MeasurementSet uvw, as CASA does, matches all 130,032 of CASA's weights to 4.2e-10;
  • the three fields together, at the test's centre (the middle field's): PSF NRMS 9.3e-3 under uniform weighting, 5.6e-4 under Briggs 0.5 (2.6e-2 is sparser: each field's density holds a third of the samples); with one density over all fields (mosweight=False), Briggs PSF 3.9e-4.

So this ALMA mosaic cube's differences under a density weighting, with or without mosweight, are this entry's mechanism (#789 records the seven-pointing case). An EVLA mosaic cube (refim_oneshiftpoint.mosaic.ms, three one-channel windows) differs from CASA under uniform weighting even for one field at its own centre, with or without mosweight (PSF NRMS 3.6e-3, ten .pb mask pixels), where the standard gridder agrees to 1e-7; this mechanism does not explain it, and it stays open in #789.

docs.title: Continuum briggsabs at robust 0 and noise 0 weighs every visibility infinite
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#980)
  • Affected code (CASA 6.7.6.14):
  • casatools/src/code/synthesis/ImagerObjects/SynthesisImagerVi2.cc (weight)
  • casatools/src/code/msvis/MSVis/VisImagingWeight.cc (the VisibilityIterator2 constructor and weightUniform)

Absolute Briggs weighting (weighting='briggsabs', rmode = "abs") divides each weight by D·f² + d² with f² = robust² and d² = 2·noise². With robust = 0 and noise = 0 both vanish. For a cube with perchanweightdensity, SynthesisImagerVi2::weight refuses the pair ("Absolute Briggs formula does not allow for robust 0 and estimated noise per visibility 0") before it builds the BriggsCubeWeightor; every other density (a continuum image, or a cube without perchanweightdensity) goes to VisImagingWeight, which has no such check, so weightUniform divides every weight by zero and the imaging weights are infinite.

casa-rs refuses the pair in every mode, at the tclean reader (noise), the compiled weighting contract and the operator (WeightingGeneration::absolute_density).

docs.title: MultiTermFTNew forms Taylor imaging weights in single precision
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-11; metric approved 2026-10-15
  • Status: CASA rounding; casa-rs does not follow it (#690)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines2/MultiTermFTNew.cc (modifyVisWeights, modifyModelVis)

modifyVisWeights holds each channel frequency and the Taylor variable (ν − ν₀) / ν₀ in Float, and multiplies the Float imaging weights by its powers. The odd moments of .sumwt are sums that nearly cancel (two channels at x ≈ ±1/3 leave Σw·x ≈ −0.05 of Σ|w·x| ≈ 8·10⁴), so this rounding shows as a 1 % relative difference in .sumwt.tt1 on refim_twopoints_twochan. An emulation of both codes' arithmetic reproduces both published values to every stored digit; casa-rs, which rounds the Taylor variable to f32 once and accumulates in f64, is 0.06 % from the exact sum, CASA 0.93 %. No image reads the odd moments' sums.

casa-rs keeps its arithmetic. The T1.5 comparison judges an odd moment k by |Δ| / √(tt_{k−1} · tt_{k+1}) and every other .sumwt by its relative difference, both against 1e-6, and leaves .sumwt out of a case's image NRMS. The narrow-band mosaic MT-MFS rows (three channels at 340 GHz) still miss that bound at about 5e-6 and are listed exceptions until an emulation confirms the same mechanism there and in the odd-moment weight images.

docs.title: Facets of an image size that does not divide
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-15
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#664)
  • Affected code: synthesis/ImagerObjects/SIImageStore.cc (makeSubImage)

A facet of an n-pixel image split N ways is n / N pixels (integer division) from facet · (n / N), so when N does not divide n the top and right remainder strips belong to no facet: CASA grids and cleans nothing there, silently. casa-rs refuses such a layout (NonDivisibleFacetLayout).

docs.title: An unflagged non-finite sample turns the image to NaN
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (a NaN image loses the product, so casa-rs corrects it)
  • Affected code: CASA's gridding path, which accumulates unflagged samples without testing them for finiteness

CASA grids a NaN or infinite visibility, weight or UVW in an unflagged sample like any other, and the transform spreads it, so the products come out NaN everywhere without naming the sample. casa-rs fails the run instead (FiniteValuePolicy::RejectUnflaggedInput, and PrepareError::NonFiniteUvw for UVW found while compiling), naming the row, channel and correlation so the sample can be flagged. Flagged samples and grid padding are skipped, as in CASA. The CASA behaviour is as ARCHITECTURE.md has recorded it since the review of #792; it has not been rerun against CASA for this entry.

docs.title: tclean images DATA when CORRECTED_DATA is missing, and says nothing
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows, with a warning (simulation plan §3, decision 6)
  • Affected code: synthesis/ImagerObjects/SIMapperCollection.cc (grid), synthesis/TransformMachines2/FTMachine.cc (makeImage), synthesis/ImagerObjects/SynthesisImagerVi2.cc (selectData)

datacolumn='corrected' sets FTMachine::CORRECTED in selectData without looking at the MeasurementSet. When a VisBuffer has no corrected visibilities, SIMapperCollection::grid and FTMachine::makeImage switch to OBSERVED, so tclean images DATA (less the model in a major cycle). SynthesisImager::selectData once logged "CORRECTED_DATA column does not exist. Using DATA column instead"; that block is commented out, and CASA 6.7.6's libcasacpp_synthesis does not contain the message, so CASA logs no message for the fallback.

casa-rs's simulator writes DATA only, so its imager follows the fallback and logs CASA's old message as a warning, since the column imaged is not the one asked for.

VisibilityIterator2's existsColumn also counts CORRECTED_DATA as missing in an iteration chunk whose first row's cell is undefined (isDefined(0) on the chunk's attached table), so CASA can image DATA chunk by chunk from a partly written column. casa-rs decides by the column's presence alone and images an existing CORRECTED_DATA as before. That is a deliberate scope limit, not full parity: casa-tables' metadata-only probe (array_cell_is_defined_uncached) answers only for lazy, disk-backed TiledShapeStMan columns, and one probe would not reproduce the per-chunk rule.

docs.title: The Airy beam's blockage term uses the inverse length ratio
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs follows it (#841, PR #843)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines/PBMath1DAiry.cc (fillPBArray)

For a dish of diameter D with a central blockage of diameter b, the voltage pattern is proportional to D²·jinc(x) − b²·jinc(x·b/D), where jinc(x) = 2J₁(x)/x and x = πDθ/λ. fillPBArray tabulates (areaRatio·jinc(x) − jinc(x·lengthRatio)) / (areaRatio − 1) with lengthRatio = D/b, so it evaluates the blockage term at x·D/b instead of x·b/D.

For ALMA's default pattern (10.7 m, 0.75 m blockage), the power in the main lobe comes out about 1% above the physical pattern: 0.507 against 0.500 at the physical half-power radius, and 0.901 against 0.892 at 42% of that radius. Every Airy pattern CASA builds this way is affected: the simulator's setvp, imaging's primary beams and the mosaic gridder's HetArrayConvFunc dishes.

ALMA's 10.7 m effective diameter was chosen against CASA's beam, so casa-rs tabulates the same expression (casa_numerics::AnnularApertureVoltageTable) and its predictions match CASA's to 1.6e-7. The simulator's beam test checks CASA's formula rather than the physical one.

docs.title: The simulator stores TAI as UTC
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-20
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841, plan decision 5)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (observe, lines 1262-1280)

observe converts the reference epoch to TAI and adds its seconds to the start and stop offsets, then writes the result into TIME, whose MEASINFO says UTC. The data therefore start TAI − UTC at the reference epoch after the requested epoch (37 s since 2017, 35 s in 2014). The geometry is computed with the stored number read as UT1 (line 1546), so CASA's data are self-consistent; only the schedule is shifted.

casa-rs stores the requested UTC, and also reads the stored TIME as UT1 for the geometry, so its uvw agree with CASA's at equal stored TIME. A parity run requests a start later by TAI − UTC at the reference epoch on the casa-rs side, taken from the measures data and never written in as a number, and compares rows at equal TIME (tools/simulation/compare_sm_ms.py).

The same offset separates the calibration tables the two simulators write (setgain and setleakage with table=): CASA's TIME is TAI under the UTC label. sm.setapply of a CASA-simulated table to a casa-rs MeasurementSet, or the reverse, therefore takes its solutions TAI − UTC away (37 s today), several solutions of 10 s integrations. The corrupt-setapply-* scenarios agree with CASA because their runs are shifted as above; tables solved from real data carry true UTC and are not affected.

docs.title: The simulator charges shadowing to the antenna in front
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (blockage, lines 1780-1815)

A row's uvw is R·(X₁ − X₂), so w > 0 puts antenna 1 nearer the source. blockage zeroes antenna 2's blocked fraction when w > 0 and antenna 1's when w < 0, which leaves the blockage on the antenna in front, the one that does the blocking. CASA's own flagger (FlagAgentShadow, since casapy 4.1) flags the antenna behind. casa-rs's simulator flags the antenna behind (casa_ms::shadowing::ShadowedAntenna::Behind); the CASA convention remains available as CasaSimulatorFront.

docs.title: setspwindow relabels every spectral window's frame
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (initSpWindows, line 750)

Each setspwindow call ends with measFreqRef().fillColumn(freqType), which writes the new window's frame into MEAS_FREQ_REF for every row of SPECTRAL_WINDOW. A TOPO window followed by an LSRK one ends with both labelled LSRK, although their frequencies were given in different frames. casa-rs writes each window's own frame.

docs.title: setconfig accepts coordinate systems it cannot convert
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (initAnt, lines 452-456; longlat2global, lines 566-575)

For coordsystem='longlat', longlat2global logs SEVERE "not yet implemented"; for an unknown name, initAnt logs SEVERE "Unknown coordinate system type". In both cases the antennas are added at the Earth's centre and setconfig returns True, so the script continues with an array whose geometry is meaningless. In casa-rs, longlat raises RuntimeError and an unknown name logs CASA's message and returns False; neither adds antennas.

docs.title: The tools convert quantities whose units do not conform
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools' argument conversion (casaQuantity, casaMDirection) used by simulator_cmpt.cc and the other tools

A tool argument such as integrationtime or freq is read as a quantity and converted to the unit the method needs without checking that the units conform. CASA 6.7.6 takes integrationtime='10Jy' as 1e-25 s, integrationtime='10m' (metres, perhaps meant as minutes) as 10 s and freq='1s' as 1 Hz. A direction string whose second or third token does not read keeps the previous value, so 'J2000 12h00m00 garbage' has a declination of 180°. casa-rs refuses both with casacore's "From/to units not consistent" or a parse error. The conversions CASA defines between dimensions are kept: a dimensionless number is the SI unit, an angle is a time at 360° a day, and a length is a frequency through c.

docs.title: Simulator calls before setconfig abort the process
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (initFeeds, observe)

setfeed or observe before any setconfig builds a table slice over zero antennas. casacore's array code throws std::runtime_error (an empty Slicer), which the tool binding does not catch, and the Python process aborts. casa-rs raises RuntimeError from setfeed, and observe returns False with "Antenna information not yet defined".

docs.title: A zero integration time adds rows without bound
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: simulator_cmpt.cc (settimes, line 221); ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (observe)

settimes asserts only that the integration time is not negative, and settimes() with no arguments sets 0 s. observe then divides the scan's span by zero to count integrations; over a nonzero span this adds billions of rows before the disk fills. casa-rs's observe returns False for an integration time that is not positive ("observe: the integration time must be positive").

docs.title: simutil.readantenna averages a stale loop variable
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py (readantenna, lines 1783-1791)

When a configuration file gives absolute coordinates, names no known observatory and has no COFA header, readantenna means to place the observatory at the mean antenna position. It averages x, y and z, which are the loop variables of the UTM branch, rather than the antenna lists stnx, stny and stnz. For an XYZ file the names are unbound and the call raises UnboundLocalError; for a UTM file the observatory becomes the last antenna. It then assigns xyz2long's (longitude, latitude, height) to (latitude, longitude, height), so the two angles are swapped. casa-rs converts the mean antenna position, as the comment intends (casa_simulation::readantenna, which lists its smaller divergences).

docs.title: simutil.readantenna names antennas after blank lines
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py (readantenna)

readantenna skips a line with fewer than four values, but still appends a default A%02d pad and antenna name for it, so the names run ahead of the positions by one for every such line. CASA's own WSRT.cfg has two blank lines, so readantenna returns 16 names for 14 antennas, starting A00, A01, RT0, and a CASA simulation of WSRT names every dish wrongly. casa-rs skips such lines entirely.

docs.title: The measures tool converts with a frame at MJD 0 and the geocentre
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA behaviour; casa-rs does not follow it (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/measures/measures_cmpt.cc (the measures constructor)

The measures tool starts with a frame of a default epoch (MJD 0 UTC), a default position (the zero vector) and a default direction (the J2000 pole). A conversion that needs a frame element me.doframe has not set uses these without a warning, so me.measure(me.direction('J2000', '12h00m00', '45d00m00'), 'AZEL') in a fresh tool returns an azimuth and elevation for 1858-11-17 at the centre of the Earth (casacore only notes, at INFO, that MJD 0 is outside its Earth-orientation table). After me.done() the frame is empty and the same call fails with "Cannot convert due to missing frame information". casa-rs's tool starts with the empty frame, so such a conversion always fails with that message until doframe sets the element.

docs.title: sm.predict rewrites the model image
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (createSkyEquation, lines 2319-2344)

createSkyEquation opens each model as a PagedImage<Float>, gives its coordinate system an LSRK spectral conversion and Hz world units ("FTMachine only works in Hz and LSRK") and stores it back with setCoordinateInfo, so predicting rewrites the model's table.dat. Later reads of the model, including another predict, see coordinates the user did not write; the CASA oracle (tools/simulation/casa_sm_observe_oracle.py --model-root) copies the model for every call because of it. casa-rs converts the spectral axis to Hz in memory and never writes the model.

docs.title: sm.predict accepts models the simulator cannot read
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-21
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/simulator/simulator_cmpt.cc (predict, lines 620-629); synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (createSkyEquation, lines 2313-2319 and 2568-2572; predict, lines 2161-2163)

casatools' binding checks each model with ImageFactory::fromFile, which also opens FITS images and complex-valued CASA images. The simulator then reads each model as a PagedImage<Float>. A FITS file is not a table, so it logs "… is unreadable" and then "No model images found"; a complex image throws when opened as Float, which createSkyEquation catches ("Caught exception: …"). Either way sm.predict logs "Failed to create SkyEquation" and returns False, and the script continues with DATA not predicted. These outcomes are read from the source and were not probed. casa-rs's check opens each model as the simulator reads it, so a FITS or complex model raises RuntimeError "Unable to open image …" at the call.

docs.title: IAU 2000 keeps the IAU 1980 sidereal time and ecliptic obliquities
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-22
  • Status: casacore behaviour; casa-rs follows it for parity (#850)
  • Affected code: measures/Measures/MCEpoch.cc (initConvert, UT1_GAST), measures/Measures/MeasMath.cc (applyMECLIPtoJMEAN, applyTECLIPtoJTRUE), measures/Measures/MeasTable.cc (fundArg)

With measures.iau2000.b_use set, casacore still forms GAST from the IAU 1982 GMST and the IAU 1980 equation of the equinoxes of Nutation::STANDARD, without the 1994 complementary terms, and every HADEC, AZEL and ITRF conversion takes its LAST from that GAST. TECLIPTIC rotates by the IAU 1980 true obliquity and MECLIPTIC by MeasTable::fundArg(0), under either model. That polynomial's T² term is −0.0059″, where IAU 1976 has −0.00059″: 0.37 mas in MECLIPTIC by 2026. casa-rs computes all of these as casacore does (casacore_sidereal, casacore_frames), which moved its IAU 2000A J2000→HADEC from 20.4 to 16.7 mas off casacore, the residual of the APP step alone.

docs.title: Direction latitudes come from an unnormalized vector
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-22
  • Status: casacore numerical defect; casa-rs does not follow it (#850)
  • Affected code: measures/Measures/MeasData.cc (GALtoJ2000, GALtoB1950, MToB1950, MToJ2000), measures/Measures/MCDirection.cc (doConvert), casa/Quanta/MVDirection.cc (getLat, get)

casacore's galactic and FK4 matrices are 10-digit literals, orthogonal only to about 7e-11 (1.5e-8 for MToB1950(4)), and MCDirection::doConvert does not renormalize after applying them. MVDirection::getLat() and get() then take asin(z), assuming a unit vector, so the latitude casacore reports is off by about (|v| − 1)·tan(b) and becomes NaN once z exceeds 1. casa-rs converts with the same matrices, renormalizes, and reports the latitude of the unit vector. The two directions agree to 0.01 µas; the reported angles differ by up to 51 µas for B1950→GALACTIC on the law's grid and by 1.6 mas for J2000→B1950 at b = −89.77°, where tan(b) is 250 (measures_frames_interop).

docs.title: IAU 2000 JMEAN to J2000 applies bias and precession in the wrong order
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-22
  • Status: casacore bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#850)
  • Affected code: measures/Measures/MeasMath.cc (deapplyPrecession)

Under IAU 2000, applyPrecession takes J2000 to JMEAN as in *= B; in *= P, v′ = Pᵀ·Bᵀ·v, with B the frame bias and P the precession. The inverse, deapplyPrecession, applies in = B·in and then in = P·in, which is P·B·v′, not B·P·v′. The two do not commute, so casacore's JMEAN→J2000 is not the inverse of its J2000→JMEAN: MECLIPTIC→J2000 and TECLIPTIC→J2000 are 0.14 mas off in 2026, and the error grows with time from J2000. casa-rs inverts exactly; the frame law compares the IAU 2000 ecliptics from the equator of date.

docs.title: IAU 2000 GMST1 adds the TT day fraction
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-22
  • Status: casacore bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#850)
  • Affected code: measures/Measures/MCEpoch.cc (UT1_GMST1, GMST1_UT1), measures/Measures/MeasTable.cc (GMST00)

Under IAU 2000, UT1_GMST1 turns the UT1 epoch into TT and adds GMST00/(2π) and 6713 days to it. GMST00 is already the sidereal time of day (the Earth rotation angle in [0, 2π) plus precession), so the TT day fraction is counted twice: UT1 51544.5 gives GMST1 58258.280, against the IAU 1976 path's 58257.779 and a GAST of 58257.779, and LMST inherits the error. GMST1_UT1's iteration does not undo it: GMST1 58258.280 converts back to UT1 51544.999. casa-rs uses the IAU 1976 GMST1 under either model, as casacore's own GAST does, so its GMST1, LMST, GAST and LAST agree with each other and, under IAU 1976, with casacore.

docs.title: Writing a limb-darkened disk without an exponent aborts CASA
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/components/ComponentModels/ComponentList.cc (writeTable, lines 1016-1022; readTable, lines 1155-1161)

A component list holding a limb-darkened disk gets an Optional_Parameters column, and writeTable puts each such component's optional parameters in it; the first is the disk's limb-darkening exponent. A limb-darkened disk made through cl.fromrecord without optionalParameters has none, and writing it throws casacore::indexError from the ComponentList destructor, which terminates the process (probed with CASA 6.7.6: fromrecord and rename succeed, close aborts). Had the empty vector been stored, readTable would read its first element out of bounds. casa-rs leaves the cell undefined, which CASA reads as the shape's default exponent of 0.05, as it reads every other row the column does not describe.

docs.title: A negative component turns positive under the primary beam
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines/BeamSkyJones.cc (apply(SkyComponent&, …), lines 488-511)

With sm.setvp(dovp=True), SkyEquation::applySkyJones applies the beam to each component with fullspectral set. That path multiplies the beam-applied flux, which keeps the component's sign, by a per-channel factor of the spectrum's sample over abs(flux), which carries the sign again, so a negative flux comes out positive. Probed with CASA 6.7.6: a −0.4 Jy point 20 arcsec from the pointing centre predicts −0.4 Jy without the beam and +0.4 Jy times the beam with it. casa-rs keeps the sign; sm_components_scenarios.json keeps negative components away from the beam.

docs.title: A single spectral index is read past its end
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/components/ComponentModels/SpectralIndex.cc (sampleStokes, lines 138-146 and 213-237); components/ComponentModels/SkyCompRep.cc (visibility, line 314)

cl.addcomponent(spectrumtype="spectral index", index=α) stores one index. The per-frequency sampleStokes scales only I by it and leaves Q, U and V alone; the matrix sampleStokes, which SkyCompRep::visibility and so every component prediction uses, has no one-index branch and reads indices 1 to 3 out of bounds. For an unpolarised component the out-of-bounds factors multiply zeros. Read from the source and not probed: a polarised component with a single index predicts Q, U and V scaled by whatever follows the vector. casa-rs reads a single index as [α, 0, 0, 0], so the fractional polarisation is constant, as the matrix sampler's comments describe; sm_components_scenarios.json gives its polarised components no index.

docs.title: The primary beam's component spectrum labels topocentric samples LSRK
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines/BeamSkyJones.cc (apply(SkyComponent&, …), lines 494-529); components/ComponentModels/SkyCompRep.cc (visibility, lines 303-314)

The full-spectral beam path evaluates the beam and the spectrum at each channel's topocentric frequency, stores the products in a TabularSpectrum at the channels' LSRK frequencies, and labels it LSRK. SkyCompRep::visibility then looks the table up at the topocentric frequencies, which it takes to be in the component's frame, so each channel reads the table shifted by the observatory's velocity, up to about 1e-4 of the frequency. casa-rs evaluates the beam and the spectrum at each channel's own frequency. With the beam, sm_components_scenarios.json agrees with CASA to 7e-5 and 1e-4 normalized RMS, against 1.3e-5 or better without it: consistent in size with this shift, though the shift was not isolated.

docs.title: cl.addcomponent stores four flux values as Stokes
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs follows it (#841, owner decision 2026-10-23)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/componentlist/componentlist_cmpt.cc (setflux, lines 831-930); components/ComponentModels/Flux.tcc (FluxRep::setValue(const Vector<T>&), lines 363-368)

setflux, which addcomponent calls, sets the flux's representation from polarization and then stores four values with FluxRep::setValue(Vector<Double>), which resets the representation to Stokes. So cl.addcomponent(flux=[1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.9], polarization='circular') stores I = 1, Q = 0.1, U = 0.2, V = 0.9 rather than RR, RL, LR and LL (probed with CASA 6.7.6 for 'Circular', 'circular', 'CIRCULAR' and 'linear'). polarization still has effects: an unknown name raises, and one value with a representation other than Stokes raises. casa-rs does the same, so a script gets the list CASA would give it.

docs.title: cl.addcomponent stores the flux in single precision
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/componentlist/componentlist_cmpt.cc (setflux, lines 858-870)

setflux reads the values into a Vector<Complex> (single precision) before storing them as doubles, so flux=0.1 is stored as 0.10000000149011612 (probed with CASA 6.7.6). casa-rs keeps the values given; they differ from CASA's by at most one single-precision rounding, 6e-8 relative.

docs.title: The cl tool records a shape's axes in the units it was given
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: components/ComponentModels/TwoSidedShape.cc (toRecord, lines 265-330)

TwoSidedShape remembers the units its axes were set in, and its record gives them in those units: a Gaussian made by addcomponent with majoraxis='1arcsec' records {'unit': 'arcsec', 'value': 1.0}. A shape read from a table has the units readTable sets: arcmin for the axes and degrees for the position angle, with the errors in radians. casa-rs holds radians and records every shape as CASA records one read from a table ({'unit': 'arcmin', 'value': 0.016666666666666666}); the quantities are the same, and the table is the same either way.

docs.title: cl.addcomponent keeps a point for a shape it cannot make
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows (#841)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/componentlist/componentlist_cmpt.cc (addcomponent, lines 453-526; setshape, lines 1285-1386)

addcomponent adds a point and then calls setshape, ignoring what it returns. setshape logs SEVERE and returns False for a shape name it does not know, for a limb-darkened disk ("not implemented yet"), and for an axis that is not an angle (none given, a number, or another unit), so the component stays a point at the given direction and addcomponent returns True (probed with CASA 6.7.6). casa-rs does the same and logs the message at ERROR. Scripts that misspell a shape name therefore get points, as they do in CASA.

What setshape raises, addcomponent raises too, after removing the component it began: an axis that does not read as a quantity ('garbage', a complex number), and what the shape's constructor raises, such as a Gaussian's position angle outside ±2π (Gaussian2DParam::setPA) or axes that are not positive. A minor axis longer than the major raises as well: TwoSidedShape::fromRecord (TwoSidedShape.cc, lines 229-263) means to refuse it, but compares the minor axis with itself (near(minorAxisInRad, minorAxisInRad), line 249), so the check never fires and the constructor raises instead. casa-rs raises in each case with casacore's message, and adds nothing.

docs.title: setmosaicfield sits its grid off the field centre
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 2, plan §4 "Diverged and recorded")
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (setmosaicfield, lines 849-901)

setmosaicfield tests for an odd count with (nx/2)!=floor(nx/2) on integers. That is always false, so every grid takes the even-count offsets. Those offsets, (i − ceil(nx/2)) − 0.5 spacings in right ascension and (j − ceil(ny/2.0)) − 0.5 in declination, count i and j from zero where one was meant.

Measured with CASA 6.7.6 at 1′ spacing: - 3 × 3: right ascension offsets −1.5, −0.5 and +0.5 spacings; declination offsets −2.5, −1.5 and −0.5. - 2 × 2: −1.5 and −0.5 spacings on both axes.

A centred grid would be at −1, 0 and +1, and at ±0.5.

Over a pole, CASA also sets the right ascension to |π − α|, where crossing the pole adds π.

casa-rs centres every grid: offsets (i − (n − 1)/2) spacings, right ascension divided by the centre's cos δ. It crosses a pole as the sphere does. The fields keep CASA's names, {sourcename}_{k}, numbered down each column and then across.

docs.title: observemany pads one name with empty ones
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs follows its outcome (#841 Phase 2)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/tools/simulator/simulator_cmpt.cc (observemany, lines 318-326)

casatools means one source name, or one direction, to stand for every pointing. It grows the list with Vector<String>::resize(nptg, true), which keeps the existing elements and default-constructs the rest, so the new entries are empty strings, not copies. With one name and several pointings, pointing 1's field is "". NewMSSimulator::observe raises "Field 1: not yet defined", and sm.observemany logs it and returns False (measured with CASA 6.7.6). With one direction, the later pointings have none, and each keeps the previous pointing's phase centre while the field stays the same.

casars.tools.simulator pads the lists the same way, so it returns the same False, and moves only the first pointing. Unlike CASA, it adds no rows before refusing (next entry).

docs.title: observemany adds rows before it looks up later fields
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 2)
  • Affected code: ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (observe, the vector form)

observe adds every pointing's MAIN rows (ms_p->addRow(nNewRows)) before its pointing loop. It looks up the first pointing's field before that, but each later field only when the loop reaches it. A later field that is not defined raises with the rows already added: their FIELD_ID, TIME and UVW are unwritten, and the call returns False. casa-rs looks up every pointing's field before it plans anything, so the same call returns False with the same message and leaves no rows.

docs.title: sm.predict through WProjectFT without planes crashes the simulator
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 2)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (createSkyEquation, line 2465); synthesis/TransformMachines/WPConvFunc.cc (findConvFunction, lines 164-176)

The simulator builds its WProjectFT with no w statistics (minW, maxW and rmsW all −1). For setoptions(ftmachine='wproject', wprojplanes=…) below 1, findConvFunction takes its automatic branch, whose largest w then comes out negative and whose plane count comes out zero or negative. Measured on CASA 6.7.6: setoptions returns True, and predict with wprojplanes=0 or -1 kills the Python process with a segmentation fault (exit 139) after it logs "Fourier transforms will use specified common tangent point". casa-rs records the planes at setoptions, as CASA does, and its predict raises RuntimeError ("W projection needs at least two planes").

What casa-rs follows of the same machine: - wprojplanes=1 returns False from predict with CASA's "Convolution function integral is not positive". - WProjectFT pads by 1, its constructor's default, whatever setoptions(padding=…) says. - Autocorrelations predict zero, since the machine is built with usezero off. - Rows beyond the largest w the planes reach (0.25/|cell|) predict zero.

docs.title: SDGrid predicts total power into cross-correlations with no positive uvw
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SDGrid.cc (get, the rowFlags loop)

sm.predict after setoptions(ftmachine='sd') samples the model at each row's pointing. SDGrid::get leaves out a row whose uvw has a positive component (max(uvw) > 0), which is meant to keep the cross-correlations of a single-dish predict at zero. A cross-correlation whose u, v and w are all zero or negative passes that test and is given the pointing's total power as if it were one dish's autocorrelation. Read from the source; a probe with two antennas saw only rows with a positive component. casa-rs predicts total power into autocorrelations only.

docs.title: The EVLA's beam table has no 11052 MHz fit
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: likely CASA bug; casa-rs follows it for parity (#841 Phase 2)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines/PBMath1DEVLA.cc (init, line 320)

PBMath1DEVLA::init fills its map of polynomial beam fits by frequency, in MHz, one 128 MHz step at a time. In X band the sequence runs 10948, then 10052, then 11180: the second 10052 was meant for 11052. Through std::map::operator[] it replaces the first 10052 fit, so the map has no 11052 entry. The 10052 MHz frequencies use the fit meant for 11052, and those near 11052 MHz take a neighbour's. The coefficients differ by about 1% in the linear term, which moves the beam by a few 1e-3 at its half power. casa-rs's table (casa_numerics::EvlaPowerPattern, shared by the simulator and imaging) is CASA's map as built.

docs.title: sm.close() aborts the process after a mosaic predict
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 2)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (close, after createSkyEquation built MosaicFTNew with HetArrayConvFunc)

After setoptions(ftmachine='mosaic') and a predict that returns True, CASA 6.7.6's sm.close() kills the Python process: libc++abi prints "Pure virtual function called!" and raises SIGABRT (exit 134 from a shell). simobserve's own sequence (setvp, setoptions(ftmachine='mosaic'), predict, close) aborts the same way. It was not traced to the destructor that makes the call. DATA is complete on disk when it happens: a rerun whose abort was turned into a quiet exit wrote the same DATA, UVW, FLAG and TIME bit for bit, and those MeasurementSets agree with casa-rs's to a few 1e-7 normalized RMS. casa-rs's close returns normally. The CASA oracle (tools/simulation/casa_sm_observe_oracle.py) runs such scenarios (close_aborts) in a child process, accepts the abort only when every predict returned True, and records close as aborted.

docs.title: The simulator's mosaic machine is not tclean's
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows for parity, per machine (#841 Phase 2, #875)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines/HetArrayConvFunc.cc, SimplePBConvFunc.cc and MosaicFT.cc (the simulator's, through MosaicFTNew) against their synthesis/TransformMachines2/ namesakes (tclean's)

sm.predict after setoptions(ftmachine='mosaic') degrids through the earlier heterogeneous-array machine, and tclean(gridder='mosaic') through the later one. They differ in: - the dish's support radius: 150″ at 100 GHz for every ALMA and ACA dish in the simulator; in tclean, max(150″, fov/5) for a 12 m dish and max(300″, fov/3) for any other; - the screen's least size: none in the simulator, a tenth of the image in tclean; - the frequency cells (findUsefulChannels): from the selected channels alone in the simulator, lround(span / 0.5 % of the top) cells matched in Float; stepping down from the window's top frequency in tclean; - the support search: in the simulator, inwards from the lattice's edge along the row and the column one cell off its centre, the radius found widened by √2; in tclean, outwards from the weight plane's peak; - the channel frequencies: the window's own in the simulator; tclean converts them to the image's frame (LSRK).

Both grid every row of a window with the widest pair's support (MosaicFT hands sectgmosd2 and the degridders max(convSupportPlanes_p)), each pair normalised over its own; casa-rs took tclean's rows each with its own support until #980, which put mixed 12 m and 7 m tclean mosaics 2.5e-3 normalized RMS from CASA, and 1.8e-2 for the 7 m antennas of a mixed array, where they agree to 6e-7.

On the #875 probe (six 12 m and six 7 m ALMA antennas over three fields at 230 GHz) CASA logs supports [6, 6, 6] for the simulator and [7, 6, 6] for tclean, and the two machines' predictions of one model differ by 4.5–5.6e-3 normalized RMS per dish-pair class on a TOPO MeasurementSet and 1.9–2.4e-3 on an LSRK one. casa-rs's mosaic set takes either machine's rules (casa_imaging_operator::MosaicRules): imaging follows tclean's, the simulator its own.

Both machines reproject rows through FTMachine::girarUVW, whose new u and v take no share of w, where GridFT's rotateUVW applies the full rotation. At offsets of 10–17″ the two differ by a few 1e-4 cells, which flips the fine offset of a sample near a rounding boundary; with the mosaic's ten offsets a cell, such a sample moved by up to 10% (#841: 33 of 4,752 rows, until the simulator took girarUVW too).

docs.title: tclean's mosaic beams for a MeasurementSet know only the dishes met before it
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: casa-rs diverges (#980); one beam set over every MeasurementSet's dishes for every pass
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines2/HetArrayConvFunc.cc (findAntennaSizes, findConvFunction)

With a list of MeasurementSets, findAntennaSizes adds each MeasurementSet's dish diameters to those of the ones the visibility iterator met before it, and findConvFunction rebuilds the beams of a MeasurementSet's window whenever the iterator moves to another MeasurementSet (msId_p != vb.msId()). In the first pass (the PSF and the weight image) the first MeasurementSet's beams therefore know only its own dishes, and in every later pass every MeasurementSet's: the screen size (the widest dish's support radius) and the gridding support (the widest pair's) of its rows change between passes, so the result depends on the order CASA visits the list in. casa-rs builds one set from every MeasurementSet's dishes and grids every pass with it.

On CASA's own ALMA 12 m and ACA 7 m lists (test_het_mosaic_mfs_alma_listofms CAS-14255 and CAS-14350, 12 m data first, whose pair has the widest support) only the first pass's screen size differs: every product agrees to 1.3e-5 normalized RMS. With the 7 m data made earlier, so that CASA meets it first, the first pass grids the 7 m rows with the 7 m support alone, and the products differ by up to 5.4e-4; each MeasurementSet imaged alone agrees to 7e-7.

docs.title: A mosaic's weight image is transformed in single precision
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-03
  • Status: casa-rs diverges (#980); its weight image is transformed in double precision, so a .pb pixel within single-precision rounding of pblimit can fall on the other side of CASA's mask
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines2/MosaicFT.cc (finalizeToSky: convertArray(griddedWeight, griddedWeight2), then ft_p.c2cFFT(*weightLattice) on the Complex grid)

MosaicFT accumulates the gridded weights in DComplex but converts them to Complex before their inverse transform, so the weight image, and the .pb (sqrt(weight / max)) and pixel mask SIImageStore::makePBFromWeight form from it, carry single-precision rounding: about 1e-8 of the peak, which is a few 1e-6 of the weight where the beam meets a pblimit of 0.05. Pixels the image's symmetry makes equal show it: on refim_sim_hetarray_alma.ms (test_het_antenna_mosaic_cube_alma.3, channel 2), four mirror pixels have CASA beams 0.0500000405, 0.0500001221, 0.0499998446 and 0.0499997467, whose mean, 0.04999993, is casa-rs's 0.0499999261–0.0499999285 at all four. CASA keeps the first two and masks the others; casa-rs masks all four. At double grid precision casa-rs grids and transforms the weights in double precision, rounding each pixel to single only as it publishes it, and does not add CASA's rounding.

Every other pixel agrees: the cube mosaics of that MeasurementSet's cross baselines (.3) and of all its antennas (.4) differ from CASA in 2 and 1 .pb mask pixels of channel 2, each within 1.3e-7 of pblimit, and in no pixel of their other channels or of the 12 m, 7 m and two-field cubes (.1, .2, .5); their products agree to 4e-5 normalized RMS. Such pixels cannot measure parity.

docs.title: sm.predict phases a moved observemany pointing on its field
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows for parity (#884, which corrected the session's own phasing of #861)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/NewMSSimulator.cc (observe, the vector form observemany calls) and msvis/MSVis/VisBuffer.cc (phaseCenter, from FIELD)

A pointing observemany gives a direction keeps its field's FIELD row. NewMSSimulator computes its UVW and elevation at the direction and writes that direction to POINTING, but leaves FIELD as it was. predict reads the MeasurementSet through a VisBuffer, whose phase centre is FIELD's PHASE_DIR, so it phases the pointing on the field while its UVW belong to the moved direction. Measured on CASA 6.7.6 (twelve ALMA antennas, a second pointing moved 10.4″ east): a 1 Jy point at the field's direction predicts 1 Jy at zero phase in both pointings, and one at the moved direction predicts phases spread over ±180° (rms 101°) in the pointing centred on it.

casa-rs follows. A moved pointing's UVW, elevation limit and POINTING are at the moved direction (Scan::pointing_rad), and its DATA is phased on its field (Scan::phase_center_rad). Total power samples where POINTING points (#874), as CASA's SDGrid does. The phasing is what every imager and calibrator reading the MeasurementSet assumes: FIELD is the only phase centre it records, so DATA phased on the moved direction would image shifted by the offset. The UVW at the moved direction are CASA's inconsistency. They distort the geometry only at second order, in the offset times a source's distance from the phase centre.

Evidence on the CPU and on Metal: - components-moved-pointing in tools/simulation/sm_components_scenarios.json, an image and a component list without a beam: 8.36e-6 normalized RMS; - the openfromms-moved-pointing-* scenarios of sm_openfromms_scenarios.json: 0 and 7e-11.

A primary beam on a moved pointing is a separate matter, and casa-rs refuses it (the next entry).

docs.title: The beam on a moved pointing stays where the field's first row points
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs refuses a primary beam, and the mosaic machine, on a moved pointing rather than follow it (#884, PR #888 review)
  • Affected code: synthesis/TransformMachines/BeamSkyJones.cc (changed, update) and synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (makeVisSet's sort)

VPSkyJones, the simulator's primary beam, inherits BeamSkyJones::update, which takes the beam's centre from POINTING (VisBufferUtil::getPointingDir) at the row it updates on. It updates only when BeamSkyJones::changed fires: - the MeasurementSet, the array or the field changes; - the parallactic angle moves past setvp's parangleincrement. Its default of 360° means never; - POINTING is in a local frame and the time changes.

The comparisons of the pointing directions themselves are commented out. predict iterates FIELD_ID first, then FEED1, ARRAY_ID, DATA_DESC_ID and TIME. So every row of a field is beamed where the field's first-visited row points, whichever direction a later pointing of the field was moved to.

Measured on CASA 6.7.6, ALMA at 230 GHz, a second pointing moved 10.4″ east: - Field first, then moved: a point at the moved direction keeps 0.652 of the beam's peak in both pointings. The beam stays on the field. - Moved first, then back at the field (Astra's probe on PR #888): 1.0 in both. The beam stays on the moved direction. - Total power: SDGrid samples POINTING's moved direction while the beam stays where the first row pointed. With one antenna, a constant model and the BOX kernel, CASA's moved samples are 0.671.

None of these is the beam the moved pointing sees, which follows the antennas. casa-rs refuses a primary beam over a model image, a component list or total power, and the mosaic machine, on a pointing observemany moved off its field. It does not reproduce a cache. simobserve gives each pointing its own field and never reaches this.

docs.title: predict and corrupt add scratch columns to a MeasurementSet without them
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-23
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (plan decision 6)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (predict and corrupt build a VisSet) and msvis/MSVis/VisSet.cc (its constructor's addCalSet2 and initCalSet)

CASA's simulator writes its steps' results through a VisSet, whose constructor adds MODEL_DATA (1) and CORRECTED_DATA (DATA) to a MeasurementSet without CORRECTED_DATA. predict then sets CORRECTED_DATA to the new DATA and MODEL_DATA to 1, and corrupt sets CORRECTED_DATA to the corrupted DATA. casa-rs's simulator writes DATA only (plan decision 6), and after openfromms it creates neither column: it keeps those MAIN already has in step with DATA as CASA does, and leaves a MeasurementSet without them without them.

docs.title: CASA's gain screens read past their transform
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (fBM::initialize, GJonesCorruptor::initialize)

sm.setgain(mode='fbm') draws each antenna's amplitude and phase screens with fBM::initialize on n even slots of 5 s. It fills a half spectrum F of n/2 values, all but the last, and transforms it with FFTServer::fft into a real G whose length the server chooses: the last value's imaginary part is zero and the server was sized n, which is neither 2·(n/2) − 2 nor 2·(n/2) − 1, so G has n − 2 values for an even n and n − 3 for an odd one. It then copies n values out of G, the last two or three from past its end, and GJonesCorruptor::initialize scales each screen by its root-mean-square, those values included.

What lies past the end changes from run to run. Measured with CASA 6.7.6: - three runs of corrupt-gain (tools/simulation/sm_corrupt_scenarios.json, the same seed) gave amplitude scales of 0.969, 0.966 and 1.005 of the documented one; - in a six-antenna probe with amplitude=[0.1], the phases' scale was 0.15 to 0.22 of it in one run and 1.0 in another; - with a table written, one run's last solution was unit gain, as zeros past the end would make it; - in one run of corrupt-gain-table, antennas 0–6 and 10 of 12 had unit gain throughout, their screens normalised by a value large enough to flatten them.

casa-rs transforms every slot, so its screens have the documented scale. The CASA comparison holds CASA's gains to closure only, reports rather than checks CASA's unit-gain antennas, and compares the two implementations' screens by their autocorrelations, which a screen's scale does not change.

settrop(mode='individual')'s water-vapour series come from the same fBM::initialize and normalise the same way (#841 Phase 4d): in one probe, antenna 0's phases were all below 5·10⁻¹⁰ rad. casa-rs transforms every slot there too. On fewer than six slots the spectrum's bins i < N/2 − 1 hold only the mean, so whatever varies in CASA's series is what it read past the transform; casa-rs refuses individual mode on so short a track rather than add no turbulence.

docs.title: Gain screens of neighbouring antennas share a seed
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (GJonesCorruptor::initialize)

GJonesCorruptor::initialize seeds antenna a's amplitude screen for receptor r with seed + a + r, and its phase screen with 100 times that. Antenna a's second receptor and antenna a + 1's first draw the same screens: measured, their amplitudes are identical. casa-rs keys each antenna's and receptor's screens apart.

docs.title: setgain(mode='random') draws gains about zero
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (owner, 2026-10-24: follow CASA only if there is a good reason for its behaviour, which there is not; #841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (GJonesCorruptor::simPar)

The random mode, which setgain's documentation does not list but Simulator::setgain accepts, returns camp.re·n₁ + i·camp.im·n₂ per integration, antenna and receptor, without adding one: gains of a few hundredths, which all but erase the data. Measured with CASA 6.7.6, amplitude=[0.05] on a 1 Jy point: the table's gains have a mean modulus of 0.065, real parts of mean 0.0000 and standard deviation 0.048, and DATA a mean modulus of 0.0046 Jy. The fbm gains scatter about one, and the amplitude is documented as the gain variations' scale. Gain errors are multiplicative and near unity: a well-designed array's gains factor into antenna gains to within a per cent, and simulations of gain errors draw deviations of a per cent and a degree about one (Synthesis Imaging in Radio Astronomy II, pp. 122 and 354; Heywood, Calibration II, NRAO Synthesis Imaging Workshop 2024, slide 22). Nothing in CASA adds the one back for random; it appears in GJonesCorruptor::simPar and GJones::createCorruptor only. casa-rs draws 1 + camp.re·n₁ + i·camp.im·n₂.

docs.title: An autocorrelation row resets its antenna's simulated term
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate)

SolvableVisCal::setSimulate fills a solution from its chunk's rows, setting ANTENNA1's value at every row, and at an autocorrelation sets it to 1 for a multiplicative term instead of a draw. An antenna's autocorrelation comes before its cross-correlations as ANTENNA1, which set it again, except for the last antenna, which is ANTENNA1 only of its autocorrelation. So with autocorrelations written, CASA's default, the last antenna has unit gain throughout (setgain) and a leakage of 1 on both receptors (setleakage); measured, antenna 42 of 43 in corrupt-gain. casa-rs simulates every antenna's term. settrop's Tf term takes the same loop (its modes are not ones whose autocorrelations CASA simulates), and casa-rs simulates every antenna's there too (#841 Phase 4d).

docs.title: setleakage simulates only the first two spectral windows
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate, sizeUpSim); the cause was not traced

Measured with CASA 6.7.6, five ALMA antennas and setleakage(table=...): with three, four or eight spectral windows, observed once or twice each, the table has solutions for windows 0 and 1 only, and corrupt logs "Encountered data spw N for which there is no (simulated) calibration" for each later window and leaves its rows as they were. setgain is not affected: with four windows its table has solutions for all four, and every window is corrupted. casa-rs simulates a leakage for every window. The CASA comparison, corrupt-leakage, observes two windows.

docs.title: setleakage draws one leakage per window for the whole run
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (setleakage), synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate) and JonesGenLin

Simulator::setleakage simulates with an infinite solution interval: its table has one solution per spectral window and antenna, spanning every scan and field, and corrupt applies it alike to every scan (measured: eight scans of two windows). corrupt applies it as the linearised JonesGenLin, which raises "JonesGenLin matrix apply (J::aR) incompatible with VisVector." on data with two correlations. casa-rs follows both, and likewise does not read setgain's interval, whose documentation says it is not used: CASA's gains are solved per integration.

docs.title: A simulated term's table is written when the term is set
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate, storeNCT) and NewCalTable::writeToDisk

setgain(table=...) and setleakage(table=...) write the term's calibration table as soon as they simulate it, replacing a table of that name, its subtables copied from the MeasurementSet as it then is. casa-rs writes the MeasurementSet only at close, so it writes the table there, from the MeasurementSet it wrote: its rows, sorted by spectral window, time and antenna as CASA sorts them, are the same (tables in tools/simulation/sm_corrupt_scenarios.json compares them with CASA's), but the table appears at close, after reset too, and its subtables include what was observed after the call. casa-rs replaces only a table at the path; anything else there is refused.

docs.title: tsys-manual noise takes stale or borrowed system temperatures
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bugs; casa-rs does not follow them (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (AtmosCorruptor::setCurrTime and simPar), synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate) and synthesis/MeasurementComponents/Jones.cc (JonesScal::invert, setMatByOk)

setnoise(mode='tsys-manual') adds a unit-amplitude ANoise term and a T term flagged NoiseScale, whose inverse scales the noise: σ_ij = c a / sqrt(Δν t) · sqrt(Tsys(A_i) Tsys(A_j)) / (D_i D_j) (casa_simulation's corrupt::tsys has the whole formula). CASA computes the T table when setnoise is called, one solution per integration and spectral window, and applies it at corrupt by the nearest time.
