Measured on CASA 6.7.6 (the probe scripts and their results are on the NAS under casa-rs/issue-841-tsys-3a/probes; seven antennas of 12 m and 7 m, per-row variances over 32 to 128 channels): the formula holds to 4·10⁻⁴ (cross 0.99999 ± 0.00036, autocorrelations 1.0003 ± 0.0009, 12+12, 12+7 and 7+7 m pairs alike, and to 6·10⁻⁴ with every parameter away from its default), and CASA's T table, written with integrations of 120 s so that the cache below refreshes at each, gives every row's σ within 1.9·10⁻⁶ of casa-rs's (5,040 rows, two windows). But four inputs are not the row's own:

  • The airmass is up to 100 s stale. simPar caches each antenna's airmass and setCurrTime recomputes it only when the solution time has moved more than 100 s since (the comment's intent is a 1 % tolerance at elevations above 5°). At 10 to 14° elevation with τ₀ = 1 and 2 s integrations, CASA's per-integration variance against the formula at the integration's own time rises in a sawtooth with a 102 s period from 1.01 to 1.56, 1.176 ± 0.0014 on average. The cache is not reset at a field change either.
  • Rows observed after setnoise take another integration's solution. The table holds only the integrations observed by then; a scan observed later is scaled by the nearest one. A scan at 51.6° elevation observed after setnoise got the noise of the earlier scan's last integration at 72.7°: 0.666 ± 0.002 of its own variance (τ₀ = 0.5).
  • Every row takes the first row's EXPOSURE (exposure()(0)): after settimes changed the integration time from 10 s to 2 s, the 2 s scan's variance was 0.1999 of its own, 0.9994 of the first row's.
  • An antenna without an unflagged row applies as 1. setSimulate skips fully flagged rows, so a shadowed or low antenna gets no solution; JonesScal::invert marks it bad and setMatByOk applies it as 1. Its rows get the unit noise times the other antenna's scale (variance 1.0006 of 1 Jy² when both are bad, 1.009 of s_j² when one is).

casa-rs computes each row's σ from its own integration: each antenna's airmass at the phase centre at the row's TIME, the row's EXPOSURE, its window and dishes, whatever the flags and whenever the row was observed. The CASA comparison scenarios (tools/simulation/sm_noise_scenarios.json) observe above 40° elevation with one integration time and no flagged rows, where the stale airmass moves Tsys by under 0.1 %. casa-rs keeps CASA's rule for a T that is not finite and positive (Tsys overflowing single precision below the horizon, airmass 1000): that antenna scales by 1.

docs.title: A tsys-manual term scales every noise term
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (owner, 2026-10-24: follow CASA only if its product is the better simulation, which it is not; #841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/VisEquation.cc (collapseForSim)

collapseForSim first adds every ANoise term's noise to DATA, then applies every NoiseScale T term to DATA, in correct mode. So each tsys-manual term's scale multiplies the noise of every term, its own and the others'. Measured on CASA 6.7.6: two tsys-manual terms of one seed gave variance 4 σ⁴ (1.004 of it) rather than 4 σ², in Jy⁴, and a 0.5 Jy simplenoise term with a tsys-manual term gave (0.25 + 1) σ² (0.998 of it) rather than 0.25 + σ²: the 0.5 Jy noise came out scaled by the system temperature. casa-rs adds each term's noise with its own σ, as simplenoise terms add, so simplenoise's σ stays in Jy whatever else is set; terms of one seed still add coherently. simobserve sets one noise term and never reaches this.

CASA's product has no physical counterpart. A system temperature is the sum of its contributions (receiver, atmosphere, spillover, CMB), which a single tsys-manual term already models; a baseline's noise variance scales as the product of its two antennas' system temperatures; and the powers of uncorrelated noise add (Thompson, Moran & Swenson, Interferometry and Synthesis in Radio Astronomy, 3rd ed., pp. 55, 266, 386 and 733). Multiplying one term's σ by another's gives Jy², not a noise in Jy.

docs.title: A refused tsys-manual setnoise leaves a unit noise term
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 3)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Simulator.cc (setnoise)

setnoise creates the unit-amplitude ANoise term before it checks the Tsys parameters. A water vapour above 100 mm, or a zenith Tsys that is not positive or above 10⁶ K, then makes it return False, but the ANoise stays: the next corrupt adds 1 Jy of noise (CASA 6.7.6, pwv='200mm': variance 0.872 over cross- and autocorrelations, where 1 Jy gives 0.875). casa-rs refuses such a setnoise without adding a term. tsys-atm takes the same path in setnoise (the ANoise is created before either Tsys mode's checks; read from the source, not measured), and casa-rs refuses it the same way.

docs.title: tsys-atm noise takes its atmosphere half a band below each channel
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bugs; casa-rs does not follow them (#841 Phase 4c)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (AtmosCorruptor::initAtm, tsys, opac) and synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate)

setnoise(mode='tsys-atm') scales a unit ANoise by a Tf term ("TF NOISE") whose Tsys comes from ATM for each channel: Tsys(A, c) = (hν/k) e^(τA) (1/(e^(hν/k/T_ebb(A)) − 1) + T_rx/(hν/k)) (1 + g), τ the zenith opacity and T_ebb the sky's equivalent blackbody temperature at airmass A, with hν/k from the channel's frequency (casa_simulation's corrupt::tsys_atm has the whole model). Measured on CASA 6.7.6 (ALMA's site defaults, 1 mm of water, 64-channel windows of 100 MHz from 180 GHz, across the 183 GHz line, and from 321 GHz, 2 s integrations; the probe scripts and results are on the NAS under casa-rs/issue-841-tsys-4c), every channel's noise variance agrees with that formula, through casa-atmosphere, with no free parameter (ratio 1.0000 and 1.0027, rms 0.0106 and 0.0100 per channel, against a statistical 1σ of 0.0149) once the atmosphere is taken at the frequencies CASA gives ATM, which are not the channels':

  • The atmosphere is half a band below the channel. initAtm builds each window's ATM grid from REF_FREQUENCY, which the simulator sets to the first channel's frequency, with the reference at the middle channel: ATM's channel i is at REF + (i − n/2)·Δν for the first window and REF + (i − n/2 − 1)·Δν for the others, and opac and tsys read channel c of that grid. So channel c's τ and T_ebb are those of a frequency half the band below it (3.2 GHz for the probe's windows), while hν/k is the channel's own. Against the atmosphere at each channel's own frequency, CASA's variance across the 183 GHz line is off by a mean factor of 6.1 and up to 103; at 321 GHz by 0.39 on average and up to 5.5. The shift grows with the window's width and matters wherever the atmosphere changes across it: the 183 GHz line's brightness changes by tens of kelvin over a few GHz at a 5,000 m site (Thompson, Moran & Swenson, Interferometry and Synthesis in Radio Astronomy, 3rd ed., p. 746, Fig. 13.21), and an ozone line at 231.7 GHz nearly doubles ALMA's system temperature within a band (B. Svoboda, Special Topics: Spectral Lines, NRAO Synthesis Imaging Workshop 2026, slide 18).
  • A one-channel window after the first gets no Tsys. For n = 1 the later windows' channel map is read past its end, which is undefined behaviour. In CASA 6.7.6 on macOS the index it read pointed past the grid (the log reads "ch 972849296/20"); the term's T came out bad, setMatByOk applied it as 1, and the probe's 2 GHz continuum window at 230 GHz got unscaled 1 Jy noise (variance 0.996 Jy²). Another build may read something else.

casa-rs evaluates ATM at each channel's CHAN_FREQ, for every window and a one-channel window alike, so a channel's σ follows the sky it observes. As for tsys-manual, each row takes its own integration's airmasses and EXPOSURE (stale and borrowed system temperatures); the term is also refused when its zenith Tsys at the first window's centre is not a number, which CASA's check (> 10⁶ K or ≤ 0) lets through.

docs.title: settrop turns the phase by the dispersive wet delay alone
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 4d)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (AtmosCorruptor::cphase)

sm.settrop adds a Tf Jones term whose value for antenna a in channel c is exp(i·δ_a·φ(c)): δ the fractional excess of water vapour over pwv above the antenna (fractional Brownian motion of rms deltapwv) and φ ATM's zenith wet phase delay for pwv (casa_simulation's corrupt::troposphere has the whole model). cphase takes φ from SkyStatus::getDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay: the dispersive part alone, the refraction the water lines add. Measured on CASA 6.7.6 (seven antennas, 1 mm of water, 64-channel windows of 100 MHz from 180 GHz, across the 183 GHz line, and of 15.625 MHz at 230 GHz; tools/simulation/sm_trop_scenarios.json, probes on the NAS under casa-rs/issue-841-trop-4d), each row of CASA's table is one δ times that dispersive delay (on CASA's grid, below) to 2.2·10⁻⁵ (single precision), where the whole wet delay at the channels' frequencies leaves δ spread across a row by 0.17 of itself (median).

The path a column of water vapour adds is mostly its non-dispersive part, the refractivity of the water molecule's permanent dipole: ℒ_V ≃ 6.3w, "an excellent approximation for frequencies below 100 GHz", rising to about 8w in the windows above (Thompson, Moran & Swenson, Interferometry and Synthesis in Radio Astronomy, 3rd ed., eq. 13.19, p. 702). At settrop's site ATM gives 7.0 mm of path per mm of water at 100 GHz, and the whole wet delay is 940, 119, 36, 23 and 8.5 times the dispersive part at 43, 100, 183, 230 and 345 GHz. With settrop's defaults (3 mm of water fluctuating by 15 %), CASA's phases have an rms of 3° at 100 GHz and 39° at 230 GHz where a fluctuation that size in the water column turns the phase by about 380° and 910°.

casa-rs takes the whole wet delay, the dispersive and non-dispersive parts together, so deltapwv means the fluctuation of the water column it names. With CASA's defaults the phases are then fully scrambled at millimetre wavelengths; a deltapwv of 1 % of 3 mm (30 µm of water) turns them by about 60° rms at 230 GHz.

docs.title: settrop takes its atmosphere half a band below each channel
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 4d)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (AtmosCorruptor::initAtm, cphase)

settrop's delays come from the same ATM grid as tsys-atm's noise, and cphase reads channel c of it through the same channel map: each channel's φ is the atmosphere's half a band below it, and a one-channel window after the first reads the map past its end (tsys-atm's atmosphere half a band away). In the Phase 4d probe's CASA table, δ (a row's phase over the dispersive delay) is one value across the row to 2.8·10⁻⁶ of itself with the delay on that grid, and spreads by 2.5 of itself across the 183 GHz line with the delay at the channels' own frequencies. casa-rs evaluates ATM at each channel's CHAN_FREQ.

docs.title: settrop's screen has an anisotropic spectrum
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bugs; casa-rs does not follow them (#841 Phase 4d)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/CalCorruptor.cc (fBM::initialize, two dimensions)

settrop(mode='screen') blows one two-dimensional screen of fractional Brownian motion across the array. fBM::initialize fills a half spectrum F2(i, j), i along the wind (the half axis) and j across it, with amplitudes |(i, j)|^−(β+½)/2 times a normal draw (its comment: "still something not quite right with exponent"; an earlier line, left commented out, had −(β+1)/2):

  • The wavenumbers are indices. The screen is long along the wind (CASA's probe screen was 1,359 by 271 pixels), so an index along it is a fifth of the wavenumber of an index across it: the spectrum is stretched along the wind, and the screen is not isotropic.
  • The full axis is not wrapped. j runs to the screen's width, where the indices past half of it are negative wavenumbers; taking them as large ones gives the negative wavenumbers the smallest amplitudes.
  • The exponent. A two-dimensional fractional Brownian motion whose cuts have the spectral exponent β (as individual mode's series, and beta's documentation, have it) has amplitudes |k|^−(β+1)/2.
  • Out of bounds. It sets the imaginary parts of F2(s0/2, 0) and F2(s0/2, s1/2), one past the end of the half axis's s0/2 entries, and a half axis of s0/2 entries transforms to s0 − 2 real pixels along the wind, of which it copies s0: the last two from past the end of the output, as the one-dimensional series do (gain screens read past their transform). CASA's own settrop test is skipped for "intermittent failures".

Isotropic turbulence's phase spectrum depends only on the spatial frequency's size, |q|^−11/3 in two dimensions (Thompson, Moran & Swenson, 3rd ed., sec. 13.1.7, p. 725). casa-rs draws |k|^−(β+1)/2 on the wavenumbers in cycles per pixel, the full axis wrapped, with the conjugate pairs and real bins the real transform needs on the half axis's first and Nyquist columns (drawn apart, those modes come out at half the power), and transforms every pixel: on a screen five times as long as wide its structure function is the same along the wind and across it, where CASA's differ by five, and its boundary modes have their interior neighbours' power (corrupt::troposphere's unit tests).

docs.title: settrop with simint stamps a solution halfway to its interval's start
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 4d)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc (setSimulate)

With simint longer than an integration, setSimulate iterates the MeasurementSet in intervals of simint and keeps a solution for each integration, stamped (t₀ + t)/2, t₀ the interval's first integration's time and t its own, and takes the screen's slot nearest that stamp. Measured on CASA 6.7.6 (simint=6 on 2 s integrations): the table's times are 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, … s for integrations at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 s, and corrupt, applying the solution nearest each row's time, gives an interval's later integrations a slot from earlier in it. casa-rs stamps each solution with its integration's time and takes the slot nearest it, as CASA does when simint is not set (each integration its own interval). The slots are simint wide either way.

docs.title: ATM's HCN catalogue misplaces a line at 106 GHz
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM data error; casa-rs corrects it (#841 Phase 4, casa-atmosphere; owner decision, 2026-10-24)
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndex.cc:796 (mkSpecificRefractivity_hcn, fre[18])

HCN's rotational lines are spaced by about 88.6 GHz (J=1–0 at 88.631 GHz, 2–1 at 177.260, 3–2 at 265.886; Synthesis Imaging in Radio Astronomy II, printed p. 568, PDF p. 592): the table runs 88.63, 177.26, …, 974.49 GHz, then gives the J=12–11 line as 106.298069519 before continuing at 1151.45 GHz. The line belongs at 1062.98 GHz (as the JPL catalogue has it, c027001.cat); the decimal point moved. ATM therefore sums a J=12–11-strength HCN line at 106.3 GHz and none at 1063 GHz. HCN is a trace gas (a few 1e-4 ppmv), but near 106.3 GHz the misplaced line is not negligible: with the default Chajnantor profile, the compiled C++ gives a zenith opacity of 0.029368 at 106.298 GHz, of which HCN is 4.5·10⁻⁴; with the line moved to 1062.98 GHz it gives 0.028919, HCN 1.3·10⁻⁷, so the total is 1.5 % high there (measured in the #894 review). Away from 106.3 GHz the line's wings fall off (in at_tool_check.py's bands the correction moves the dry opacity by at most 3.5·10⁻⁵ and Tebb by 1.3·10⁻⁵, at 90 GHz), and at 1063 GHz the missing line is lost among water's.

casa-rs moves the decimal point back: the line is at 1062.98069519 GHz. The correction is one of four in tools/atmosphere/atm-corrections.patch, which extract_atm_tables.py applies before it generates the port's tables and build-atm-oracle.sh before it compiles the C++ the tests compare with. at_tool_check.py shows the C++ built without the patch equals CASA's at tool (to 7.5·10⁻¹⁵) and the port equals the C++ built with it (to 8.1·10⁻¹⁵), so the port differs from the at tool by the four corrections alone.

docs.title: ATM's reference air densities drop a digit at sea level
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM data error; casa-rs corrects it (#841 Phase 4; owner decision, 2026-10-24)
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMProfile.cc:1360, :1367, :1374, :1381, :1388 (st76, den[6][50])

st76 converts the minor gases' mixing ratios to number densities with a tabulated air density. For the mid-latitude, subarctic and US Standard atmospheres the sea-level entry has lost its leading digit: .496E+19, .711E+19, .549E+19, .855E+19, .548E+19 cm⁻³ where the next entries (2.26e19 and so on at 1 km) and the tropical profile's 2.450e19 show about 2.5e19 was meant. The parabola st76 fits through 0, 1 and 2 km then falls far below the true density near the ground: in the committed sea-level mid-latitude summer case, restoring the digit raises the first layer's interpolated density 4.075 times (#894 review). So O3, N2O, CO, NO2, SO2, HCl and HCN are up to about four times too scarce in layers whose middle is below 1 km. Only sea-level-to-1-km sites with those atmospheres see it, and those gases' columns lie mostly higher.

casa-rs restores the digit: 2.496e19, 2.711e19, 2.549e19, 2.855e19 and 2.548e19 cm⁻³. Air density falls with height, by about e⁻¹ in a dry-air scale height of 8 km (Interferometry and Synthesis in Radio Astronomy, 3rd ed., printed pp. 661 and 668, PDF pp. 700 and 707), and the restored values fall by 0.88 to 0.91 to their 1 km entries, as the tropical profile's untouched 2.450e19 does; the typo's values rise 3 to 5 times instead. The US Standard Atmosphere's sea-level 1013.25 hPa and 288.15 K give 2.547e19 by the ideal gas law. In at_tool_check.py's humid sea-level atmosphere (mid-latitude summer) the correction raises the O3, CO and N2O line opacities by up to 1.8 %, 7.7 % and 8.5 % and the dry opacity by up to 0.22 % (at 690 GHz); Tebb moves by at most 1.2·10⁻⁵. Sites at 1 km and above do not change.

docs.title: ATM weights H2(17)O by the (18)O abundance
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM bug; casa-rs corrects it (#841 Phase 4; owner decision, 2026-10-24)
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndex.cc:449 (mkEarthSpecificRefractivity, ratiohh17o)

ratiohh17o = abun_18o/(1+abun_18o+abun_17o+2.0*abun_d) uses the (18)O/(16)O ratio (0.0020439) where the (17)O ratio (0.000375) belongs, so H2(17)O lines are 5.45 times too strong. ATM's own (17)O fractions for oxygen and ozone use abun_17o. casa-rs does too. Over at_tool_check.py's atmospheres and bands the correction lowers the wet opacity by up to 0.61 % (at 990 GHz) and Tebb by up to 0.087 % (at 460 GHz), and changes the dispersive wet phase by up to 4 % where it is small (at 380 GHz); at Chajnantor the zenith opacity at 230 GHz moves by 2·10⁻⁴.

docs.title: ATM's HDO weight divides by three
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM typo; casa-rs corrects it (#841 Phase 4; owner decision, 2026-10-24)
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndex.cc:450 (mkEarthSpecificRefractivity, ratiohdo)

ratiohdo = 2.0*abun_d/(1+abun_18o+abun_17o+2-0*abun_d) reads 2-0*abun_d (that is, 2) where every sibling ratio has 2.0*abun_d. The denominator is 3.0024 instead of 1.0030, so HDO lines are about three times too weak. casa-rs uses 2.0*abun_d. Of the four corrections this one matters most: at Chajnantor the zenith opacity rises 0.32 % at 230 GHz (near HDO's 225.9 GHz line) and 0.15 % at 90 GHz (near its 80.6 GHz line), with Tebb 0.24 % and 0.10 % higher; over at_tool_check.py's atmospheres and bands the wet opacity rises by up to 1.8 % and Tebb by up to 0.47 % (both at 850 GHz).

docs.title: ATM's HCN profile stops at 100 km
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM data gap; casa-rs follows it (#841 Phase 4): there are no values to restore, and the air above 90 km (below 0.002 hPa) is about 2·10⁻⁶ of the column
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMProfile.cc:1429 (st76, hcn[50])

hcn[50] is initialised with 45 values, so C++ zero-fills its last five levels (100 to 120 km) and the interpolated HCN falls to zero over them. A layer whose middle is above 90 km already interpolates toward the zero at 100 km: the tropical fixture keeps, under a 95 km top, a layer with its middle at 90.8 km and its top at 94.1 km (#894 review). So profiles topped above about 90 km see the gap; tools/atmosphere/extract_atm_tables.py reports it whenever it regenerates the tables.

docs.title: Copying an AtmProfile copies its top pressures as bottom pressures
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM bug; no effect on what casa-rs ports
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMProfile.cc:567 (copy constructor)

The copy constructor fills v_layerPressure0_ from a.v_layerPressure1_. RefractiveIndexProfile (and so SkyStatus) copies its AtmProfile this way, so their getLayerBottomPressure returns each layer's top pressure and setAltitude would take a wrong ground pressure. No opacity, path or brightness calculation reads bottom pressures. casa-atmosphere keeps one profile and never copies it through such a path.

docs.title: ATM leaves the ozone isotopologue layers unpadded
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: latent ATM bug; does not arise with ATM's own profiles
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndexProfile.cc:723–725 (mkRefractiveIndexProfile)

For a layer without ozone, mkRefractiveIndexProfile pushes a zero onto the total-ozone vector only. The eight ozone state and isotopologue vectors get nothing, so they become shorter than the layer count and later layers' values shift down one place. ATM's standard profiles have ozone in every layer, so this needs a user profile with zero ozone.

docs.title: ATM omits (16)O(17)O
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: deliberate in ATM; casa-rs follows it
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndex.cc:3252 (mkSpecificRefractivity_16o17o)

The (16)O(17)O function returns zero before its line loop. The comment says the isotope was removed in 2024 while its catalogue is reviewed, because it gave lines that do not exist. The port returns zero too and keeps the catalogue in its tables for the record.

docs.title: RefractiveIndexProfile's averaged non-dispersive wet phase reads a channel as a water column
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: ATM bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 4b)
  • Affected code: atmosphere/ATM/ATMRefractiveIndexProfile.cc:2466 (getAverageNonDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay(const Length &, unsigned int))

The window average calls getNonDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay(v_transfertId_[spwid] + i). RefractiveIndexProfile has no overload taking a channel alone, so the index converts to a Length in metres, and the call returns channel 0's phase for a water column of 0, 1, 2 … metres. The average is then scaled again by the requested column. For the simulator's Chajnantor atmosphere and 1.3 mm of water this gives 306,132° in a 22 GHz window, where the channels' mean is a few degrees (casa-atmosphere's oracle_absorption test reproduces ATM's number exactly). CASA's at tool does not reach this function: its averages go through SkyStatus, whose override is correct. casa-atmosphere takes the mean of the channels' phases.

docs.title: VisCalSolver2 fails a solve whose chi-square is exactly zero
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-24
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#903, #905)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/VisCalSolver2.cc:180–185 (and :353–358, the other solve overload), CASA 6.7.5.18

Each Levenberg-Marquardt iteration recomputes chi-square and, if it is exactly 0.0, prints "CHI2 IS SPURIOUSLY ZERO!" and returns False, so Calibrater::genericGatherAndSolve records no solution for the interval (and writes no table when no interval solves). Chi-square is exactly zero only when the current gains reproduce every unflagged sample to the last bit, which in practice means noise-free synthetic data whose first guess is already the answer. That is an exact fit, not a failure; CASA's oracle runs on the casa-rs gain fixtures had to add noise to get a table at all. casa-rs's solve_graphs keeps an exact fit as a solution. A chi-square that is small but not zero follows CASA's convergence rule unchanged, so noise-free data that converge only linearly can still reach CASA's 50-iteration limit and fail as CASA's would.

docs.title: calc_pointings2's ALMA tiling reads an undefined pbcoeff
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-26
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5a)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:611 (calc_pointings2)

For maptype='ALMA' (and its aliases alma, ALMA-OT), when the caller gives no primary beam (beam <= 0), calc_pointings2 defaults it to spacing_asec*pbcoeff*pl.sqrt(3). pbcoeff is a local of task_simobserve.py, not defined in simutil.py, so the call raises NameError (CASA 6.7.6). simobserve reaches it with an ALMA map and no antenna list, and any script that calls calc_pointings2 directly without beam does too. casa-rs uses simobserve's value, 1.13, as the default clearly intends (casa_simulation::simutil::pointings::PBCOEFF); the pointings are then those of the beam spacing × 1.13 × √3.

docs.title: noisetemp reads the wrong receiver temperature at the edges of its tables
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-26
  • Status: CASA bugs; casa-rs does not follow them (#841 Phase 5a)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:1124–1134 (noisetemp)

noisetemp looks the receiver temperature up with while(f0[z]<obsfreq and z<len(t0)): z+=1 and then t_rx=t0[z-1]:

  • At the first band edge. A frequency at or above the table's lower limit but not above its first edge leaves z = 0, and t0[-1] is Python's last entry. ALMA, ACA and total power at exactly 35 GHz get 230 K (band 10's) instead of 28 K, the (E)VLA from 0.8 to 1 GHz 28 K (Q band's) instead of 10 K, and the SMA at 180 GHz 500 K instead of 67 K. casa-rs takes the first temperature there.
  • Above the last edge of an unknown telescope's table. For a telescope noisetemp does not know, the frequency edges and temperatures are lists of the same length ([10, 900], [200, 200]), so above 900 GHz the test reads f0[2] before checking z and raises IndexError (CASA 6.7.6, WSRT at 950 GHz). casa-rs keeps the last temperature, 200 K. For the telescopes it knows, the edges have one more entry than the temperatures and the test does not overrun.

The efficiencies are unchanged. tools/simulation/simutil_oracle.py records both cases, and tests/simutil_casa.rs checks that casa-rs departs exactly there.

docs.title: direction_splitter cannot split a direction without an epoch
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-26
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs refuses the input (#841 Phase 5a)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:876–894 (direction_splitter)

direction_splitter keeps the epoch only when a direction has three fields, but reads the longitude from field 1 and the latitude from field 2 whatever the count. A direction without an epoch ('18h00m00 -23d00m00') therefore raises IndexError, and a latitude its regular expression ([+-]?\d+).(\d+).(\d+\.?\d*) does not match raises AttributeError (CASA 6.7.6). casa-rs refuses both with "can't interpret ... as a direction", the message isdirection gives, so a simobserve that is given such a direction stops with a clear error rather than a traceback. A direction with more than three fields is split as CASA splits it (no epoch, fields 1 and 2).

docs.title: modifymodel swaps axes into place and refuses a cyclic order
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5b)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:2951–2971 (modifymodel)

modifymodel finds which of the model's axes is each of the four it writes (direction, direction, Stokes, spectral) and then moves them with for ax in range(4): if axmap[ax] != ax: arr = arr.swapaxes(ax, axmap[ax]), marking both axes done after each swap. That orders a model whose axes are a transposition of the four (the FITS order, spectral before Stokes), but not a cyclic one: a model with its spectral axis first ([spectral, RA, Dec, Stokes]) is left out of order, and the check before it raises "internal error: I'm confused about the shape if your model data cube" (CASA 6.7.6), with the new image already created and empty. casa-rs permutes the axes, so any order of the four is written as [RA, Dec, Stokes, spectral]; tests/skymodel_casa.rs checks the cyclic case pixel by pixel.

docs.title: modifymodel labels the new image's Stokes planes by their count
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5b)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:2838–2912 (modifymodel)

modifymodel returns the model's Stokes labels (model_stokes), but the image it writes takes its Stokes axis from ia.fromshape, whose default coordinate system labels the planes by their count: I, IQ, IQU or IQUV (CoordinateUtil::addStokesAxis). So: - a model labelled I and V comes out labelled I and Q, the V data then read as Stokes Q; - three unlabelled planes come out IQU, though modifymodel warns "setting IQV Stokes parameters from the 4th axis of you model" and returns "IQV".

casa-rs keeps the model's labels and labels unlabelled planes as modifymodel reports them (IQV for three). Models of Stokes I alone, the usual case, are unaffected. A model labelled in a circular or linear basis (RR and LL, or XX and YY) also keeps its labels, so flatimage (which wants a Stokes I plane) and adding components (which wants I, Q, U or V) refuse it, where CASA relabels it I and Q and goes on; simobserve's sky model is a brightness in Stokes parameters.

docs.title: modifymodel indexes the map it makes of two cells
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5b)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py:2631–2632, 2720 (modifymodel)

Given incell as a list of two cells, modifymodel converts them with incell = map(qa.convert, incell, ['arcsec', 'arcsec']) and later reads incell[0]. Under Python 3 map returns an iterator, and the index raises TypeError: 'map' object is not subscriptable (CASA 6.7.6). casa-rs takes the two cells, converted to arcsec and used as given (signs included), as the code did under Python 2. A single cell is unaffected: it becomes [−cell, cell].

docs.title: An unset compwidth gives the component-only model a meaningless spectral increment
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5b)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py:506

With a component list and no sky image, simobserve observes a bandwidth of compwidth, or 2 GHz when compwidth is not a quantity, but sets the .compskymodel image's spectral increment with modelcsys.setincrement(type="spectral", value=compwidth) whatever it is. For compwidth="", coordsys.setincrement puts a meaningless value there: in CASA 6.7.6 the model's right ascension in radians, read as hertz (4.976 Hz for RA 19h). casa-rs uses the 2 GHz simobserve observes with. The increment is the model's only spectral information beyond its reference frequency, since the model has one channel.

docs.title: ia.modify converts a component spectrum through the image's default measures frame
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA behaviour; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5b)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/imageanalysis/Images/ComponentListImage.cc (_cacheCoordinateInfo), components/ComponentModels/SpectralModel.cc:100–116 (refFreqInFrame)

When ia.modify adds a component list to an image, each spectral model converts its reference frequency into the image's spectral frame (refFreqInFrame) through the measures frame of the image's spectral coordinate. An image made from a shape (ia.fromshape, as modifymodel and simobserve make theirs) has that frame at its defaults: the geocentre, an epoch of 0, and the J2000 pole, the same defaults as the measures tool's. So a TOPO spectrum on an LSRK image, or LSRK spectra on a TOPO image, are shifted by a velocity no observation has, about 1e-4 of the frequency in CASA 6.7.6's oracle, which a spectral index turns into a flux difference of about 1e-4.

casa-rs converts as CASA does when the image's conversion layer carries a real frame: an epoch and an observatory position (and the direction). The oracle's LSRD image, with an LSRK conversion layer at the VLA on 2025-06-01, agrees with CASA to 1e-6 (a 1 Jy point at the reference frequency stays 1 Jy). With no conversion layer, or the placeholder (an epoch of 0 at the geocentre), casa-rs takes the frequencies as they are: a meaningful conversion would need the observation's epoch and position, which such a sky model does not carry.

Components in the image's own frame, the usual case, are unaffected. The oracle's matched-frame cases (LSRK spectra on an LSRK cube, TOPO spectra on a TOPO cube) agree with CASA to 1e-6, where the same cube with spectra in the other frame and only the placeholder differs by 1.1e-4.

docs.title: simobserve's calibrator: the last pass, its scans and two component lists
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bugs; casa-rs does not follow them (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6: the observing loop, sm.setdata(fieldid=range(0,nfld)), and the complist+","+cal.cclist joins); Simulator::createSkyEquation

With a phase calibrator (caldirection and calflux), CASA 6.7.6's simobserve has three faults. Each was measured by tools/simulation/simobserve_parity.py's CASA runs.

The last pass. The observing loop calls observemany for the map's pointings only when a pass over them completes, and observes the calibrator after it. Pointings of a pass that totaltime ends inside are collected but never observed. With totaltime='300s' over a 105-pointing map at 10 s, CASA's MeasurementSet holds the calibrator's one scan and no pointing at all. casa-rs observes the pointings the time allows, as CASA does without a calibrator. With totaltime a whole number of passes, the two schedules are the same.

The calibrator's scans. Before predicting, the task selects the map's fields, setdata(fieldid=range(0,nfld)). The calibrator's field is nfld, so its scans keep the zeros observe wrote; noise is then added to them. casa-rs predicts every scan, the calibrator's included.

Two component lists. With a complist and a calibrator, the task predicts from complist + "," + <stem>.cal.cclist. createSkyEquation opens that string as one table, which does not exist ("ComponentList … not readable"), so predict returns False. The task does not check it: the MeasurementSet is left unpredicted, every visibility zero, for a model image with a list or for a list alone. casa-rs predicts both lists, as one list of their components (PredictSpec::component_lists).

The parity cases calibrator and calibrator_lists compare casa-rs with CASA's own simulator doing what the task meant: CASA's MeasurementSet predicted again over every field, from the model image and the lists merged into one. DATA agrees to an NRMS of 5.3e-9 and 5.5e-9.

docs.title: simobserve leaves <stem>.noisier.T.cal
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, setnoise(..., table=noisymsroot) and the clean-up)

tsys-atm noise is set with table=<noisy root>, so CASA writes the T term's table beside the noisy MeasurementSet. The task's clean-up deletes <stem>.noisy.T.cal and <stem>.noisy.sd.T.cal, but not <stem>.noisier.T.cal, the one written when leakage comes first. The table is a by-product the task means to remove; casa-rs writes no Tsys table for any of the three.

docs.title: simobserve's observing loop never ends for pointings of no length
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs refuses the input (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, the while (sttime-scanstart) < totalsec loop)

The loop advances the time by each pointing's scan length. When the lengths of a pass sum to zero, as they do for integration='0s' or a pointing file of zero times, the time never advances and CASA loops forever, collecting pointings. casa-rs refuses such a schedule with a message.

docs.title: simutil.ismstp takes any zero UVW value for total power
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py (ismstp)

When simobserve corrupts an existing MeasurementSet (obsmode=''), it asks ismstp whether the data are total power. For a MeasurementSet whose first antenna's name has no TP and which has more than one antenna, the test is uvw.all() == 0.. That is true when any UVW value is zero, not when all are. An interferometer's MeasurementSet with one zero coordinate is then corrupted as a single dish's, with the wrong file names and sensitivity constant. casa-rs tests whether every value is zero.

docs.title: simobserve deletes a sky model that is the model it writes
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs refuses the input (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, the newmodel set-up)

The task writes <project>/<stem>.skymodel, or <stem>.newmodel when skymodel is the bare name <stem>.skymodel. Given the full path <project>/<stem>.skymodel, as a rerun on an earlier run's model would give it, the output is the input: with overwrite=True, the default, CASA deletes it and then fails to read it. casa-rs refuses it, and the model is left in place.

docs.title: simobserve nests a project path inside itself
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA limitation; casa-rs departs (#841 Phase 5c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, fileroot + "/" + project)

The task makes the directory project and names its files fileroot + "/" + project + "." + <configuration>, so a project given as a path, a/b, names its files a/b/a/b.<cfg>…, in a directory that does not exist. Only a plain name in the working directory works. casa-rs names the files by the directory's last component, a/b/b.<cfg>…. For a plain name the two are the same.

docs.title: simobserve writes through a symbolic link in the project
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA limitation; casa-rs departs (#841 Phase 5c, #920 review)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, shutil.copyfile(ptgfile, ...ptg.txt), util.write_pointings after os.path.exists, and the shutil.rmtree calls before each product is written)

overwrite=True replaces the project's files without asking. CASA writes <stem>.ptg.txt through a symbolic link there in two ways: - a pointing file copied from ptgfile replaces the file outside the project that the link points to (shutil.copyfile follows it); - laid-out pointings over a dangling link create the file the link names outside the project. os.path.exists follows the link, finds nothing to remove, and open(..., 'w') follows it.

A link to a table that it replaces stops the task instead, since shutil.rmtree refuses links. Its existence checks follow links, so a dangling link does not count as an existing file under overwrite=False.

casa-rs replaces a link in the project with the new file or table and leaves what the link points to as it was. A link counts as an existing file under overwrite=False, dangling or not. The project's own files are the only ones overwrite replaces (the owner's decision of 2026-10-26, recorded with the provider contracts' overwrite exception).

docs.title: simobserve rounds a direction list of one to its mean
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA artefact; casa-rs simobserve departs (#841 Phase 5c, after the #913 review)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simobserve.py (CASA 6.7.6, dir = direction for a list) and simutil.direction_splitter

CASA passes a direction list to calc_pointings2 as a list, even a list of one. direction_splitter centres a list at its mean, written at precision 5 and read back. So ['J2000 18h00m00.123456789s …'] lays its map out about 1e-5 s of right ascension (0.15 mas) from the same direction given as a string.

casa-rs's simutil tool follows CASA here, since its lists must match CASA's (#913 review). casa-rs's simobserve cannot tell the two apart. The task contract resolves a string to a list of one, as it does for every parameter that takes a string or a list. So simobserve lays a map out at a single direction exactly as given, whether a string or a list of one. A list of several is the pointings themselves, as in CASA. The rounding carries no information, so the exact direction is the better answer.

docs.title: A gain table's solved window records its frequency as its resolution and total bandwidth
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs follows, for CASA's append (#917)
  • Affected code: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc, SolvableVisCal::setCTFrequencies, CASA 6.7.5.18

A G or T table holds one channel per spectral window. For a window a solve reaches, setCTFrequencies writes that channel's frequency and width from FreqMetaData. It then takes const Vector<Double>& chres(chfr); // resolution same as freq and Double totbw=sum(chfr);, so RESOLUTION and TOTAL_BANDWIDTH both hold the frequency. On ngc5921 (gaincal, spw='0') the table's window reads CHAN_FREQ 1413421909.706 Hz, CHAN_WIDTH 1538085.9 Hz, and RESOLUTION and TOTAL_BANDWIDTH 1413421909.706 Hz.

The values are plainly meant to be widths: - the same function sets EFFECTIVE_BW to the width; - the older setOrVerifyCTFrequencies sets resolution, effective bandwidth and total bandwidth to the width; - NewCalTable::setSpwFreqs sets TOTAL_BANDWIDTH to the summed width; - a window no solve reached keeps its summed resolution and the MeasurementSet's total bandwidth (createMemCalTable2).

Nothing in CASA's apply path reads either column, so the error does not change calibrated data. But CASA's gaincal(append=True) merges the new solutions' windows into the table's (NewCalTable::mergeSpwMetaInfo). It requires NUM_CHAN, CHAN_FREQ, CHAN_WIDTH, RESOLUTION, EFFECTIVE_BW, REF_FREQUENCY and TOTAL_BANDWIDTH to equal its own exactly for any window both hold.

A casa-rs table that wrote the widths there was refused ("Error merging spw=0's meta info"). So casa-rs writes the frequency as CASA does: the interoperability contract outranks the correction.

The law casa_appends_to_a_casa_rs_gain_table (casa-calibration slow-tests) appends CASA's solutions to a casa-rs table. With gain_table_windows_match_casa_on_ngc5921 and its two-sideband companion, it asserts that every column of every window row equals CASA's exactly.

docs.title: imregrid refuses a one-channel template in another spectral frame
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#841 Phase 6a)
  • Affected code: CASA 6.7.6's imregrid (casacore ImageRegrid through ImageRegridder)

casacore does not regrid an axis whose input and template both have one pixel. CASA 6.7.6 keeps the input's coordinate for it in the output: a template one channel 3 MHz away, or with its one Stokes plane labelled Q, gives the input's channel and Stokes I (tools/images/image_analysis_oracle.py, cases imregrid_one_channel_moved and imregrid_one_stokes_plane_relabelled). The same template with that one channel in another frame (LSRK to TOPO) stops instead, with "Failed to set conversion layer state".

casa-rs treats that channel as it treats the others: it is not regridded, and the output keeps the input's (casa_images::regrid). Converting the frame of an axis that is never regridded serves no purpose.

docs.title: tsdimaging's theoretical beam models the kernels, not the gridder's
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs does not follow (#938 part 1, #841 Phase 6c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/sdbeamutil.py (TheoreticalBeam.get_kernel and the kernel functions it calls)

tsdimaging gives its image the beam sdbeamutil.TheoreticalBeam computes: the antenna's Gaussian beam convolved with a cut through the gridding kernel and with a box as wide as the sampling, then fitted with a Gaussian. The kernel it convolves with is not the gridder's (SDGrid::init) but a model of it, and the models disagree with the gridder: - GAUSS. The gridder takes gwidth as a half width at half maximum; sdbeamutil passes it to a Gaussian that takes a full width. It also cuts the kernel at 1.5 gwidth where the gridder cuts at truncate (default 3 gwidth). - GJINC. sdbeamutil ignores truncate ("NOT SUPPORTED YET") and always cuts at the jinc's first null. - SF. The gridder's kernel is (1 − ν²) grdsf(ν); sdbeamutil uses SciPy's prolate spheroid pro_ang1(0, 0, c) with c = 5.356π/2, chosen to resemble it. - PB. The gridder takes the telescope's power pattern (for ALMA, the 10.7 m Airy pattern of VPSkyJones); sdbeamutil takes an Airy disk scaled to the Gaussian beam's width, for the antenna's own diameter. - BOX. sdbeamutil makes the box one pixel wide whatever convsupport is; the gridder's box reaches 2s + 1 pixels.

The reported beam is then not the image's. Against CASA 6.7.6 on the oracle's setups (tools/singledish/tsdimaging_oracle.py), the gridder's own kernels give beams wider by 0.60% to 3.3% for GAUSS, and 0.31% narrower for GJINC with a truncate. They differ by at most 6.0e-4 for SF, PB and GJINC at its defaults. The gridder reads its table at the radius truncated to a hundredth of a pixel, which widens the kernel slightly. That accounts for all of GJINC's difference at its defaults (read at the rounded radius, it agrees with CASA to 1e-6) and for about 40% of SF's. The rest of SF's is SciPy's spheroid against grdsf.

casa-rs cuts through the gridder's own table (casa_imaging_singledish:: theoretical_beam_arcsec), so the beam describes the image the gridder makes. BOX at its default support, which both describe alike, agrees with CASA to 2e-8.

The cost falls downstream. simanalyze and simalma grid total power with SF of support 6 and scale its flux by this beam's area. A beam 6e-4 wider is an area about 1.2e-3 larger, so their scaled total-power and feathered products differ from CASA's by about that factor, at the edge of the 1e-3 acceptance. Phases 6g and 6h measure it.

docs.title: getPointingSamplingRaster measures the row spacing in raw longitude
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#938 part 1, #841 Phase 6c)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/synthesis/Utilities/SingleDishBeamUtil.cc (getPointingSamplingRaster)

CASA estimates a raster's sampling from its pointings. Along the scan it scales each longitude step by the cosine of the map's central latitude, so the step is an angle on the sky. Across the scan it projects the steps between rows' median positions on the perpendicular without that factor. A map scanned in latitude, whose rows step in longitude, then has its row spacing overestimated by 1/cos δ, 15% at δ = −30°. The beam tsdimaging reports widens with it.

casa-rs scales the rows' longitude steps as it scales the along-scan ones (casa_imaging_singledish::raster_sampling). A map scanned in longitude, as simobserve scans one, is unaffected: CASA and casa-rs agree on the oracle's maps to 1e-15.

docs.title: tsdimaging writes the weight mask's threshold to six decimal places
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#938 part 1, #841 Phase 6c)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_tsdimaging.py (CASA 6.7.6, do_weight_mask: ia.calcmask("'%s'>%f" % (weightimage, weight_threshold)))

minweight masks the pixels whose weight is at most minweight times the median positive weight. The threshold goes into the mask expression through %f, which keeps six decimal places. A threshold under 5e-7 is written 0, so every pixel with a positive weight stays unmasked, and one of 1.4e-6 is written 0.000001, masking less than asked. Weights have no fixed scale, so a MeasurementSet whose weights are all small loses its minweight mask entirely. casa-rs compares with the threshold itself (casa_imaging_singledish::weight_mask_threshold; tools/singledish/tsdimaging_oracle.py, case sf_small_weights).

docs.title: SDGrid grids nothing with an SF kernel of no support
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA behaviour casa-rs refuses (#938 part 1, #841 Phase 6c)
  • Affected code: casatools/src/code/synthesis/TransformMachines2/SDGrid.cc (SDGrid::init)

SDGrid::init tabulates the SF kernel over convsupport pixels, so convsupport=0 gives a kernel of zeros. Every pixel's weight is then zero, the image is empty, and tsdimaging only warns that no weight is positive. casa-rs refuses that kernel, asking for a support of at least 1 or CASA's default of 3 (casa_imaging_singledish::GridFunction::from_casa).

docs.title: simanalyze writes the fidelity's floor to six decimal places
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 6f)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simanalyze.py (CASA 6.7.6, "max(abs('%s'), %f)" % (difference, maxdiff/pl.sqrt(2.0)))

The fidelity image divides the convolved model by the difference, floored at the difference's median absolute deviation over √2. The floor goes into the image expression through %f, which keeps six decimal places. A floor of 5.19e-7 Jy/beam is written 0.000001, nearly twice its value, and one under 5e-7 is written 0, so a pixel where the difference is zero divides by zero. Simulations of faint sources have differences that small (tools/simulation/simanalyze_analysis_oracle.py, case faint). casa-rs uses the floor itself (casa_simulation::simutil::analysis::fidelity).

docs.title: simanalyze's fidelity image is labelled Jy/beam
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA artefact; casa-rs departs (#841 Phase 6f)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/task_simanalyze.py (CASA 6.7.6, ia.imagecalc(fidelityim, "abs('%s') / '%s'" % (convolved, absdiff)))

The fidelity is the ratio of two images in Jy/beam. CASA's image expression copies its unit from the first image it names, so the fidelity is labelled Jy/beam. casa-rs writes it without a unit.

docs.title: statim scales a Jy/beam image without a beam by the pixel area
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 6f)
  • Affected code: casatasks/src/private/simutil.py (CASA 6.7.6, statim: toJyarcsec=1. when ia.restoringbeam() is empty, then toJypix=toJyarcsec*pixarea)

statim multiplies an image's minimum, maximum and corner rms by a flux-per-pixel factor. For Jy/pixel, and for Jy/beam with a restoring beam, the factor is 1, so the statistics stay in the image's unit. For Jy/beam without a beam it treats the image as Jy per square arcsecond, and the factor becomes the pixel area in square arcseconds: 0.04 for 0.2″ pixels. It still reports the unit as Jy/beam, so the numbers are in no unit at all. Without a beam, Jy/beam cannot be converted to anything. casa-rs reports the image's own values in its own unit (casa_simulation::simutil::analysis::statim; tools/simulation/simanalyze_analysis_oracle.py, image beamless.flat). simanalyze's reported statistics of its image do not meet this case: it reads the image's beam first, and fails without one.

docs.title: Image expressions containing "pa" are labelled as position angles
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-27
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#841 Phase 6f)
  • Affected code: casatools imageanalysis/ImageAnalysis/ImageExprCalculator.tcc (_expr.contains(casacore::Regex("pa\\(*")))

ImageExprCalculator looks for the pa() function with the regular expression pa\(*, which matches "pa" followed by any number of parentheses, so any "pa" at all. An expression whose image paths contain "pa" (a project named pancake, or a path through scratchpad) has its output's unit set to deg and its Stokes axis replaced by Pangle. simanalyze's difference, absolute difference, fidelity and absolute model are all image expressions over <project>/<project>.<configuration>, so a project whose path contains "pa" gets a fidelity labelled deg, and difference and fidelity images whose Stokes plane is a position angle. casa-rs computes those images directly and keeps the Stokes axis.

docs.title: concat leaves a merged SOURCE row's TIME unchanged
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/MSConcat.cc (updateSource: sourceCol.interval().put(j, newTime) before sourceCol.interval().put(j, newInterval))

When two SOURCE rows of one window are equivalent, updateSource keeps the first and widens its validity to span both: it computes the union's centre and length, then writes the centre into INTERVAL and overwrites it with the length. TIME is never written, so the kept row is valid over an interval centred on its old time, which misses the end of the other row's validity. casa-rs centres the record on the union (casa_observation::merge, sources.rs, widen).

docs.title: concat's source equivalence lets its last optional column decide
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/MSConcat.cc (sourceRowsEquivalent)

sourceRowsEquivalent compares the required columns with &&, then tests each optional column present (POSITION, PULSAR_ID, REST_FREQUENCY, SYSVEL, TRANSITION) by assigning its result to areEquivalent, so the last optional column tested decides: two rows with different rest frequencies but equal transitions are equivalent, and their lines are merged into one. casa-rs requires every member to be equal (an optional one stated by both or by neither).

docs.title: concat renumbers merged sources so that one can split and fields dangle
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/MSConcat.cc (updateSource, "renumber consecutively"; copyField, newSourceIndex2_p)

After removing redundant SOURCE rows, updateSource renumbers source IDs row by row: a row whose ID exceeds the count so far gets the next number. A source of several rows (one per window) after a removed ID therefore gets one number for its first row and another for the next, splitting it. The IDs it changes are applied to the fields copyField appends, not to the fields already in the output, which can then name a source ID no row has. casa-rs numbers merged sources in the order they first appear, every record of a source keeping its number, and maps every field (casa_observation::merge, sources.rs, regroup).

docs.title: concat leaves gaps in observation IDs after removing duplicates
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/MSConcat.cc (copyObservation)

copyObservation appends the incoming OBSERVATION rows, removes each row equivalent to an earlier one, and maps it to the last earlier equivalent. It does not shift the IDs of the rows after a removed one, as copyProcessor does with removedSoFar, so an input of several observations can have its rows mapped past the end of the table, or onto another observation, once a duplicate is removed. casa-rs maps each duplicate to its first equivalent and numbers the distinct observations consecutively, for processors and observations alike (casa_observation::merge, distinct).

docs.title: concat drops every state when one input has none
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA behaviour; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSOper/MSConcat.cc (concatenate, "merge STATE")

When one of the two MeasurementSets has no STATE rows, concatenate writes no states at all: it deletes the first MeasurementSet's STATE rows and sets every row's STATE_ID to -1, so the intents of the input that had them are lost. casa-rs keeps them: the rows of an input without states have STATE_ID -1, and the others keep their merged states (casa_observation::merge, states).

docs.title: concat writes into the MeasurementSets it appends
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA behaviour; casa-rs does not follow it (#937 PR B, #939)
  • Affected code: casatools src/tools/ms/ms_cmpt.cc (ms::concatenate, line 6497)

After appending a MeasurementSet, ms::concatenate writes a HISTORY row ("… appended to …", with its parameters) into the appended MeasurementSet, an input, rather than into the output; the inputs' own HISTORY is never copied. A task that reads several MeasurementSets to make another should leave them as they were. casa-rs never writes an input: the output's HISTORY holds what the creating task records of itself (CreationOptions::history), and the inputs' HISTORY is a declared loss.

docs.title: tclean reads a uvtaper with no unit as radians
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs refuses the value (#841 Phase 6b)
  • Affected code: casatools synthesisimager_cmpt.cc (setweighting) and msvis/MSVis/VisImagingWeight.cc (setFilter)

tclean's documentation gives uvtaper=['300.0'] as a taper in wavelengths ("default units are lambda in aperture plane"). setFilter takes the uv-plane path only when the unit contains "lambda", and otherwise treats the value as an image-plane angle, here 300 radians. The filter is then exp(-π²θ²/(4 ln 2) u²), which underflows to zero on every baseline of refim_point.ms. Every imaging weight is zero there, and the image is empty with a beam of 1e-6 arcsec (CASA 6.7.6). A unitless value is always an angle in radians to CASA, never the documented wavelengths. Whether it empties the image depends on the value and the baselines, and a small enough one does not. casa-rs refuses a uvtaper entry without a unit and asks for an angle or for wavelengths (casa_imaging_application::ImagingRequest::uvtaper).

docs.title: tclean corrupts an absolute directory when numbering a restart
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-31
  • Status: CASA bug; owner approved preserving the correct directory (#944). Native restart=False numbering is still unfinished.
  • Affected build/code: CASA 6.7.6.14, casatasks private/imagerhelpers/input_parameters.py, incrementImageNameList.

With existing products and restart=False, CASA finds the next shared numbered image prefix. Its Python helper removes the first two characters of each directory with dirnames[immod][2:], assuming a ./ prefix. For an absolute imagename under /Volumes/, this instead produces olumes/ and fails to create the numbered PSF. Relative prefixes in the same probe correctly produce _2 and _3. The exact build, parameters and failure are recorded on #944 and in the lifecycle receipt linked from the generated compatibility reference. The approved casa-rs target keeps the requested absolute directory; this decision is not evidence that restart is complete.

docs.title: tclean cleans nothing with nsigma, fastnoise=False and no mask
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs cleans the whole image, as CASA does with fastnoise=True (#980)
  • Affected build/code: CASA 6.7.6.14, casatools synthesis/ImagerObjects/SIImageStore.cc (calcRobustRMS) and SynthesisDeconvolver.cc (initMinorCycle, setupMask)

With usemask='user', no mask, nsigma>0 and fastnoise=False, the first initMinorCycle estimates the noise with calcRobustImageStatistics(*residual(), *mask(), ...). mask() creates the .mask image there, filled with zeros. setupMask then finds an existing mask and keeps it ("Initializing to existing mask") instead of setting the whole image to 1, as it does when no mask exists. The run stops at once with the zero-mask stop code 7, an empty .mask and an empty model (CASA 6.7.6.14 on refim_twochan.ms, imsize=100, cell='8.0arcsec', niter=300, nsigma=3). With fastnoise=True the noise estimate never touches mask() and the whole image is cleaned. casa-rs cleans the whole image in both cases: without a mask its noise estimate is Chauvenet's over every valid pixel, as CASA's would be once the full mask existed.

docs.title: A faceted tclean image carries no primary-beam mask
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs masks a faceted residual and restored image where the primary beam is under pblimit, as CASA masks every other image (#980)
  • Affected build/code: CASA 6.7.6.14, casatools synthesis/ImagerObjects/SynthesisNormalizer.cc (divideResidualByWeight) and SIImageStore.cc (divideResidualByWeight, copyMask)

SIImageStore::divideResidualByWeight copies the primary beam's mask0 onto the residual whenever the image has a primary beam and pblimit >= 0 ("A T/F mask in the residual will confuse users"), and restoration copies the residual's mask onto the image. With facets > 1, SynthesisNormalizer::divideResidualByWeight normalizes each facet's sub-image store instead, and copyMask finds no mask0 default mask on a facet's sub-image of the primary beam, so it copies nothing: the published .residual and .image have no mask, although .pb masks the same pixels. On refim_twopoints_twochan.ms (imsize=200, cell='8.0arcsec', facets=2, niter=30, CASA's test_multifield_facets_mfs) CASA's .pb masks 2,471 pixels below pblimit 0.2 and its .image and .residual mask none; casa-rs's .pb, .image and .residual mask those 2,471 pixels, and every pixel value agrees (normalized RMS 8e-7 and 3e-6).

docs.title: tclean seeds a Stokes I image from a Stokes Q start model
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-28
  • Status: CASA behavior retained with a warning (owner decision #980, 2026-10-31; supersedes #970's refusal)
  • Affected code: casatools synthesis/ImagerObjects/SIImageStore.cc (setModelImageOne, regridToModelImage) and casacore images/Images/ImageRegrid.tcc

regridToModelImage regrids a start model on its direction and spectral axes only. ImageRegrid copies the Stokes axis without comparing its coordinate, so a one-plane Stokes Q model seeds the model of a Stokes I run. Its pixels are then predicted, subtracted and restored as Stokes I. casa-rs now matches this positional copy for equal-count Stokes axes and warns when the labels differ (casa_imaging_application's StartModel). The owner requested matching CASA with a warning on 2026-10-31 (#980), replacing the earlier refusal. This is not a physical polarization conversion; published coordinates still describe the requested target image. Unequal-plane-count forms remain unassessed for equivalence.

A degenerate spectral axis is replicated the same way: an MFS start model of one plane seeds the MFS plane at whatever frequency it is stated. That is physically sound for a continuum model, and casa-rs keeps it. A cube's start model must have the cube's spectral axis.

docs.title: flagmanager gives the version a save renames the new comment
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#931, #997 review)
  • Affected code: casatasks private/task_flagmanager.py (mode save, lines 51–83)

Saving a version under a name that already exists first renames the old version to <name>.old.<seconds since 1970>, so both stay restorable. The task then rewrites the old entry of FLAG_VERSION_LIST as tmpname + ' : ' + comment, where comment is the comment of the new save. CASA 6.7.6.14 lists {0: {'name': 'v1.old.1793292269', 'comment': 'second'}, 1: {'name': 'v1', 'comment': 'second'}} after saving v1 with 'first' and then 'second'; the first comment is lost. casa-rs renames the version the same way and keeps its own comment (flagmanager's keep_existing_version).

docs.title: flagdata's summary aborts on a correlation it cannot name
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#931, #997 review)
  • Affected code: casatools flagging/Flagging/FlagMSHandler.cc (open) and FlagDataHandler.cc (generatePolarizationsMap)

With a polarization whose CORR_TYPE is RX, RY, LX and LY (casacore Stokes types 13 to 16), CASA 6.7.6.14's flagdata(mode='summary') warns "Correlation product unknown found: 13" and "The 0 th correlation is unknown: 13", then aborts the Python process with an uncaught std::out_of_range from map::at; there is no summary. casa-rs names every correlation by casacore's Stokes::name, so the summary keys those correlations RX, RY, LX and LY (listobs::stokes_name).

docs.title: A subimage offsets a tabular coordinate's world values instead of moving its table
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-29
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1001, PR #1005 review)
  • Affected code: casacore coordinates/Coordinates/CoordinateSystem.cc (subImageInSitu) and TabularCoordinate.cc (toWorld, setReferencePixel)

A TabularCoordinate with a nonlinear table converts a pixel through its channel corrector first and its linear part (crval, cdelt, crpix) second. subImageInSitu moves a tabular coordinate's reference pixel by the subimage's start, as for a linear axis, but the corrector stays in the input's pixels. A subimage's world values are therefore the input's at the same pixel, offset by cdelt × start, not the input's at the pixel they were cut from. For a table at pixels [0, 1, 3, 4] with world values [10, 11, 15, 22], coordsys.subimage(originshft=[0, 1]) gives world values [13, 14, 16] at pixels 0 to 2, where the input has [11, 13, 15] (CASA 6.7.6). A tabular spectral coordinate is not affected: subImageInSitu rebuilds its table over the subimage's channels. casa-rs moves the table's pixels with the reference pixel (casa_images imsubimage), so a subimage reads the input's world values at the pixels it was cut from. CASA's imsubimage ignores a box on an image without a direction coordinate, the only way casa-rs cuts a tabular coordinate's axis, so no task reaches this in CASA.

docs.title: tb.getcol refuses a column of int64
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casatools src/code/stdcasa/StdCasa/CasacSupport.cc (fromValueHolder)

tb.getcol of a scalar column of Int64 raises RuntimeError: Unknown casa DataType! in CASA 6.7.6.14, while tb.getcell of the same column returns the value as a Python int and getcol of an Int (32-bit) column returns an int64 array. fromValueHolder, which turns the column's ValueHolder into the Python value, has a TpInt64 case for a scalar but none for TpArrayInt64 (the converter for records in the same file has both). The recording is crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_table_tool.json (cells, getcol('id'); the fixture's id column is Int64). casa-rs returns the int64 array, as it does for every other integer column.

docs.title: tb.putkeyword stores an int beyond 32 bits as 0
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casatools ValueHolder conversion for table keywords

tb.putkeyword('name', 2**40) returns True and tb.getkeyword('name') then gives 0, both for a new keyword and for an existing 32-bit Int one (CASA 6.7.6.14; the casa_bugs scenario of crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_table_tool.json). The Python int is narrowed to casacore's 32-bit Int without a range check. casa-rs stores a new keyword whose value does not fit 32 bits as a 64-bit integer, and refuses such a value for an existing 32-bit keyword with RuntimeError: ... does not fit the integer keyword NAME, which holds fewer bits, rather than store a wrong number.

docs.title: tb slices with a wrong rank or a start outside the array abort the process
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casatools table::getcellslice, getcolslice, putcellslice and putcolslice, over casacore's Slicer

In CASA 6.7.6.14 a slice whose blc, trc or incr has the wrong number of elements for the array, or whose blc lies outside the array, throws an ArraySlicerError that nothing catches, and the Python process ends (libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type casacore::ArraySlicerError, exit status 134). The default incr=[1] is such a slice for an array of more than one axis, so tb.getcellslice('DATA', 0, [0, 0], [1, 3]) aborts. casa-rs raises a RuntimeError for each of them and takes a one-element incr as the step of every axis. The recording (crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_table_tool.json, slices and ms_slices) holds only the cases CASA survives. CASA is also inconsistent about trc=-1: getcellslice refuses it ("All elements of trc must be greater than or equal to 0"), getcolslice takes it as the last element; casa-rs follows both.

docs.title: tb.putcell and putcol wrap an int beyond 32 bits in an int cell
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casatools ValueHolder conversion to a column's type

tb.putcell('ANTENNA1', 0, 2147483648) returns True and the cell then holds -2147483648; -2147483649 becomes 2147483647 and 4294967297 becomes 1 (CASA 6.7.6.14; the int_overflow scenario of crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_table_tool.json, which the replay leaves out). putcol wraps the same way. A Python int is narrowed to the 32-bit column type without a range check, as for putkeyword above. casa-rs raises RuntimeError: a value is out of range for a column of Int and leaves the cell, rather than store a wrong number. Astra's review of #1034 noted the departure.

docs.title: tb.putcell with several rows writes those before a missing one
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA behaviour that casa-rs does not follow (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casacore TableProxy::putCell

tb.putcell('id', [0, 3], 22) on a table of three rows writes row 0, then fails on row 3 with no such row: TableProxy::putCell checks and writes one row at a time, so a call that raises has still changed the table (rows_vector scenario). casa-rs checks every row first and raises with the table as it was. The recording follows the failed call with a write that puts row 0 back, so that its later reads agree.

docs.title: tb.addrows with a negative count removes rows
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-31
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1025, the table tool)
  • Affected code: casacore TableProxy::addRow (the count is an Int handed to Table::addRow(rownr_t))

tb.addrows(-1) on a table of three rows returns True and leaves two; addrows(-2) leaves none, and the table reopens with no rows (addrows_negative scenario). The count converts to a huge unsigned number and the table's row count wraps. casa-rs raises RuntimeError ("the number of rows must not be negative") and changes nothing.

docs.title: tb.removerows and tb.addcols do part of a call that fails
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-31
  • Status: CASA behaviour that casa-rs does not follow (#1025, the table tool; Astra's review of #1036)
  • Affected code: casacore BaseTable::removeRow(Vector) and TableProxy::addColumns

tb.removerows([2, 2]) on a table of three rows removes the first row 2, then raises "rownr 2 too high ... (#rows=2)", leaving two rows: the row numbers are taken from the highest down and each is checked against the table as it then is. (A number beyond the table, even among valid ones, fails before any row goes: it is the highest.) tb.addcols of aaa and id on a table that has id adds aaa and then raises "column already exists": addColumns builds the whole description first (a malformed field fails the call with nothing added) and then adds the columns one by one, in the record's sorted order (structure_partial scenario). casa-rs checks the whole call before it changes anything: both raise CASA's message and leave the table as it was. The successful calls, repeats included (removerows([0, 0]) removes two rows), are CASA's.

docs.title: importfits reads every FITS date as UTC
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA bug; casa-rs does not follow it (#1017)
  • Affected code: casacore coordinates/Coordinates/FITSCoordinateUtil.cc (getObsInfo, which reads TIMESYS from the header record, and the WCS date wcslib holds)

exportfits writes an image's observation date in the epoch's own time scale, DATE-OBS with TIMESYS naming the scale (ObsInfo::toFITS). importfits gives the date back with the same calendar value but labelled UTC, whatever TIMESYS says. An image observed at 2020-05-31 12:00 TAI exported by CASA 6.7.6 with TIMESYS = 'TAI' imports at 2020-05-31 12:00 UTC, 37 seconds later. Where the scale is lost was not pinned down: getObsInfo reads TIMESYS from the header record and the date from wcslib's mjdobs, so the scale is gone by then. casa-rs reads MJD-OBS or DATE-OBS in the scale TIMESYS names, UTC when it names none (casa_coordinates::fits::from_fits_header), so the round trip keeps the date.

docs.title: feather fails on an image whose direction is not on its first two axes
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-30
  • Status: CASA limitation; casa-rs does not follow it (#1002, PR #1022 review)
  • Affected code: casatools synthesis/MeasurementEquations/Feather.cc (its FFT, cursor and weight-image paths)

feather finds an image's direction axes for part of its setup, but its lattice cursors and FFTs assume the direction plane is the first two axes. CASA 6.7.6.14's feather of a pair of 16 by 16 pixel images, one Stokes and two channels, with 2″ and 6″ beams, succeeds over [RA, Dec, Stokes, Freq]. The same pair over [Stokes, RA, Dec, Freq] or [Freq, RA, Dec, Stokes], as imtrans makes it, fails with LatticeStepper::setCursorShape: cursorShape <=0 or > latticeShape. casa-rs feathers each direction plane wherever its axes are. The transposed pair's result is the transpose of the direction-first pair's (casa-images casa_axis_maps test feather_takes_the_direction_wherever_its_axes_are), and the direction-first result is checked against CASA's in image_analysis_casa.

docs.title: tb.copyrows adds the rows before it finds a cell it cannot convert, and wraps integers
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-10-31
  • Status: CASA behaviour that casa-rs does not follow (#1025, the table tool; Astra's review of #1039)
  • Affected code: casacore TableCopy::copyRows and ROTableRow/TableRow::put (RecordInterface::as...)

copyRows adds an output row and then puts its cells one by one. When a shared column has a type the input's cell cannot be converted to (a double output column for a dcomplex input, RecordInterface::asDouble - invalid data type; an int output column for a float array input, TableRecordRep::get_pointer - incorrect data type used for field ...), the call raises with the rows already added and their cells never set: reading them gives whatever the heap held (copyrows_types scenario of crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_table_tool.json, which does not compare the table after a refusal). casa-rs checks the types before it changes anything and raises with the output table as it was.

Which conversions CASA accepts was probed pair by pair and is what casa-rs accepts (tools/table/cell_convert.rs), with one exception: an integer that does not fit the output column's type is wrapped as a C cast does (a Short -5 becomes the uChar 251, a uInt 4294967291), the same narrowing as putcell above. casa-rs raises RuntimeError: a value is out of range for a column of ..., before the output is touched, rather than store a wrong number.

docs.title: Later timerange terms take their defaults from row 0
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA quirk casa-rs follows for parity (#980, casa-ms selection::time_expr)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSSel/MSTimeParse.cc (getDefaults)

A timerange time with missing fields (09:00:00, *, 2017/03/01) takes them, and a single time's tolerance and a bracketed range's edge width take the EXPOSURE, from the "first logical row". getDefaults sets firstLogicalRow = 0 and searches for the first logical row only while the static defaultTimeComputed is false, which its first call makes true. Every comma-separated term calls it once, so the first term reads the first logical row and every later term reads row 0. With field='1' on an MS whose FIELD 1 rows start a day after row 0, CASA 6.7.6.14 selects 10:30:00.5 on FIELD 1's day in 10:30:00.5,10:40:00.5 but looks for 10:40:00.5 on row 0's day (fields cases of resources/casa-compat/evidence/msselection-time-casa-20261102.json). casa-rs resolves the terms the same way (TimeSelectorDefaults).

docs.title: The timerange defaults ignore FLAG_ROW when other selections are set
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA quirk casa-rs follows for parity (#980)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSSel/MSTimeParse.cc (getDefaults)

MSSelection builds its time parser with honourRowFlags true. With no other selection expression, the first logical row is the first row whose FLAG_ROW is false. With one, getDefaults tests FLAG_ROW but both branches of the test read the other expressions' condition the same way, so the first logical row is the first row they select, flagged or not. casa-rs follows both (msselection_first_logical_row).

docs.title: A refused bracketed timerange makes later ranges edge-inclusive
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: CASA bug casa-rs does not follow (#980)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MSSel/MSTimeGram.yy (brangetimeexpr)

The grammar keeps a bracketed range's state in the process globals MSTimeEdgeInclusiveRange and MSTimeEdgeBuffer, set when [ (or N[) is read and cleared only when a range completes. A bracketed range that is refused ([09:00:00], 10.25[09:00:00~08:00:00]) leaves them set, so the next unbracketed range anywhere in the process is edge-inclusive with that width until a range completes. In CASA 6.7.6.14, 09:00:00~09:01:00 after 10.25[09:00:00~08:00:00] selects 35 rows of a 2 s MS instead of 30, and 09:00:00.5+00:00:30 after 0.0[09:00:10~09:00:00] loses both end rows (bracket_state_leaks in resources/casa-compat/evidence/msselection-time-casa-20261102.json, whose other cases each run after a completed range clears the state). casa-rs keeps no state between parses.

docs.title: MSIter keeps the previous window's receptor angles for a window without its own FEED row
docs.text:
• Date noted: 2026-11-02
  • Status: casacore behaviour that casa-rs does not follow (MSv2 adapter, Feeds::receptors)
  • Affected code: casacore ms/MeasurementSets/MSIter.cc (setFeedInfo, lines 779-814 on master)

The MeasurementSet definition makes a FEED row with SPECTRAL_WINDOW_ID -1 valid for every spectral window. setFeedInfo instead decides once per table: if every row is -1 it uses them for every window, and otherwise (spwDepFeed_p) it copies into its cache only the rows whose window is the iterator's current one.
