  2. Keep independent command-line and Python parameter definitions, or let each consumer define its own bundle shape.
  3. Use unversioned TOML maps without catalog identities or explicit migrations.
  4. Keep every historical migration and alias on every surface, including those that declare themselves current-only.
  5. Load stale profiles silently against current defaults, which changes meaning while looking valid.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: catalog completeness, contract invariants (including the homonym review and the refusal of aliases on a surface with no migrations), sparse TOML round trips, migrations, managed-store lifecycle and cross-surface resolution parity in casa-provider-contracts and casa-task-runtime; the Python package's parameter and binding tests - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-parameter-surface-catalog.py; consumers may project provider definitions but add no authoritative default or alias - CI checks: just arch-check, whose scripts/check-parameter-contract-history.py keeps semantic fingerprints append-only (a changed concept revision or surface contract cannot replace an existing (id, version) entry), and just docs-check, which checks the generated parameter reference - review trigger: changes to catalog concepts, public bindings, defaults, migrations, persistence behaviour or the parameter document format - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - the same canonical parameter name acquires different value semantics on two surfaces - a command-line parser or Python wrapper supplies a default not present in the provider definition, or hand-defines schema that does not round-trip through the bundle - a parameter file contains current default values after canonical save - task aliases share Last state only because they use the same executable - a current-only surface publishes an alias or migration, or accepts a stale contract - a shipped profile does not name its surface's current contract - run state, plans, caches or resource inventory enter a human profile - an explicit source profile changes without an explicit save action

docs.title: ADR-0008: Casacore storage and bounded MeasurementSet writes
docs.text:
Status: accepted

Date: 2026-07-18

Reaffirmed: 2026-08-26

Amended: 2026-10-09, on owner direction: casa-rs writes nothing into a MeasurementSet that CASA does not write.

Amended: 2026-10-10, on owner direction: in-place mutation waits for a table lock another process holds, as casacore does, instead of being refused at once.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
CASA interoperability depends on the casacore table data model and persisted data-manager metadata, not on a casa-rs-specific row layout. MeasurementSets may be created by CASA with different valid storage-manager bindings, tile shapes, hypercube layouts, and variable array shapes. At the same time, production writers must not materialize a large MAIN table or retain payloads proportional to its row count.

Earlier design discussion considered rollback or snapshot machinery for large writes. No product requirement currently calls for transactional rollback, historical generations, or user-visible snapshots, and those mechanisms would add persistent state and recovery complexity to the interoperability boundary.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Table row, column, and cell accessors remain the primary public table-data interface. A column's storage manager is a strategic creation-time choice. Opening an existing table reads its persisted data-manager sequence, type, columns, properties, and tile or hypercube metadata; mutation preserves those bindings rather than replacing them with casa-rs conventions.

casa-tables natively reads the supported standard casacore managers and writes their canonical formats. A manager implemented only by an external casacore plugin may be reported as unsupported. TiledShapeStMan uses one hypercube for each distinct cell shape, and rows with the same shape reuse that hypercube. Unused planned shapes do not create payload files or row maps.

MAIN-table producers use one MeasurementSetWritePlan and one MeasurementSetWriteSession. The immutable plan names every owned scalar and array column, derives tile geometry from the existing storage planner, fixes batch and queue sizes, reserves every scalar and array writer buffer, and reports the maximum modeled writer-owned resident bytes. The session streams typed cells, installs the planned columns, and reports rows, bytes, producer time, bounded-queue wait, assembly, physical-write, and finalization time.

Creation uses a sibling staging directory and publishes it only after a complete interoperable table has been written. In-place mutation holds casacore's table write lock from its first change until it completes or is abandoned, as CASA does. When another process holds a lock on the table, in-place mutation waits for it, as casacore does by default: the waiter adds its process id to the request list in table.lock, so that a holder using casacore's AutoLocking releases its lock at its next inspection, and the wait is logged when it starts, periodically while it lasts, and when it ends. casacore throttles those inspections, so a holder that uses the table only lightly may keep its lock until it closes the table. The wait blocks in the kernel, as casacore's does, so the kernel refuses a wait that would deadlock, such as the second of two processes upgrading their read locks, and that writer fails. A writer whose table was opened without locking and that finds another process wrote the table while it waited is refused, because what it read beforehand is stale. A save that locks several tables of a MeasurementSet never waits while it holds another table's lock, and is refused before writing when another process wrote a table it released to wait. A released write lock publishes the table as persisted (rows, columns and one change counter per data manager, read from table.dat). An in-place writer publishes every table it started to write, so a write interrupted part way is announced; a locked table handle publishes when it wrote the table under its write lock, even if it reloaded the table afterwards, and publishes nothing when nothing reached the disk, as casacore's PlainTable::putFile announces each write it makes. A conflicting handle in the same process is refused at once, because it may belong to the waiting thread. casa-rs does not yet release a lock it holds when another process requests it (#694); a waiter, CASA's or casa-rs's, waits until a casa-rs holder, such as an imaging run with its retained read locks, finishes. On a file system without lock support (fcntl refused with ENOLCK, or ENOTSUP as on macOS SMB mounts) the table is used unlocked, with a warning, as casacore does for ENOLCK; there is then no cross-process exclusion. casa-rs adds nothing of its own to a MeasurementSet: no table keywords, marker files, generations or identities. An interrupted in-place write may leave cells partly written, as an interrupted CASA write does; rerunning the producing task recomputes them.

The persistence layer does not provide rollback, snapshot generations, journaling, or copy-on-write recovery. Such a feature requires a new concrete product requirement and a separate architecture decision.

This applies explicitly to imaging MODEL_DATA and CORRECTED_DATA. Prediction writes selected cells in place under the exact source-scoped table lock. The writer retains at most one array cell, persists that cell through the selected-row/selected-column table seam, and discards its cache entry before accepting another row; it does not materialize MAIN rows or the full column. Unrelated MeasurementSets may therefore progress concurrently while two live writers for the same source remain mutually exclusive. Successful completion flushes the column and releases the lock. An interrupted write may leave partial derived values, which the next run recomputes. Full-column staging copies, backup columns, content digests, and rollback are prohibited unless a later concrete requirement demonstrates that CASA-compatible in-place behavior is inadequate and separately accounts for the I/O and storage cost.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• CASA-generated MeasurementSets need not follow casa-rs creation conventions to be readable or safely mutated.
  • Memory use is planned from the real column shapes and writer buffers rather than a fixed row-count heuristic.
  • New-output failure is isolated before publication. In-place failure may have written some cells, as in CASA; rerunning the task recomputes them.
  • A MeasurementSet written by casa-rs carries only what CASA would write, so CASA and casa-rs can each open the other's output without preparation.
  • Flag-version tables remain an explicit domain feature of flagmanager; they are not a transaction or rollback mechanism for general table writes.
  • Storage changes require Rust-read/Rust-write and C++-read/C++-write interoperability evidence, including heterogeneous TiledShapeStMan data when that path changes.

docs.title: ADR-0009: Mathematical imaging architecture
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-08-18 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by: ADR-0016, in part (the migration rules and the attestation and identity wording, since removed from this record)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Imaging behavior was distributed across application dispatch, mode-specific preparation, imaging modules, solver controllers, and product writers. Continuum, spectral-line, mosaic, W/AW-projection, MT-MFS, CPU, and Metal paths repeated or reinterpreted scientific choices. Geometry, measurement-equation terms, weighting, normalization and products had no enforceable dependency boundaries. A new vocabulary alone would permit the same architecture to reappear behind new names.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: CASA-RS imaging follows one normative mathematical and ownership architecture.

docs.title: Ownership and dependency direction
docs.text:
Application and frontend layers may version-migrate and validate request syntax, select a Resource Policy, invoke compile and run, and present results. They do not query devices, evaluate scientific capability/backend eligibility, select gridders or solvers, construct science caches, allocate imaging work buffers, or define or write scientific products.

Scientific definitions depend on no frontend, execution backend, or device API. Observation and MeasurementSet interoperability are isolated behind observation interfaces. Reconstruction depends on Measurement Operator and Normal State contracts rather than casacore or concrete backends. Product semantics depend on scientific state rather than solvers or execution implementations. Backends implement declarative work and operator interfaces and do not own modes, coordinates, weighting, normalization, or products.

There is one production engine behind the application-owned typed installed-implementation availability boundary. casa-imaging-application checks compiled and task-only requirements against the implementation installed in the build before any work. Capabilities whose owners have not landed are returned typed unavailable rather than delegated to an alternate implementation. CI enforces the permitted crate graph and rejects forbidden edges (ADR-0016).

docs.title: Compile, plan, and run boundary
docs.text:
compile(request) produces an immutable Compiled Problem containing logical science, an Observation Snapshot (a manifest of the selection; bulk samples remain bounded streams), required capabilities, coordinate and reconstruction contracts, measurement-equation and weighting contracts, a Numerics Contract, and a Product Contract. It contains no backend-specific prepared operator or resource allocation.

Planning binds the compiled problem to a backend and a Resource Policy; each phase is admitted against the host before it runs (ADR-0016 decision 4).

run executes only what was compiled and admitted. It does not silently recompile, perform capability routing, choose an unlisted backend, or fall back to another implementation.

docs.title: Measurement equation and weighting
docs.text:
Let X be the declared model-coefficient space and D the selected unweighted visibility-sample space. The complete logical measurement operator is A: X -> D. A* is its adjoint under explicitly declared inner products. W is the positive-semidefinite data metric containing flags, input weights, tapering, and globally derived uniform or Briggs density weights.

The authoritative normal right-hand side is b = A* W d. For model x, the authoritative normal residual is g(x) = A* W (d - A x), and the logical normal operator is H = A* W A.

Any phase transformation, spectral sampling, polarization or Mueller mapping, channel integration, or direction-dependent response that affects both prediction and imaging belongs to a paired operator or explicitly paired composition. Data-only interpolation may not bypass the adjoint contract.

Published normalization, PB correction, sensitivity division, residual scaling, restoring-beam convolution, blanking, and unit conversion belong to the Product Contract and its normalization rules. They are not silently folded into a backend adjoint.

docs.title: Geometry and polarization
docs.text:
Compiled Geometry owns coordinate frames, image-domain charts, requested output coordinates, user-visible facet and outlier definitions, and deterministic transform specifications. It does not own sample-sized UVW, frequency, phase, or pointing arrays. Selected Observation streams evaluate per-sample coordinates from the compiled specifications.

Facet batching, tiling, halo sizing, and device partitioning are execution. W-, AW-, and facet convolution kernels are Measurement Operator implementations. Requested polarization coordinates belong to reconstruction; feed/correlation basis, parallactic-angle behavior, and Mueller response belong to the measurement equation and instrument response.

docs.title: Spectral semantics
docs.text:
Continuum and line share reconstruction, Measurement Operator, Normal State, product, and execution interfaces. Four distinct contracts define spectral behavior:

  • Spectral Coordinate Law defines native/output frames, rest frequency, velocity convention, epoch/direction/ephemeris dependencies, channel boundaries, and output WCS.
  • Spectral Sampling Operator defines paired channel integration or interpolation, coverage, flag/weight propagation, edge behavior, and the declared treatment of induced inter-channel covariance.
  • Reconstruction Basis defines constant, Taylor, channel-local, or other model coefficient functions.
  • Spectral Coupling Policy defines whether channels or basis blocks are independent, sequentially transformed, jointly reconstructed, regularized, or coupled through shared products such as a common restoring beam.

A cube uses a channel-local Reconstruction Basis but is not defined by that basis and is not an application loop around a continuum imager. Sequential continuum fitting/subtraction is an explicit visibility transform with fit channels, weights, model, provenance, and output-weight semantics (ADR-0011). Joint continuum-plus-line reconstruction is a different capability requiring a block normal operator with continuum-line cross terms and a separately accepted scientific decision.

docs.title: Side effects
docs.text: Read and write sets are explicit. Scientific products publish after the final complete-data reconciliation. Optional MODEL_DATA follows ADR-0008: the final pass predicts from the final model and writes the selected cells in place under casacore's table lock. Interruption may leave partial derived values, as in CASA; the next run recomputes them. Imaging adds no staging column, backup generation, content digest, or rollback mechanism beyond CASA-compatible table behavior.

docs.title: Major and Minor Cycles
docs.text:
A Major Cycle performs complete-data reconciliation over every selected sample using the logical operator and one frozen weighting generation. Complete-data excludes Minor Cycle approximations but does not imply bitwise identity, full materialization, one resident grid, or a shift-invariant PSF.

A Normal State Generation comprises the model generation, weighting generation, normal right-hand side, normal-operator or PSF approximation, sensitivity and sum-weight state, valid support, and Numerics Contract. It may be partitioned, streamed, tiled, sparse, or operator-backed.

A Minor Cycle consumes an immutable Minor Cycle View recording the approximation, valid domain, error or staleness bound, cycle threshold, and maximum admissible update. It returns a Model Delta and Solver Evidence and stops before violating that envelope. A final Major Cycle is mandatory before restoration and publication.

docs.title: Products
docs.text: A Product Contract and Product Graph own required/optional products, authoritative source generations, WCS and axes, units and normalization, per-plane/common-beam policy, residual scaling and restoration, PB/sensitivity correction, blanking and validity, cross-product dependencies, output schema, and the atomic replacement of each product. Backends may provide primitive transforms but may not define the meaning of image, residual, PSF, alpha, beam, mask, sensitivity, or PB-corrected products. Generation needs no content hashing or full-array reread to authorize publication (ADR-0014).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - code and verification follow the normal-equation and cycle mathematics - geometry, spectral sampling, reconstruction, normalization, and execution have distinct enforceable owners - continuum and line share infrastructure without claiming false semantic equivalence - each product is replaced atomically; MeasurementSet side effects follow CASA (ADR-0008)

Negative: - every solver and backend must satisfy explicit science and product contracts

Neutral / tradeoffs: - exact CLEAN component order and bitwise pixels are not preserved; agreement is judged by normalized tolerance

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Preserve mode-oriented runners and share utilities.
  2. Translate LibRA/CASA C++ class and inheritance families directly.
  3. Build one broad imaging-run object owning science, resources, solvers, and products.
  4. Treat continuum, line, mosaic, and projections as independent top-level modes.
  5. Let a channel-local basis alone define spectral-line semantics.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: the T0 laws (weighted adjoint, linearity, spectral identity and nonidentity, cycle invariants) and T1 end-to-end tests of TESTING.md "Imaging tiers and evidence" - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py rejects forbidden frontend, backend, observation, reconstruction, and product dependencies (ADR-0016) - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: stop before adding a second public run interface, an alternate stage path, backend-owned science/product semantics, or unpaired sampling - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a frontend or backend evaluates a science mode or writes a scientific product - Geometry owns sample-sized arrays or execution tiling - spectral interpolation is not represented in prediction and adjoint paths - a Minor Cycle mutates authoritative residual state or exceeds its view envelope - a capability can silently retry through another implementation - a solver or backend defines normalization, restoration, or output semantics

docs.title: ADR-0011: Continuum-line coupling
docs.text:
Status: retired Date: 2026-08-31 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by: ADR-0016 decision 11

ADR-0016 decision 11 removed the joint continuum-plus-line solver this ADR introduced; only the sequential continuum transform below still applies, and git history keeps the original text (#531).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: CASA's uvcontsub fits and subtracts the continuum in the visibility domain before line imaging (casatasks/src/private/task_uvcontsub.py, casatools/src/code/mstransform/TVI/UVContSubTVI.cc). casa-rs ports that transform. This ADR also accepted a joint continuum-plus-line reconstruction, which no longer exists in the code.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The sequential continuum transform is CASA's visibility-domain fit and subtraction, composed before independent channel-local line imaging. It fits each row and correlation over the fit channels with CASA's min/max frequency basis, subtracts the fit on the application channels, keeps the input flags and weights, and claims no propagated fit covariance. It is a visibility transform, not a joint reconstruction, and is never described as one. It lives in casa-imaging-operator (fit_and_subtract_continuum).

A joint continuum-plus-line solver would be a new capability with its own scientific contract and a new ADR (ADR-0016 decision 11).

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: continuum_transform_* and t46_sequential_uvcontsub_anchor_v1_matches_frozen_casa_row (a frozen CASA UVContSubTVI row) in crates/casa-imaging-operator/tests/continuum.rs - none / guidance only: retired; kept as the record of the sequential transform

docs.title: ADR-0014: Identity is ownership, without content attestation
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-09-18 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by:

Amended: 2026-10-03, on owner direction: private same-run spill keeps no checksums, and ownership-only association extends to imaging inputs, replay and reprojection targets (this replaced the spill exemption of 2026-09-18). 2026-10-09, on owner direction: nothing of casa-rs's is stored in the MeasurementSet (ADR-0008). 2026-11-02, on owner approval: the 2026-10-03 decision, recorded separately until then, is merged here.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Imaging once hashed product content and reread complete arrays to authorize publication, kept SHA-256 or CRC framing on private same-run spill, and minted content identities for models, plans and normal state. None of it had an independent trust boundary: the generator and its writer, and a spill file's writer and reader, are the same trusted process. A fresh digest with no independently trusted expected value detects no corruption; it only gives corrupted bytes a different identity. The mechanism cost initial hashes, repeated verification, private backing arrays, copies and staged records on the timed path.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Identity is ownership.

  1. No content attestation. Production code computes no SHA-256, CRC or other digest over scientific arrays (visibilities, models, weights, reprojection targets, replay contributions), compiled problems, plans, run summaries or spill to mint, verify or authorize an identity, and makes no verification-only pass over full arrays. There is no optional mode, renamed substitute, memoized seal or compatibility checksum. Already available metadata is compared directly, not serialized and hashed.
  2. Ownership. Trusted data within one process is associated by ownership, compiled selection and shape, row and channel order, actual completion counts and live lifecycle checks. A live owner token is not a content fingerprint and is not a portable identity for another run. Values and support are validated where they enter or change; continuing, preparing a delta or completing does not rehash or reread an unchanged model.
  3. Nothing in the MeasurementSet. Holding the open MeasurementSet is the ownership. casa-rs stores no keywords, generations, identities or marker files in it (ADR-0008).
  4. Run-local spill. Private same-run spill is part of the bounded buffer system, not a trust boundary. It keeps versioned framing, exact lengths and offsets, frame order and counts, shape and inventory, source association, file identity, truncation and EOF checks and ordinary I/O error propagation, and no payload or header checksums.
  5. Products. Generation writes bounded owned windows directly into the CASA-compatible writer's private staging images. It keeps the member inventory and shape, ordered complete window coverage, metadata, WCS, masks and beams, fallible writes and flushes, resource admission and the atomic replacement of each image. If publication fails the run fails and its output set is incomplete; rerunning is required. There is no resumable member ledger, partial-publication recovery or rollback, the set is not an atomic transaction, and a failed set is never reported as a success.
  6. Bounded telemetry. Progress stays in memory and is O(1) per phase; nothing serializes, hashes or walks whole plans, models or history. A run leaves one final success or failure summary.

Unchanged: CASA-compatible formats and the integrity their formats define; checksums that external formats or imported artifacts carry; scientific algorithms, flags, masks, WCS, beams and numerical acceptance; bounded memory. Diagnostic fingerprints are allowed in explicitly invoked tests and benchmarks and never add work to production execution.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - no hashing, rereads, backing copies or verification phases on the timed path - one notion of identity across products, models, plans and spill

Negative: - an equal-length corruption of private spill is not detected by a checksum; scientific value checks still apply where data is consumed - a failed publication leaves an incomplete output set to regenerate

Neutral / tradeoffs: - no bitwise floating-point output requirement may justify extra production buffers, passes or arithmetic beyond scientific acceptance

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep product attestation as an optional mode. Rejected: it keeps the mechanism and its cost under another name.
  2. Keep CRCs on private spill. Rejected: the writer and reader are one trusted process, and framing checks catch truncation and misordering.
  3. Make the output set an atomic transaction with member recovery. Rejected on owner direction: rerunning the task is the recovery.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: product publication tests of write-only bounded ownership, complete ordered coverage, unchanged science and metadata and real I/O failures (TESTING.md); count, order, source and lifecycle checks on owned data - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py refuses content hashing in the imaging and simulation crates (no-content-hashing-in-imaging-crates); imaging code rule 4 in ARCHITECTURE.md - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: reintroducing production attestation, a verification-only full-array pass or a telemetry exception needs a new ADR and the owner's approval, with a concrete failure model and measured CPU, memory, I/O and end-to-end cost; a ban on the word "seal" is not a sufficient check - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a hash, CRC or digest is computed over scientific data, a plan or spill in production code, under any name - a phase rereads a complete product or model only to authorize it - progress reporting serializes or scans whole plans, models or history - casa-rs writes anything into a MeasurementSet that CASA would not - a failed publication is reported as a success or partly recovered

docs.title: ADR-0016: Imaging foundation
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-07 Truth class: normative Supersedes: the unified imaging resource authority ADR of 2026-08-18 (deleted 2026-11-02; git history keeps it); the "Migration" section and the attestation wording of ADR-0009; the joint continuum-plus-line decision of ADR-0011 Superseded by:

Amended: 2026-10-25, on owner direction: every imaging crate may depend on the definitional crates (decision 10). 2026-10-28, on owner approval: the model may also depend on casa-observation (decision 10; imaging port decision 1,

Amended: 2026-10-28, on owner direction of 2026-10-27 (#938): single-dish image-plane gridding is its own operator family (decision 13).

Amended: 2026-11-02, on owner approval: the foundation plan this ADR cited was deleted; its references now point to ARCHITECTURE.md, TESTING.md or git history, and the ticket and review-gate process (decision 12) is reduced to what still holds.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Programme #486 delivered cube, MFS, Clark, multi-worker and Metal imaging as several parallel routes: four CPU gridding drivers, two Metal drivers, closed enums selecting gridders, a 20k-line replay cache standing in for re-reading the MeasurementSet, and a runtime whose receipts, execution DAG, resource topology and identity hashing were almost entirely write-only. W-projection, AW-projection and mosaic could not reach the fast cube path or Metal. The programme's own process machinery (a migration matrix, a 3,578-line checker hashing Rust function bodies, per-ticket contract revisions) would resist any consolidation. The owner reviewed this state on 2026-10-07 and approved the imaging foundation plan, which git keeps at 0b470017:docs/imaging-architecture/imaging-foundation-plan-20261007.md.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
CASA-RS imaging is one measurement operator, one major-cycle pass, one deconvolution driver and one execution model. This ADR records the binding decisions. The plan's review rules (its section 10) are the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md, and its test tiers (section 7) are TESTING.md "Imaging tiers and evidence"; the rest of the plan is the design as landed, kept in git at the location above as a record, not a binding document.

  1. One operator. casa-imaging-operator owns Placement/SampleBlock records, a ConvolutionFunctionSet trait with exactly four implementations (standard spheroidal, W-planes, AW catalog, mosaic PB), a GridBackend trait with exactly two implementations (CPU, Metal), GridAccumulator, MeasurementOperator and WeightingGeneration. Standard, W, AW, mosaic, MT-MFS, cube and MFS imaging are parameterisations of these types. Paired forward/adjoint choices (kernel set, conjugation, Mueller routing, phase gradient, phase-centre phasor, channel and polarisation maps, Taylor factors) live in the operator's kernel contract: the Placement, SampleBlock and GridBackend rustdoc (the plan's section 5.3 records the design as landed).
  2. One pass. Every major cycle re-traverses the selected MeasurementSet through MajorCyclePass and grids residual samples. No replay cache of visibility-independent factors is retained; a bounded tap-plan cache may be added later only as a measured execution strategy over the same operator.
  3. One driver. casa-imaging-deconvolution owns the minor-cycle driver, the controller (thresholds, cycleniter, convergence and divergence rules) and a Solver trait with Hogbom, Clark, multiscale and Taylor implementations.
  4. Runtime core. Resource handling is HostResources, a ResourcePolicy, one admit() per phase returning an RAII reservation, a sequential phase list with a cancel token, the Metal execution state and the bounded worker team. There are no execution receipts, execution DAG, lease epochs, logical/physical slot ledgers, cost-model profiles, adaptation transitions or plan identities. The only runtime record is an O(1)-per-phase run summary. The earlier unified resource authority is superseded in full.
  5. No identity hashing. Compiled problems, plans, products and selections are compared directly or by ownership. No identity is persisted; an AW convolution-function cache is reused by its cell layout (decision 7). ADR-0014 (identity is ownership) remains in force and covers plans and run summaries. Nothing of casa-rs's is persisted in a MeasurementSet: no keywords, generations, identities or marker files. Imaging opens a MeasurementSet as CASA writes it (owner direction 2026-10-09, which amends ADR-0008).
  6. Grid precision. Metal accumulates in f32; CPU defaults to f64 and offers f32 as a user-selectable request field. Acceptance is the 1e-3 normalised tolerance of the owner's 2026-09-24 direction, not bitwise agreement.
  7. AW cache. CASA CF images are read directly (headers at open, cells on demand into a bounded in-memory LRU). Native EVLA generation writes CASA-format CF images. There is no private content-addressed store, manifest, payload hash or eviction ledger.
  8. Request layer. One ImagingRequest struct defaulted and validated from the provider-contracts catalog; one CompiledProblem; one availability gate. Capabilities that are rejected are not in the catalog.
  9. Diagnostics. Library crates read no environment variables and emit no eprintln!; diagnostic switches are request fields; emission is tracing.
  10. Crates. casa-imaging-model, casa-imaging-operator, casa-imaging-deconvolution, casa-imaging-products, casa-imaging-runtime, casa-imaging-metal (macOS), and casa-imaging-application. casa-imaging-reconstruction is deleted when empty. Dependency direction is enforced by scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py over cargo metadata. Every crate the policy covers, the model included, may depend on the definitional crates: crates that define values, units, quanta, measures and coordinate systems and the pure functions on them, do no file, network, process or environment I/O, start no threads, use no device, and depend on no workspace crate but one another. They are casa-values, casa-types and casa-coordinates; beyond them the model depends only on casa-observation, the observation boundary, whose catalogue, batches and pointing samples its batch geometry reads (amended 2026-10-28 on owner approval; imaging port decision 1 of 2026-10-27, #932). The policy names the definitional crates and lists each crate's other workspace dependencies exactly. Adding a crate to the definitional set widens what every layer may use, so it is the owner's decision, recorded on its pull request; the checks above then apply to it. (Amended 2026-10-25 on owner direction: with no workspace dependencies at all, the model could not share the workspace's correlation, measure and coordinate vocabulary and kept private copies of it, such as CorrelationType, DirectionFrame, FrequencyFrame and Epoch.)
  11. Joint continuum-plus-line reconstruction is removed from the code. ADR-0011's sequential continuum subtraction remains; its joint-basis decision is superseded and may be re-proposed as a separate ADR with its own scientific contract.
  12. Process. The migration matrix, contract revisions, evidence registries and programme-specific closure rules are retired and are not restored. Every imaging change is held to the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md; reviews follow AGENTS.md "Review".
  13. Single-dish gridding. Single-dish (total-power) imaging, CASA's SDGrid, places each spectrum at its pointing's pixel and spreads it with a radial kernel: no FFT, no uv coordinates and no gridding correction. It is its own operator family, outside decision 1's measurement operator and its four kernel sets. casa-imaging-singledish joins decision 10's crates in the execution layer. It owns the single-dish kernels, the image-plane gridder and the degridder that the simulator's total-power prediction uses, its adjoint. It admits its grids through the runtime and grids on its worker team. (Amended 2026-10-28, on owner direction of 2026-10-27, #938.)

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - One place for each scientific choice; W, AW and mosaic reach every backend and the cube streaming path. - About 130k lines of parallel routes and write-only bookkeeping removed; target under 70k non-test imaging lines. - Tests become laws and tolerances rather than fixture expectations.

Negative: - Later major cycles re-read the MeasurementSet; the performance pass must show this is within the measured checkpoints or add a bounded cache. - Execution receipts are gone; the run summary is the one run record.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - Metal f32 accumulation differs from CPU f64 within tolerance; this is a precision choice, not a correctness gap.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep the replay cache as the default residual path. Rejected: it is not scientifically required, its scratch footprint exceeds the input, and it duplicates the operator in a second record-based implementation.
  2. Keep the earlier resource authority and trim it. Rejected: its admission decisions reduce to one arithmetic formula, and every other structure was write-only.
  3. Keep the architecture checker and update its ratchets per commit. Rejected: it enforced programme process, not architecture.
  4. (Amendment of 2026-10-25.) Keep the model free of workspace dependencies and convert between vocabularies at the application, or admit each definitional dependency into each crate's exact set. Rejected: the first keeps two types for one meaning; the second makes every use of a unit or measure a policy edit while guarding nothing, since a definitional crate brings in no persistence, I/O or device. casa-numerics and casa-fft are algorithms rather than definitions and stay listed where used.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: T0 operator laws and T1 end-to-end capability tests (TESTING.md "Imaging tiers and evidence") - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py (crate edges, definitional crates closed and free of I/O, device APIs only in casa-imaging-metal, no std::env or eprintln! in library crates, no content hashing in imaging crates) - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md for every imaging change; adding a definitional crate (decision 10) is the owner's decision

docs.title: ADR-0017: Python and headless task providers are the product surface
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: the native macOS GUI prototype and the scientific notebooks and assistant ADRs (both deleted 2026-11-02; git history keeps them); the stateful-session provider and session-surface parts of ADR-0006 and of the provider schema bundle ADR, whose surviving rule ADR-0006 now holds Superseded by:

Amended: 2026-10-27, on owner direction (#931): Python binds Rust through PyO3 only (item 4, Enforcement and Drift detection). This was the first stage of #931. Amended: 2026-10-28, on owner direction (#931 PR 3): the casars launcher is retired and Python starts each task's executable directly (items 1 and 4, Enforcement and Drift detection, in their final wording).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
From May to October 2026 casa-rs carried several interactive surfaces beside its Python package and command-line tasks: a ratatui terminal launcher with image and table browsers (casars), a native macOS SwiftUI workbench (apps/casars-mac), a scientific-notebook and AI-assistant program (casa-notebook), JSONL browser-session providers (imexplore --session, tablebrowser) with their own parameter surfaces, and Rust-side plot rasterisation (PNG/PDF through plotters, image and printpdf). The experiments showed that one computational codebase and one task/parameter contract can serve several frontends, but each frontend added code, tests, CI time (a macOS GUI gate on every pull request) and support crates that competed with the scientific work.

The project's direction is a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces (casatasks-style task calls and ia/tb-style tools) so casa-rs can replace CASA in existing scripts. Interactive inspection and plotting are better served by Python tools (NumPy, Matplotlib, Jupyter) than by project-owned GUIs.

The last state of the interactive surfaces is preserved at the tag ui-experiments-2026-10-20 (commit 42ba2012); the GUI and the notebook program each had an ADR, which git history keeps.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. The product surfaces are the Python package (casars) and the task executables listed in the application catalog.
  2. casa-rs has no terminal UI, native GUI, notebook or assistant program, interactive browser sessions, or Rust-side plot rasterisation. Every parameter surface is a one-shot task; SurfaceKind and SurfaceDefinition keep a single task variant so the serialized contracts keep their shape.
  3. Plots are typed data. Rust builds plot documents and text point manifests (msexplore/plotms --plot-format txt); Python renders them with Matplotlib (casars.data.plot_matplotlib, casars.imexplore).
  4. The Python package binds in-process Rust functionality through PyO3 in casars._core. Task calls start the catalog-selected task-provider executable directly as a child process; a provider may host a task family. Python and the executable use the shared task front end in casa-task-runtime. Ordinary Python task calls neither load nor save managed Last state; command-line lifecycle policy is explicit. There is no separate casars launcher or UniFFI layer.
  5. New interactive surfaces, if ever wanted again, start from a new ADR rather than from the retired code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - The workspace loses the terminal, GUI, notebook, browser-protocol and rasterisation crates and dependencies (ratatui*, crossterm, plotters, image, printpdf, rusqlite, UniFFI Swift bindings and others). - CI no longer needs a macOS GUI job; the required checks are lint_test, python_package and docs. - Contract and runtime code no longer carries session-only branches.

Negative: - There is no point-and-click inspection; users inspect data from Python. - msexplore/plotms no longer write PNG or PDF files.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - Catalog presentation fields (show_in_tui, show_in_swift, shell_kind, interaction) and the provider CLI parser schema (casa_ms::presentation::UiCommandSchema) remain until the CASA-shaped Python work reshapes them.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep the Swift GUI as the primary surface: rejected; Python reaches the intended users and existing CASA scripts directly.
  2. Keep the TUI as a lightweight viewer: rejected; it duplicated the GUI's browsing model and carried terminal-graphics dependencies for little gain.
  3. Keep the code dormant behind feature flags: rejected; dormant code still costs build time, review and maintenance, and the tag preserves it.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: - the Python package tests: test_task_runner.py (a task call starts the executable its catalog override names with --json-run -, streams its log, and leaves Last untouched on success, failure and interruption) and test_task_end_to_end.py (a real executable, found in a development checkout's build); - scripts/test-task-cli-hosts.py (every catalog executable is on the shared task front end and answers its machine actions); - the command line's Last lifecycle and its equivalence with --json-run: the front end's tests in casa-task-runtime, crates/casars-imexplore/tests/imexplore_cli.rs and the imager's t1::routes; - the provider-contract and catalog tests (26 task surfaces, every application a task, no launcher, no session kinds), and the resolver's tests in casa-provider-contracts; - lint/import/dependency rules: none beyond the workspace manifests; - CI checks: just quick, scripts/test-python-package.sh in the python_package job (its binding snapshots pin what the binding returns to Python, and it tests the built wheel and sdist), the suite_install job (scripts/test-install-suite.sh --hide-checkout: the installed suite's commands and Python, with the checkout moved aside), just docs-check; - review trigger: any pull request that adds a UI, rendering or session dependency or crate.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
Suspect drift if: - Cargo.lock gains ratatui, crossterm, plotters, image, printpdf or uniffi; - a parameter surface or provider declares a non-task kind; - a second native module appears beside casars._core; - a crate spawns catalog executables on Python's behalf.

These pair with the direct-launch, no-Last and command-line-equivalence tests above.

docs.title: ADR-0018: Rust computes; Python is the interface
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0017 makes the product surface a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces: casatasks-style tasks and ia/tb-style tools. CASA puts a large share of its user-level logic in Python. Whole tasks such as simobserve, simanalyze and simalma are Python scripts over C++ tools, and helper modules such as simutil compute pointings, sensitivities and sky-model rescaling with NumPy. Copying that structure would put interpreted, GIL-bound code on the paths users time, and would split each task's behaviour between two languages with two sets of defaults and validation.

Performance is a top priority for casa-rs, and its Rust crates already own parallelism, memory budgets and casacore-compatible I/O.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Computation lives in Rust. Numerical work, data access, file formats, and the orchestration that CASA writes in Python (task scripts and helpers such as simutil) are implemented in Rust crates. When CASA implements a task or tool in Python, casa-rs reads that Python as the specification and ports its semantics to Rust, as it does for C++.
  2. Python is an interface. The casars package:
  3. presents CASA's module, function and method names, signatures and return shapes;
  4. converts arguments and results: Python scalars, lists and dicts, and NumPy arrays as an exchange format;
  5. maps errors to Python exceptions;
  6. starts the work.

It contains no loops over rows, pixels or channels, no numerical algorithms and no file-format code. 3. One source of defaults and validation. Defaults, value normalization and validation come from Rust-owned definitions, for tools as well as tasks. For tasks that is the parameter contract of ADR-0006. The Python layer keeps no second copy. 4. Plot rendering stays in Python, under ADR-0017 item 3. Python may turn Rust-built plot documents into Matplotlib figures, including deriving the coordinate metadata that Matplotlib and Astropy need. This is the only computation the Python layer performs. 5. Rust APIs stay idiomatic: casa-rs is a native Rust implementation, not a C++ API mirror (AGENTS.md, "Engineering Rules"). CASA's call shapes exist only in the Python layer, which maps them onto Rust APIs. Rust crates do not grow CASA-shaped wrappers for the binding's convenience. 6. Rust owns parallelism, and long calls release the GIL. - Python never divides work into chunks, processes or threads for speed. - A Rust call that can run for more than a moment releases the GIL, so other Python threads, such as a notebook kernel's event loop, keep running. - The existing casars._core Image and Table bindings do not release it yet; #839 tracks that fix. New bindings release it from the start.

This decision does not fix the binding mechanism for each surface. Today: - a task call starts the task's own executable as a child process, which runs the task on the shared task front end; Python resolves its parameters and reads its reply through casars._core (ADR-0017 item 4); - stateful tools are expected to be in-process objects in the casars._core extension, like casars.data.Image and casars.data.Table; - ADR-0017 item 4 makes PyO3 in casars._core the only binding.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Each behaviour has one implementation, in the language that sets its speed. - CASA scripts run at casa-rs speed without Python-level hot loops. - Tasks and the tools they are built on share Rust code, so they cannot drift apart. - Rust callers get the full functionality without Python.

Negative: - Porting CASA's Python-level logic, such as task scripts and simutil, takes more work than wrapping or copying it. - Each new tool needs Rust bindings for its methods; it cannot start as a quick Python prototype that ships. - Quirks in CASA's Python logic must be reproduced on purpose in Rust, or recorded as divergences in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - NumPy remains a dependency of the Python package, for array exchange rather than computation. - Exploratory Python may be used during development to understand CASA behaviour, but it does not ship.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Mirror CASA's split, porting its Python task scripts and helpers as Python over Rust primitives. Rejected: hot paths would run in the interpreter, and behaviour would be split across two languages.
  2. Allow NumPy computation in Python where it is "fast enough". Rejected: the boundary would erode case by case, and NumPy code is single-threaded and allocates on every operation.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: Python tests exercise behaviour through the Rust implementation; parity tests compare it with CASA - lint/import/dependency rules: none automatic - CI checks: none specific; the existing python_package job runs the Python tests - review trigger: a change under crates/casars-python/python/casars that does any of the following: - computes on data; - parses a file format; - loops over rows, pixels or channels; - keeps its own default or validation; - splits work for parallelism. - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a casars module other than plot rendering does arithmetic on NumPy arrays or iterates over data - a Python default or validation rule duplicates, or disagrees with, the Rust definition - a CASA task is implemented by porting its Python script into the casars package - a Rust crate gains an API whose only purpose is to mimic a CASA call shape

docs.title: ADR-0019: CASA tools are Rust-declared pyo3 objects in casars.tools
docs.text: Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-20 Truth class: normative Supersedes: Superseded by:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0017 makes a Python package that mirrors CASA's Python interfaces the product surface. ADR-0018 puts all computation in Rust, but leaves open how each surface binds to Rust. Tasks already had a mechanism: the parameter contract and the task's own executable (ADR-0017 item 4). CASA tools did not. The simulation programme brought the first one, the simulator (sm), and every later tool reuses the pattern it set: casars.tools now also has measures, quanta, componentlist, image, coordsys, table, msmetadata and ms.

CASA scripts construct tools as objects, for example from casatools import simulator; sm = simulator(), and then call methods with CASA's parameter names. The defaults those calls see are the installed Python binding's, not the text in the tool's XML. In particular, parameters of "any" type default to [], which the C++ reads as 0 before applying its own fallbacks.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Namespace.
  2. CASA tool classes live in casars.tools, under casatools' class names: simulator, image, table, ms, componentlist and the rest.
  3. Tasks stay in casars.tasks.
  4. A CASA script changes only its imports.
  5. casa-rs ships no casatools or casatasks alias packages, because they would shadow a real CASA installation.
  6. Each tool is a pyo3 class in the casars._core extension, exposed directly; the Python package adds only the module path.
  7. Methods and parameters have CASA's names, and return what CASA's return.
  8. Signatures and defaults are declared in Rust (pyo3 signature). They reproduce the installed CASA binding's effective defaults, not the XML text, where the two differ.
  9. The object-surface schema bundle describes each method from the same Rust types.
  10. Controls CASA lacks are keyword-only constructor arguments with Rust-owned defaults: the memory budget, the backend (auto, cpu, metal) and the worker count. No tool reads environment variables (ADR-0016).
  11. Tools release the GIL. Tool state is Send, and classes are not unsendable. Every method that touches the disk, copies array data or computes releases the GIL. The existing casars.data Image and Table bindings move to this rule under #839.
  12. Tools are thin over idiomatic Rust APIs (ADR-0018 item 5).
  13. The pyo3 layer maps CASA's argument conventions (quantity strings, measures records, scalar-or-list arguments) onto Rust types.
  14. Those conversions are shared by every tool, not written once per tool.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Every tool follows one pattern, so a CASA script works the same way across tools. - Signatures and defaults have one Rust-owned source, which tests can compare against CASA's installed binding. - Long calls do not freeze notebooks or other Python threads.

Negative: - Copying CASA's binding defaults exactly, including their quirks, takes care, and each one must be checked against an installed CASA. - Shared state behind a Send boundary makes the tool code more complex than thread-pinned objects.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - casars.data.Image and casars.data.Table remain beside the image and table tools as the narrower persistent data-access API. They are still unsendable and hold the GIL until #839 moves them to item 4. The tools' methods casa-rs does not implement yet raise NotImplementedError naming the issue that tracks them. - Tools bypass the task parameter contract and Last state, as CASA's tools do.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Python wrapper classes over Rust primitives. Rejected: defaults and argument handling would live in Python, against ADR-0018.
  2. UniFFI objects in casars-frontend-services. Rejected: there is no precedent, and the pyo3 Image and Table classes already work in-process with NumPy.
  3. casatools and casatasks alias packages. Rejected: they would shadow a real CASA installation in the same environment.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: each tool's Python tests construct it from casars.tools and compare every method's signature and defaults with CASA's installed binding, as recorded in tests/data/casa_<tool>_signatures.json and live when CASA is importable. - lint/import/dependency rules: none automatic - CI checks: the existing python_package job - review trigger: - a tool written as a Python class; - a default declared in Python; - a tool reading environment variables; - an unsendable tool class; - a casatools or casatasks package. - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a tool's method signature or default differs from CASA's installed binding without a recorded divergence - per-tool code re-implements quantity, measures or list conversion - a long tool call holds the GIL

docs.title: MeasurementSet boundary: rules
docs.text:
Truth class: normative Last reality check: 2026-11-02

casa-rs reads and writes MeasurementSet v2 and XRADIO MSv4 through one boundary. casa-observation holds the shared contract: the catalogue, the access request and its estimate, the traversal that delivers VisibilityBatches, scientific groups and their completion, the buffer pool, and update sessions. casa_ms::observation_io holds the adapters behind it: opening, the MSv2 and MSv4 stores, the converter and the MSv2 creation plan. Their rustdoc is the contract: what each type holds, what each store delivers, and what it refuses. This file keeps only what the code does not state: the rules that bind changes to the boundary, the owner decisions behind it, and what each capability not yet offered must meet. Moving the remaining consumers onto the boundary is tracked in #1055.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Required behavior C1: source independence No physical row IDs, Zarr keys, storage managers or MS-version branches in numerical processing loops. Only opening, creation, capabilities and diagnostics see the store. C2: faithful values Coordinates and references are native casa-rs Measures types and views, accepted directly by its conversion APIs. Canonical units; explicit frames and precision; native flag and weight semantics; full data-group association; ordered baselines. No silent scientific transform: what the profile cannot represent is refused. C3: layout independence Sample topology, memory layout, scientific grouping and storage chunking stay separate. C4: bounded ownership Every live payload, index, decode buffer, cache, packed copy and queue is admitted; borrowed views cannot outlive or refill their storage. Independent work retires separately; shared storage stays live until its last use. C5: invertible updates A sample-preserving reorder or selection keeps a checked inverse map to the store; a reduction does not, and its result goes to an explicit output. Shared variables have an explicit mutation scope. C6: honest guarantees Unsupported profiles, layouts and native features, and non-atomic writes, are explicit typed refusals. C7: bulk execution Bind numeric kind, layout and invariant context outside scalar loops; use native array views and family-specific kernels. No per-value object allocation, virtual dispatch, coordinate reconstruction or repeated setup or provider lookup.

Moving a consumer onto the boundary deletes its old route in the same change: no compatibility layer and no second production route kept for comparison (a baseline build serves that). A consumer has not moved while a wrapper still leaks physical rows or DATA_DESC_ID into its algorithm.

docs.title: Owner decisions in force
docs.text:
• Formats (2026-10-23): MSv2 and MSv4 (XRADIO schema 4.0.1 on local Zarr v3). MSv3 is deferred until a concrete dataset or producer needs it; it then comes as a named profile with its own independent producer and reader checks, never inferred from a product name. Object stores, MSv4 image persistence and Zarr v2 are separate later work.
  • Shape (2026-10-24): the interface takes MSv4's native shape, and the MSv2 adapter assembles MSv2 into it at opening.
  • Arrays (2026-10-24): numerical arrays and views are ndarray's, under thin domain types that carry axis meaning, Measures metadata, and flag and weight meaning.
  • Measures (2026-10-24): the boundary uses casa-types Measures and quanta types directly, with no observation-specific measure vocabulary, and the Measures APIs may be reworked for bulk use (below).

docs.title: Capabilities not yet offered
docs.text:
Each is refused today with a typed error, or offered only in part. It is offered when its obligation is met.

Capability Obligation Units and conversions requested at binding A requested unit holds for the view's bound scope; conversions fused with the fill; identity conversions copy nothing; weights transform as w / \|a\|² under an amplitude scale a. Precision other than Complex<f32>, bool, f32, f64 Native precision, lossless widening or approved narrowing per role, charged and fused with decode; the writer checks representability. Real-valued data (FLOAT_DATA, MSv4 SPECTRUM) Its own typed variant under its own profile, never reinterpreted as visibilities. More than one data group per traversal Each group keeps its UVW and field and source context, and explicit alias relationships to the others. Unknown occupancy Representable in the batch; conversion to rows resolves it by a declared policy or reports the ambiguity, never inventing an MSv2 row; writing into holes needs an explicit fill policy. Native flags: bitmask dtypes, reason bits, FLAG_CATEGORY, row flags as their own view Dtype and reason bits preserved on writes; generic flagging bound to the store's actual unspecified bit; clearing an effective flag never clears unknown reasons, FLAG_ROW or FLAG_CATEGORY. Per-cell weight fallback An undefined sigma or weight cell falls back per cell, recorded per cell, instead of failing the read. Updates beyond the write-back sessions Bit flags and flag categories; structural writes (a new MSv4 data group, or rebinding a group to its own copy of a shared variable); a composition rule or refusal for conflicting queued patches; per-batch MSv2 planning; a process killed during MSv4 chunk replacement, ENOSPC and stray temporary files, checked by reopening selected and unselected sentinels. Creation beyond the MSv4 writer and the MSv2 creation plan An MSv4 from several observations; failure injection at publication; the writer's held chunk admitted with the producer's batches; omitting padding without a counting pass. Calibration binding in production gainfield and nearest-field selection through bound fields; bandpass and other per-channel tables; tables solved over combined windows; FEED and receptor association; field binding tolerant of ephemeris fields. Ephemerides XRADIO's optional ephemeris variables carried through the boundary and the converter (#998). Baseline-dependent polarization (polarization_mixed) A checked per-baseline basis mapping in the catalogue. TIME_CENTROID_EXTRA_PRECISION The residual carried through the epoch view, slicing, packing and writing; adding it to a large f64 is no substitute. Four-dimensional EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATION_TIME Per-channel exposure in the batch's timing. Resource admission of the whole read and write path Everything a traversal or writer holds is admitted through the runtime's HostResources with cancellable backpressure, including zarrs codec scratch (found or conservatively bounded before work, failing with the minimum it needs) and store caches bounded in bytes. Decode on the admitted executor Executing threads and live codec buffers counted on the real decode path; no fall-through to a global pool; in-partition parallel decode (#1016). Bulk Measures conversion Below.

Updates are addressed in the store's native domain. A patch's affected extent and its conflicts are resolved after expanding data-group aliases and broadcast aliases: setting one channel's effective weight where MSv2 holds one WEIGHT for every channel needs an explicit whole-scalar scope, a channel-resolved destination created under bounded memory, or refusal. Calibration owns any reduction of channel weights into a row WEIGHT and submits both patches; storage never invents that inverse. There is no default last-writer-wins.

The MSv4 write guarantees (per-object atomic replacement, staging and publication, no cross-process lock protocol) and any change to ADR-0008's locking and partial-failure rules need a reviewed new ADR before they are advertised as persistent guarantees.

docs.title: Bulk Measures conversion
docs.text:
Every supported Measures and quanta family offers bulk operation, present and future: directions, epochs and time scales, positions, baselines and UVW, frequencies, radial velocities and Doppler conventions, magnetic and other vector measures, and unit conversions. LSRK↔TOPO is one example, not the acceptance. The shape is prepare, then apply: - bind the route, units and policy once per conversion request; - prepare context-dependent terms (matrices, factors, interpolation state) at their valid scope, in bounded groups where the context varies; - apply to numeric slices into reusable buffers, keeping the per-value nonlinear or iterative work each family needs, with no per-value object, allocation, lock or route search.

A prepared transform is tied to every input that affects it, so a context change invalidates it; equal reference enums with different contexts are not an identity. CASA-compatible ordered interpolation keeps its sequence across batches and workers. Acceptance for each family: consumers use it directly; scalar, bulk and CASA agree to that family's tolerances; and timings, with binding and preparation reported apart from apply, are compared against both the scalar path and any already-prepared production path.

docs.title: Python Support
docs.text:
casa-rs-python installs as casars and separates four public concerns:

  • casars.data provides in-process access to persistent CASA-style images and tables.
  • casars.tasks provides higher-level task wrappers, each of which starts its task's own executable.
  • casars.tools provides CASA's tools as classes under CASA's names, with CASA's methods, parameter order and defaults, so a CASA script changes only its imports (ADR-0019): simulator (CASA's sm), measures (me), quanta (qa), componentlist (cl), image (ia), coordsys (cs), table (tb), msmetadata (msmd) and ms. Each has every method of CASA 6.7.6.14's binding; a method casa-rs does not implement yet raises NotImplementedError naming the issue that records it. A tool's constructor takes only casa-rs's controls, keyword-only: simulator(*, memory_budget=None, backend='auto', workers=None) caps the memory close holds (bytes), names the device to predict on ('auto', 'cpu' or 'metal') and the threads to keep busy; None takes the machine's balanced share, and the MeasurementSet written is the same whatever the controls. casars.simutil provides the parts of CASA's simutil helper class (casatasks.private.simutil, not a tool) that sm scripts and simobserve use: readantenna, the mosaic pointings (calc_pointings2, pointing files), the direction helpers, noisetemp, bandname, polsettings, the baseline helpers, and the sky-model helpers modifymodel and flatimage. from casars import simutil is its public import.
  • casars.parameters is the accepted common API for typed task profiles described by ADR-0006, including its current-only option.

The generic casars.tasks.run() entry point accepts every catalog task. Every task is also exposed exactly once as casars.tasks.<task> through a generated CASA-named function that takes CASA's parameters. These functions share the Rust-owned parameter and result contracts. A call resolves its parameters in Rust, starts the task's executable as a child process with --json-run -, passes the task's log lines to sys.stderr as they arrive. A task whose surface names its CASA task (every task but the casa-rs tasks calibrate, msexplore and msconvert, and plotms) has CASA's exact signature and returns CASA's value; the others return a TaskCompletion. A task that refuses its parameters raises casars.tasks.TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that does not succeed casars.tasks.TaskExecutionError. The executable is the task's CASARS_<APP>_BIN override when it is set, else the one in a suite's bin/ (CASARS_SUITE_ROOT, or the suite the package was installed into), else, for a package built from a checkout, that checkout's build (Compatibility). The in-process casars.data, casars.tools and casars.simutil need no executables.

casars.data is stateful and file-backed. It is intended for interoperability with the Python ecosystem through NumPy-native reads and writes. For images, the current object surface includes pixel-slice writes on existing persistent images; image creation and coordinate-system authoring remain outside the v1 object contract.

docs.title: Parameter profiles
docs.text:
The accepted profile API is shared with the task executables' command lines:

from casars import parameters, tasks

p = parameters.load("profiles/target-imaging.toml", workspace="project")
p.update(niter=20000, threshold="1mJy")

result = tasks.run("tclean", p)   # runs in the draft's workspace, project/

A loaded profile also runs through a CASA-named wrapper, in the current directory: tasks.tclean(**parameters.load("profiles/target-imaging.toml")).

The call saves no Last profile. parameters.last(...) reads the Last that a command-line run saved.

parameters.defaults(surface, ...) and parameters.last(surface, ...) create the other common source types. The resulting TaskParameters supports mapping updates, reset, reload, sparse TOML save, and run. Rust remains the sole parser, normalizer, validator, migration engine, and sparse renderer.

casars.tasks is generated from the catalog's task definitions and supplies one CASA-named wrapper and typing stub per task. A task that mimics CASA's has CASA 6.7.6.14's signature, defaults and return value; the casa-rs tasks (calibrate, msexplore, msconvert) and plotms take keywords with an unset sentinel instead of copying catalog defaults into Python.

Python binds Rust through PyO3 alone, in one native module, casars._core. It carries task parameters, task results and MeasurementSet plot documents as well as the in-process objects: the casars.data.Image and casars.data.Table NumPy object layer, the CASA tool classes of casars.tools and the casars.simutil class.

docs.title: Plotting and image inspection
docs.text:
casa-rs does not rasterise plots. Numeric MeasurementSet plot documents are available as casars.data.measurement_set_plot(...) and are drawn with Matplotlib by casars.data.plot_matplotlib(...). casars.imexplore reads image planes as NumPy arrays (casars.imexplore.data(...)) and draws them with Matplotlib (casars.imexplore.imshow(...)).

See Task Parameter Profiles for sparse TOML, managed Last paths, source precedence, and examples.

Tagged releases build Python artifacts for Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64, plus a source distribution for environments that need to build from source. For suite installation and shell PATH setup, see Install.

docs.title: Common parameter API
docs.text:
ADR-0006 defines this common surface for task profiles, including current-only surface evolution:

casars.parameters.defaults(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.last(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.last_successful(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.load(path, *, workspace=None)

TaskParameters.update(**values)
TaskParameters.reset(name)
TaskParameters.reload()
TaskParameters.save(path)
TaskParameters.run(**values)

casars.tasks.run(task, parameters=None, /, *, workspace=None, **values)
casars.tasks.<casa_task>(casa_parameters..., *, casa_rs_controls...)
casars.tasks.<task>(**parameters)

A task call starts the task's own executable. tasks.run returns a TaskCompletion (task, command, workspace, returncode, stdout, the reply; stderr, the log; provider_invocation, status, message, parameter, value, CASA's return value; and result, the declared products). A wrapper whose surface names its CASA task (every task but the casa-rs tasks calibrate, msexplore and msconvert, and plotms) has CASA's signature, positional or by keyword with CASA's defaults, then casa-rs's own controls, keyword-only, and returns CASA's value, with NumPy arrays where CASA returns them. A parameter casa-rs does not implement yet is taken only at CASA's default; its docstring names the issue. The other wrappers take keyword arguments and return the TaskCompletion.

A value the contract refuses raises ValueError before anything starts, or TypeError for a value of the wrong type. A task that refuses its parameters raises TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that starts and does not succeed TaskExecutionError, a RuntimeError; the .completion of either says how it ended. TaskBinaryNotFoundError (a FileNotFoundError) names what the executable search lacked; TaskInvocationError means the process could not start; TaskResultError means a success's result was malformed.

A Python task call saves no Last or Last Successful profile; those record command-line runs. The CASA-named wrappers take the surface's parameters. A profile runs through one as tasks.gaincal(**parameters.load(path)), since a draft, as a mapping, holds the parameters that have a value.

TaskParameters (a SurfaceParameters constrained to a task definition) is mapping-like and retains value origins and validation diagnostics. Saving writes only required values and differences from current defaults. Surface definitions and defaults are read from the same Rust catalog that the task executables' command lines use.

The catalog-driven generic runner and generated CASA-named functions are the only public task path. Generated conveniences live directly in casars.tasks; their checked .pyi file is regenerated from crates/casa-provider-contracts/resources/parameter-surfaces.json.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
Persistent CASA-compatible image access.

This wrapper exposes rectangular slice and plane I/O using native NumPy arrays while keeping the storage model file-backed and stateful. V1 write support is limited to pixel-slice updates on existing persistent images. Image creation and coordinate/metadata authoring are intentionally out of scope.

Source code in crates/casars-python/python/casars/data.py 
class Image:
    """Persistent CASA-compatible image access.

    This wrapper exposes rectangular slice and plane I/O using native NumPy
    arrays while keeping the storage model file-backed and stateful. V1 write
    support is limited to pixel-slice updates on existing persistent images.
    Image creation and coordinate/metadata authoring are intentionally out of
    scope.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: _core.Image) -> None:
        self._inner = inner

    @classmethod
    def open(cls, path: StrPath, *, writable: bool = False) -> "Image":
        """Open an existing persistent image.

        Set ``writable=True`` to enable pixel-slice updates with
        :meth:`put_slice`.
        """

        return cls(_core.Image.open(path, writable=writable))

    @property
    def shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Image shape in CASA/Rust axis order."""

        return tuple(self._inner.shape)

    @property
    def pixel_type(self) -> str:
        """Pixel dtype name such as ``float32`` or ``complex128``."""

        return self._inner.pixel_type

    @property
    def units(self) -> str:
        """Image unit string."""

        return self._inner.units

    @property
    def image_info(self) -> RecordLike:
        """Structured image-info record."""

        return self._inner.image_info

    @property
    def misc_info(self) -> RecordLike:
        """Structured miscellaneous-info record."""

        return self._inner.misc_info

    @property
    def coordinate_system(self) -> RecordLike:
        """Renderer-neutral coordinate metadata, including celestial WCS."""

        return self._inner.coordinate_system

    def _direction_wcs(self) -> tuple[int, int, dict[str, Any]] | None:
        """The pixel axes of the image's direction and the FITS WCS keywords
        `exportfits` writes for the image, or None; for `casars.imexplore`."""

        return self._inner._direction_wcs()

    @property
    def mask_names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of persisted masks attached to the image."""

        return list(self._inner.mask_names)

    @property
    def default_mask_name(self) -> str | None:
        """Name of the default mask, if any."""

        return self._inner.default_mask_name

    def get_slice(
        self,
        start: Sequence[int],
        shape: Sequence[int],
        *,
        stride: Sequence[int] | None = None,
    ) -> ArrayLike:
        """Read a rectangular image chunk as a NumPy array."""

        return self._inner.get_slice(list(start), list(shape), stride=None if stride is None else list(stride))

    def put_slice(self, data: ArrayLike, start: Sequence[int]) -> None:
        """Write a rectangular image chunk into an existing persistent image.

        This is the supported v1 write path for images. It does not imply
        support for Python-side image creation or coordinate/metadata editing.
        """

        self._inner.put_slice(np.asarray(data), list(start))

    def get_plane(self, axis: int, index: int) -> ArrayLike:
        """Read one plane orthogonal to ``axis``."""

        return np.squeeze(self._inner.get_plane(axis, index), axis=axis)

    def get_mask_slice(
        self,
        start: Sequence[int],
        shape: Sequence[int],
        *,
        stride: Sequence[int] | None = None,
    ) -> ArrayLike | None:
        """Read a rectangular chunk from the default mask."""

        return self._inner.get_mask_slice(
            list(start),
            list(shape),
            stride=None if stride is None else list(stride),
        )

class Table:
    """Persistent CASA-compatible table access."""

    def __init__(self, inner: _core.Table) -> None:
        self._inner = inner

    @classmethod
    def open(cls, path: StrPath, *, writable: bool = False) -> "Table":
        """Open an existing persistent table."""

        return cls(_core.Table.open(path, writable=writable))

    @property
    def row_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of rows in the table."""

        return self._inner.row_count

    @property
    def column_names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Known column names."""

        return list(self._inner.column_names)

    @property
    def keywords(self) -> RecordLike:
        """Table-level keyword record."""

        return self._inner.keywords

    def column_keywords(self, name: str) -> RecordLike | None:
        """Column-level keyword record for ``name``."""

        return self._inner.column_keywords(name)

    def get_cell(self, row: int, column: str) -> Any:
        """Read one cell."""

        return self._inner.get_cell(row, column)

    def set_cell(self, row: int, column: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Write one cell."""

        self._inner.set_cell(row, column, value)

    def get_column(
        self,
        column: str,
        *,
        start: int = 0,
        count: int | None = None,
        step: int = 1,
    ) -> Any:
        """Read a column range as NumPy arrays or native Python structures."""

        return self._inner.get_column(column, start=start, count=count, step=step)

    def put_column(
        self,
        column: str,
        values: Sequence[Any],
        *,
        start: int = 0,
        step: int = 1,
    ) -> int:
        """Write a column range from Python-native values."""

        return self._inner.put_column(column, values, start=start, step=step)

    def set_column_keywords(self, column: str, keywords: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Replace the keyword record for ``column``."""

        self._inner.set_column_keywords(column, dict(keywords))

def measurement_set_plot(
    measurement_set: StrPath,
    *,
    preset: str = "amplitude_vs_time",
    data_column: str = "data",
    color_by: str | None = "field",
    selection: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    avgchannel: int | None = None,
    avgtime: float | None = None,
    avgscan: bool = False,
    avgfield: bool = False,
    avgbaseline: bool = False,
    avgantenna: bool = False,
    avgspw: bool = False,
    scalar: bool = False,
    iteraxis: str | None = None,
    max_plot_points: int = 100_000,
) -> MeasurementSetPlotData:
    """Return editable numeric plot data from the canonical Rust MS planner.

    This is an in-process data-object operation, not a task invocation. Rust
    builds a typed plot document; render it with :func:`plot_matplotlib`.
    """

    result = _core.build_measurement_set_plot(
        measurement_set,
        preset,
