def plot_matplotlib(
    plot_data: MeasurementSetPlotData,
    *,
    figure: Any = None,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Render MeasurementSet plot data into editable Matplotlib objects."""

    try:
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
    except ImportError as error:  # pragma: no cover - environment dependent
        raise ImportError(
            "Matplotlib plotting requires `pip install casa-rs-python[plot]`"
        ) from error
    panel_count = max(1, len(plot_data.panels))
    if figure is None:
        figure, axes = plt.subplots(panel_count, 1, squeeze=False)
        resolved_axes = list(axes[:, 0])
    else:
        resolved_axes = [
            figure.add_subplot(panel_count, 1, index + 1)
            for index in range(panel_count)
        ]
    for panel, axis in zip(plot_data.panels, resolved_axes, strict=True):
        for series in panel.series:
            axis.scatter(series.x, series.y, label=series.label, s=9)
        axis.set_title(panel.title)
        if panel.axes:
            axis.set_xlabel(panel.axes[0].label)
        if len(panel.axes) > 1:
            axis.set_ylabel(panel.axes[1].label)
        if plot_data.show_legend and len(panel.series) > 1:
            axis.legend()
    figure.suptitle(plot_data.title)
    return figure, resolved_axes[0] if len(resolved_axes) == 1 else resolved_axes

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TaskCompletion:
    """One finished task process: how it ended and what it wrote.

    ``status`` is the task's outcome: ``succeeded``, ``refused`` (its
    parameters, before it changed anything), ``failed``, ``interrupted``,
    ``signalled``, or ``malformed_reply``. ``stdout`` is the task's reply and
    ``stderr`` its log, which was also written to ``sys.stderr`` as the task
    ran.
    """

    task: str
    command: tuple[str, ...]
    workspace: Path
    returncode: int
    stdout: str
    stderr: str
    provider_invocation: ProviderInvocation
    status: str
    message: str | None
    parameter: str | None
    value: Any
    result: object | None

    @property
    def successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the task succeeded."""

        return self.status == "succeeded"

    @property
    def products(self) -> tuple[object, ...]:
        """Typed contract-declared products from the Rust completion decoder."""

        if self.result is None:
            return ()
        return tuple(self.result.products)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """One line saying how the task ended."""

        at = f" (parameter {self.parameter!r})" if self.parameter else ""
        if self.status == "succeeded":
            return f"{self.task} succeeded"
        if self.status == "refused":
            return f"{self.task} refused its parameters{at}: {self.message}"
        if self.status == "failed":
            return f"{self.task} failed{at}: {self.message}"
        if self.status == "interrupted":
            return f"{self.task} was interrupted: {self.message}"
        detail = self.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["no log output"]
        if self.status == "signalled":
            return f"{self.task} was ended by signal {-self.returncode}: {detail[0]}"
        return f"{self.task} gave no valid reply ({self.message}): {detail[0]}"

class TaskParameterError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a task refuses its parameters before it changes anything;
    ``completion`` says why (#931).

    A value the parameter contract refuses raises ``ValueError``, or
    ``TypeError`` for a value of the wrong type, before the task starts; this
    is the refusal of a value only the task itself can judge, such as an

    generated parameter checker in both cases.

        self.completion = completion
        super().__init__(completion.describe())

docs.text:
Run any catalog task, with CASA-named values.

parameters is a draft to start from, such as a loaded profile; the contract's defaults otherwise. The task runs in workspace: the draft's, or the current directory. Values are normalized and checked by Rust before the task starts, so a value the contract refuses raises ValueError and starts nothing.

The call loads and saves no Last profile: those record command-line runs. :meth:TaskParameters.last and :meth:TaskParameters.write_last stay explicit. CASA's own parameters, such as overwrite, are the consent to replace or change data. A task that refuses its parameters raises :class:TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that starts and does not succeed :class:TaskExecutionError, a RuntimeError; an interrupt (Ctrl-C) is passed to the task, which is given time to stop, and then raised here.

Source code in crates/casars-python/python/casars/tasks/_runner.py 
def run(
    task: str,
    parameters: SurfaceParameters | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    workspace: StrPath | None = None,
    **values: ParameterData,
) -> TaskCompletion:
    """Run any catalog task, with CASA-named ``values``.

    ``parameters`` is a draft to start from, such as a loaded profile; the
    contract's defaults otherwise. The task runs in ``workspace``: the
    draft's, or the current directory. Values are normalized and checked by
    Rust before the task starts, so a value the contract refuses raises
    ``ValueError`` and starts nothing.

    The call loads and saves no Last profile: those record command-line runs.
    :meth:`TaskParameters.last` and :meth:`TaskParameters.write_last` stay
    explicit. CASA's own parameters, such as ``overwrite``, are the consent
    to replace or change data. A task that refuses its parameters raises
    :class:`TaskParameterError`, a ``ValueError``, and one that starts and
    does not succeed :class:`TaskExecutionError`, a ``RuntimeError``; an
    interrupt (Ctrl-C) is passed to the task, which is given time to stop,
    and then raised here.
    """

    resolved_workspace = _resolve_workspace(workspace, parameters)
    if parameters is not None:
        if parameters.surface != task:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameters target {parameters.surface!r}, not requested task {task!r}"
            )
        resolved = parameters.copy()
    else:
        resolved = TaskParameters.defaults(task, workspace=resolved_workspace)
    if values:
        resolved.set_many(values)
    return _execute(task, resolved, resolved_workspace)

docs.title: casars.tools
docs.text:
CASA tools for casa-rs, under CASA's class names (ADR-0019).

A CASA script changes only its imports::

from casars.tools import measures, quanta, simulator

me = measures()
sm = simulator()
sm.open("sim.ms")
sm.setconfig(referencelocation=me.observatory("VLA"), ...)

Each tool is a class in the casars._core extension, with CASA's method names, parameter order and defaults declared in Rust. This module adds only the module path.

docs.title: casars.simutil
docs.text:
CASA's simutil helper class for casa-rs.

A CASA script changes only its import::

from casars import simutil

u = simutil.simutil()
x, y, z, d, padnames, antnames, telescope, posobs = u.readantenna("vla.d.cfg")
pointings = u.calc_pointings2("10arcsec", ["60arcsec", "40arcsec"], maptype="ALMA",
                              direction="J2000 18h00m00 -23d00m00")

In CASA, simutil is a Python helper class in the private simutil module of CASA's task package, not a CASA tool, so it is not in casars.tools or in the object-surface bundle. casa-rs implements, in Rust (the class lives in the casars._core extension, ADR-0018), the parts sm scripts and simobserve use: - readantenna; - the pointings calc_pointings2, read_pointings and write_pointings; - the direction helpers direction_splitter, average_direction, median_direction, dir_m2s, wrapang, isquantity and isdirection; - noisetemp, bandname and polsettings; - itrf2loc, baselineLengths and approxBeam; - the sky-model helpers modifymodel and flatimage.

casars.simutil is the class's public import: CASA's private path would mislabel a supported entry point.

docs.title: Data API
docs.text:
casars.data exposes persistent file-backed objects only.

The module also publishes its canonical object-surface contract directly from Rust:

  • protocol_info() returns the stable object protocol descriptor
  • schema_bundle() returns the canonical schema bundle for Image, Table and the casars.tools classes

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Use Image.open(path, writable=False) to open an existing CASA-compatible image. The v1 surface is intentionally narrow:

  • metadata access through shape, pixel_type, units, image_info, misc_info, mask_names, and default_mask_name
  • pixel I/O through get_slice, put_slice, get_plane, and get_mask_slice

Read operations return NumPy arrays for numeric payloads. Writes accept NumPy-compatible inputs and materialize them into the image as owned copies.

docs.title: V1 write policy
docs.text:
Image writes are part of the supported v1 API, but only in a narrow form:

  • supported: pixel-slice updates on existing persistent images via put_slice
  • supported: reads from the persisted default mask via get_mask_slice
  • not part of v1: image creation from Python
  • not part of v1: coordinate-system authoring or editing from Python
  • not part of v1: general metadata authoring beyond the persisted fields exposed for read access

In other words, casars.data.Image is a stable read/write pixel-access surface for existing images, not a full Python image-construction or image-metadata editing API.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Use Table.open(path, writable=False) to open an existing table. The v1 table surface focuses on cell/column access instead of browser-style row dictionaries:

  • table metadata through row_count, column_names, keywords, and column_keywords(name)
  • cell access through get_cell and set_cell
  • column access through get_column and put_column
  • column keyword updates through set_column_keywords

Returned values follow the documented type mapping:

  • scalar numeric, bool, and complex values become Python scalars
  • numeric scalar columns become NumPy arrays
  • fixed-shape numeric array cells and columns become NumPy arrays
  • variable-shape array columns fall back to Python lists of per-row NumPy arrays
  • record values become nested Python dictionaries

docs.title: Calibrate Tasks
docs.text:
The calibration tasks are generated, CASA-named wrappers in casars.tasks:

  • calibrate(mode=..., ...), the workflow surface: apply (the default), solve_gain, solve_bandpass, fluxscale, gencal, summary, stats and export_corrected_data;
  • applycal, gaincal, bandpass, fluxscale and gencal, with CASA 6.7.6's signatures: CASA's parameters in CASA's order with CASA's defaults, then casa-rs's keyword-only output, overwrite and format (and array, gaincurve_table where they apply).

The CASA-named functions return what CASA's tasks return: gaincal and bandpass a dictionary of the tables applied (apply_tables) and solved (solve_tables), the data selected (selectvis) and how many solution intervals each window and antenna reached at each stage (solvestats); fluxscale its flux densities per field and spectral window; applycal and gencal None. calibrate(...) and tasks.run(name, ...) return a TaskCompletion. A CASA parameter casa-rs does not implement yet is taken only at its default, and a CASA value it does not implement yet is refused; both refusals name #979.

Each call starts the calibrate executable directly, with the surface as its first word (calibrate gaincal), and sends one TaskRunRequest on --json-run -: the values the call set, resolved inside the executable against the same contract as its own command line. Its log lines reach sys.stderr as they arrive. Python projects no flags and builds no Rust request. A refused value names its parameter: the task's refusal raises TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and a run that does not succeed raises TaskExecutionError; the .completion of either has its status, message and parameter.

On the CASA-named surfaces the chain is CASA's: gaintable is a list of tables, and gainfield, interp and spwmap are positional lists, so gaintable[i] takes gainfield[i], interp[i] and spwmap[i], and a table past the end of a list takes CASA's default for it (every field, 'linear', no window map). calwt holds one flag for every table or one per table. docallib=True applies the calibration library callib instead.

On calibrate, gaintables and summary_paths are lists of calibration-table paths: a list, or one comma-separated string. Its per-table controls (gainfield, interp, spwmap, calwt) are ;-separated strings aligned to gaintables, one value for every table or one per table.

The calibrate binary takes the same parameters on its own command line.

docs.title: Parameter document compatibility
docs.text:
Sparse TOML documents carry two independent versions:

  • casars.format versions the document envelope and TOML conventions.
  • casars.contract versions the selected task definition.

Loading resolves sparse overrides against the current provider definition. Newly added optional parameters receive current defaults. Omitted parameters whose defaults changed also receive the new default and produce a compatibility warning. Renames and type/value changes require an explicit ordered migration; future or unmigratable versions fail before invocation.

This behavior preserves user intent rather than freezing an exact historical request. Use a separate resolved run manifest when exact replay is required. The Python implementation uses the shared Rust runtime and must not maintain an independent migration or default table.

Managed state normally lives at:

<workspace>/.casa-rs/parameters/<surface-id>/last.toml
<workspace>/.casa-rs/parameters/<surface-id>/last-successful.toml

CASA_RS_STATE_DIR redirects the managed root without changing workspace path resolution. An explicit source profile is never overwritten without an explicit save.

docs.title: Task-runner compatibility
docs.text:
Python has one task transport: every generated casars.tasks.<task> callable and casars.tasks.run start the task's own executable, named by the canonical application catalog, with its surface's fixed arguments and --json-run -. One Rust resolver (casa_provider_contracts::resolve_task_executable, through casars._core) finds that executable. The first step that applies decides:

  1. the task's catalog override variable, CASARS_<APP>_BIN (for example CASARS_IMAGER_BIN or CASARS_CALIBRATE_BIN), names the file;
  2. a suite root holds it at <root>/bin/<executable>: CASARS_SUITE_ROOT, or else the installed suite the Python package belongs to (the installer's environment is <suite>/python, beside <suite>/bin and bundle-manifest.json);
  3. a development checkout: the newest debug or release build of the executable under the workspace the package was built from, in $CARGO_TARGET_DIR or target/.

A step that applies but lacks the file raises TaskBinaryNotFoundError naming what it lacked; it never falls through to a later step, so an installed suite never runs a checkout's build. A missing development build is reported with the cargo build -p <package> --bin <executable> that makes it. Python does not search the current directory or PATH, and nothing runs through cargo. A wheel installed outside a suite, such as one from PyPI, runs tasks only with CASARS_SUITE_ROOT or the task's override set; its in-process casars.data, casars.tools and casars.simutil need no executables. The executable validates the provider contract and request before execution; Python does not maintain a second protocol descriptor, provider schema, or compatibility handshake.

Release tags also build and publish Python package artifacts separately from the Rust binaries:

  • GitHub release assets always receive the built wheels, source distribution, suite bundles, standalone binary bundles, and installer script.
  • PyPI publication is attempted from the same workflow when PYPI_API_TOKEN is configured.

That means Python package compatibility has two layers:

  1. package-version compatibility with the published wheel or sdist
  2. runtime contract compatibility with the resolved suite and its catalog-owned task executables

The casars.data surface has its own narrower stability boundary in v1:

  • stable in v1: reading existing persistent images and tables
  • stable in v1: writing pixel slices into existing persistent images with Image.put_slice
  • deferred from v1: image creation, coordinate-system authoring, and broader image metadata editing

The direct object-surface contract published by casars.data.protocol_info() and casars.data.schema_bundle() is currently:

  • protocol name: casars_data_objects
  • protocol version: 1
  • surface kind: object

That boundary is intentional. The v1 compatibility promise covers file-backed data access and pixel updates, not the full CASA image-authoring surface.

The same bundle, still at protocol version 1, also describes the casars.tools classes (simulator, measures, quanta, componentlist, image, coordsys, table, msmetadata, ms). The bundle's Python projection names casars.data as its module; a tool's projection entry names its own module (casars.tools) and class, and records the parameter order of its constructor's keyword-only controls and of each method, which the JSON Schema properties do not keep. Its annotations.python entry records whether casa-rs implements each method. A consumer reads an object's module from its own projection entry and falls back to the bundle's. The provider contract (docs/provider-contracts.md, "Object Surfaces") describes a tool's entry.

casars.simutil is the public import of CASA's simutil helper class (from casars import simutil, for CASA's from casatasks.private import simutil). It is not a CASA tool and is not in the bundle.

The installed suite's layout, channels and command links are described in Install.

docs.title: casa-rs and CASA 6.7.6.14 tasks
docs.text:
Truth class: generated reference Generated by: scripts/check-casa-inventory.py --write Sources: resources/casa-compat/casa-6.7.6.14/ (read from CASA by tools/casa-compat/dump_casa_task_inventory.py), crates/casa-provider-contracts/resources/parameter-surfaces.json, parameter-catalog.json, and reviewed resources/casa-compat/semantics/

Do not edit this file by hand. Regenerate it after changing the inventory or a surface.

Each casa-rs task that mimics a CASA task (#931) against that task as CASA 6.7.6.14 defines it: whether it presents CASA's signature, the CASA parameters casa-rs does not take yet, those it takes but accepts only at CASA's default, the parameters casa-rs takes that CASA does not (casa-rs names for CASA concepts, or casa-rs-only controls), whether the shared parameters keep CASA's order, and the defaults that differ. calibrate, msconvert and msexplore are casa-rs tasks with no CASA counterpart.

The CASA parameters casa-rs lacks or accepts only at their defaults are tracked by family: images in #977, MeasurementSet and flagging in #978, calibration in #979 and tclean in #980.

docs.text:
Implementation status is not behavioral verification. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing forms or combinations; Default only is derived from the runtime refusal contract; Not implemented has no implementation; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below. No signature or return-structure result establishes scientific equivalence.

Audit baseline: c64f13cb09054b080fe8b228a5f2c02c99bfd486. Status counts: Default only: 7, Implemented: 43, Not implemented: 0, Partial: 42, Unassessed: 0.

Mappings, defaults, catalog domains, constraints and conditional default-only refusals are generated from the existing task contract. The catalog may admit values that the native reader then refuses: the reviewed scope and linked combinations describe those restrictions.

CASA parameter CASA default casa-rs default; mapping Implementation Scope and runtime restrictions Evidence vis '' ''; vis → vis Partial Contract 38: a list of MeasurementSets images as one, as CASA's tclean images its vis list. Each is opened and surveyed with its own selectors (one per MeasurementSet, or one or a list of one for all; another length is refused with CASA's message), ordered stably by its earliest MAIN TIME and visited as CASA visits its ms0, ms1, ... keys, as text (input_parameters.checkAndFixSelectionPars, mslisthelper.sort_mslist, imager_base.selectData); one selecting no sample is left out unless it is the first (SynthesisImagerVi2::selectData). The image's coordinates (obs date, telescope, phase centre, rest frequency, a cube's axis) come from CASA's msobj (buildCoordinateSystem): the first MeasurementSet, or for a cube or cubedata whose start is a frequency or velocity the last one whose selected band holds it (CAS-12877); a continuum band, and so the MFS and MT-MFS reference frequency, spans every one. A cube reads each other MeasurementSet's window where it reaches the cube, and one that does not reach it is read so its MODEL_DATA holds the zero prediction, as CASA writes it. Weighting density spans every MeasurementSet; datacolumn falls back to DATA per MeasurementSet; savemodel writes each one's MODEL_DATA (or virtual model). CASA's addwtspec, which adds WEIGHT_SPECTRUM to a listed MeasurementSet lacking it as a Vi/VB2 workaround, is not done: casa-rs reads each MeasurementSet's own weights, which that column copies, and never modifies its inputs. A row's spectral window and field are keyed among every MeasurementSet's, as if they were concatenated, so the mosaic keeps each one's beams (CASA's msId_spw, SimplePBConvFunc::convIndex) and a mosweight density each one's fields (VisImagingWeight's msId_field) apart; its dishes are every MeasurementSet's aperture classes (HetArrayConvFunc::findAntennaSizes). MFS accepts LSRK/BARY/TOPO: the header records the selected band's envelope in that frame (MSUtil::getFreqRangeInSpw) while samples grid in LSRK as CASA's FTMachine grids them; MFS REST and other frames are refused (issue 980). spectralCatalog domain: string signature, reader veltype 'radio' 'radio'; veltype → veltype Partial MFS ignores it; cube maps radio->RADIO, optical/z->OPTICAL, beta/relativistic/true->BETA; other values refused (issue 980). spectralCatalog domain: string signature, reader restfreq [] []; restfreq → restfreq Partial A list: the first entry is the image's rest frequency (a cube's velocity axis and every header, MFS included) and the others follow it in the header's restfreqs, as buildCoordinateSystemCore appends them; a list with a blank entry is refused. Empty MFS reads SOURCE metadata using first selected SPW and CASA-VI field ordering, else the recorded band's midpoint; DOPPLER-backed lookup and multiple SOURCE key groups with stored wildcards explicitly refuse as unfinished (#980). spectralCatalog domain: list[string], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, approved-comparisons-restart interpolation 'linear' 'linear'; interpolation → interpolation Partial MFS ignores it; cube forwards it except cubic, which is refused (issue 823). spectralCatalog domain: cubic, linear, nearest, none; Constraints: [{"kind": "allowed_values", "values": ["cubic", "linear", "nearest"]}] signature, reader perchanweightdensity True True; perchanweightdensity → perchanweightdensity Implemented Copied as per-channel density-weighting flag. spectralCatalog domain: bool signature, reader gridder 'standard' 'standard'; gridder → gridder Partial Aliases standard/ft/gridft, W aliases, and mosaic aliases normalize; awproject accepted; awprojectft and other unsupported families refused (issue 980). griddersCatalog domain: awp2, awphpg, awproject, awprojectft, ft, ftmosaic, gridft, imagemosaic, mosaic, mosaicft, standard, widefield, wproject, wprojectft signature, reader facets 1 1; facets → facets Partial Standard gridder passes count; mosaic rejects count != 1 as CASA does; W/AW count != 1 refused pending support (issue 980). griddersCatalog domain: integer; Constraints: [{"kind": "positive"}] signature, reader psfphasecenter '' ''; psfphasecenter → psfphasecenter Default only Read and ignored; non-default catalog-refused for mosaic/mosaicft/ftmosaic (issue 980). Catalog domain: string; Non-default refused when (gridder='mosaic' or gridder='mosaicft' or gridder='ftmosaic') (#1062) signature, reader wprojplanes 1 1; wprojplanes → wprojplanes Implemented W: -1 becomes derive/None and positive counts pass; non-positive other than -1 refused. W aliases with one plane normalize to standard. AW: any positive count, one plane co-planar without the W term (createAWPFTMachine); a native EVLA cache generates that many planes, an imported CASA cache holds its own; -1 refused (issue 980). Ignored by other gridders. Catalog domain: integer signature, reader vptable '' ''; vptable → vptable Default only Read and ignored; non-default catalog-refused for listed non-AW gridder families (issue 980). griddersCatalog domain: string; Non-default refused when (gridder='standard' or gridder='ft' or gridder='gridft' or gridder='widefield' or gridder='wproject' or gridder='wprojectft' or gridder='mosaic' or gridder='mosaicft' or gridder='ftmosaic' or gridder='imagemosaic') (#980) signature, reader mosweight True True; mosweight → mosweight Implemented With gridder exactly mosaic and density weighting, True weighs each field by its own density and Briggs factors (multiField): a continuum density per field (VisImagingWeight), or with a cube's per-channel density each field's padded density cube, gridded from that field's rows alone with Briggs factors per channel and a fixed swing pad of two planes a side (BriggsCubeWeightor::fillImgWeightCol, issue 818); mosaicft and ftmosaic set it False, as CASA. Every field's f64 density cube is resident for the whole run, 8·(nx·ny+1)·F·(C+4) bytes for F field keys spanned (the selected fields with data, first to last, so a sparse selection multiplies it) and C channels, where CASA holds one field's Float cube at a time: a large cube mosaic is refused by admission (20 fields × 480 channels × 800² is about 50 GB; issue 1085). griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, mosweight-cube-20261103 aterm True True; aterm → aterm Partial AW: read as AWProjectFT::makeCFObject reads it; a native EVLA cache generates its cells without the aperture when false, and then without wideband cells, for an EVLA or (without the aperture only) a VLA observation; an imported CASA cache holds the cells its run made. aterm=False with psterm=False is refused, as CASA refuses it. Ignored by other gridders. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader psterm False False; psterm → psterm Partial AW: read as AWProjectFT::makeCFObject reads it; a native EVLA cache generates its cells with the prolate spheroidal when true, and an imported CASA cache holds the cells its run made. Ignored by other gridders. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader wbawp True True; wbawp → wbawp Partial AW: a native EVLA cache generates cells at each selected window's frequency when true (with the aperture), else at the image reference frequency alone (AWConvFunc::makeFreqValList); an imported CASA cache holds the cells its run made. Ignored by other gridders. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader conjbeams False False; conjbeams → conjbeams Partial AW: each sample grids with the cell nearest its conjugate frequency when true, its own otherwise (CFBuffer::nearestFreqNdx), and a native EVLA cache weighs with the beam there (AWConvFunc::fillConvFuncBuffer2); the mosaic grids with conjugate beams on an image of one plane and ignores it on a cube, as CASA; other gridders ignore it. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader cfcache '' ''; cfcache → cfcache Partial AW with default CASA-import cache requires non-empty path and passes it; otherwise ignored. griddersCatalog domain: path (directory) signature, reader usepointing False False; usepointing → usepointing Implemented Copied only for mosaic/AW; read and ignored for standard/W. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader computepastep 360.0 360.0; computepastep → computepastep Default only Read and ignored; non-default values catalog-refused for applicable AW families (issue 980). griddersCatalog domain: float; Non-default refused when (gridder='awproject' or gridder='awphpg' or gridder='awprojectft' or gridder='awp2') (#1070) signature, reader rotatepastep 360.0 360.0; rotatepastep → rotatepastep Default only Read and ignored; non-default values catalog-refused for applicable AW families (issue 980). griddersCatalog domain: float; Non-default refused when (gridder='awproject' or gridder='awprojectft') (#1070) signature, reader pointingoffsetsigdev [] []; pointingoffsetsigdev → pointingoffsetsigdev Implemented Scalar/list numbers converted to comma text for AW; otherwise ignored. griddersCatalog domain: list[float], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader pblimit 0.2 0.2; pblimit → pblimit Implemented Copied; request requires non-zero magnitude below 1. griddersCatalog domain: float signature, reader normtype 'flatnoise' 'flatnoise'; normtype → normtype Implemented Passed only to mosaic/AW; pbsquare refused (issue 823); other gridders ignore it. griddersCatalog domain: flatnoise, flatsky, pbsquare signature, reader deconvolver 'hogbom' 'hogbom'; deconvolver → deconvolver Partial hogbom/clark/multiscale/mtmfs pass; asp refused with issue 223; other CASA algorithms refused with issue 823. deconvolutionCatalog domain: asp, clark, clark_exp, clarkstokes, clarkstokes_exp, hogbom, mem, mtmfs, multiscale signature, reader scales [] []; scales → scales Partial Number list; forwarded only for multiscale/mtmfs, otherwise normalized to none; request disallows negative scales. deconvolutionCatalog domain: list[float], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader nterms 2 2; nterms → nterms Partial Used only by mtmfs; other deconvolvers force one. mtmfs nterms=1 refused (issue 980); request enforces >1 exactly for mtmfs. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader smallscalebias 0.0 0.0; smallscalebias → smallscalebias Implemented Copied to request. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader fusedthreshold 0.0 0.0; fusedthreshold → fusedthreshold Partial Ignored outside ASP, as CASA ignores it. ASP is refused (#223); no ASP implementation is claimed. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader largestscale -1 -1; largestscale → largestscale Partial Ignored outside ASP, as CASA ignores it. ASP is refused (#223); no ASP implementation is claimed. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader restoration True True; restoration → restoration Implemented Read by the request: False writes no .image, .image.pbcor or spectral index (the PB pbcor asks for is still written), as task_tclean.py skips restoreImages and pbcorImages. Active from tclean contract 34. restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader restoringbeam [] []; restoringbeam → restoringbeam Implemented As SynthesisParamsDeconv::fromRecord: empty -> each plane's fitted beam; common -> one enclosing beam; one, two or three quantities -> a circular beam, an ellipse at angle 0 or an ellipse at an angle, which restores every plane and is the image's one beam, the residual rescaled from the fitted beam as rescaleResolution does (left as it is, with a warning, when the fitted beam does not deconvolve); any other count or a zero axis -> fitted beams; non-angular, negative or inverted axes refused as CASA refuses them. deconvolutionCatalog domain: list[string], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader pbcor False False; pbcor → pbcor Implemented Copied; determines primary-beam-corrected product/beam behavior downstream. griddersCatalog domain: bool signature, reader outlierfile '' ''; outlierfile → outlierfile Partial Native outlier fields, natural weighting, dirty or Hogbom; each outlier currently has standard single-term MFS defaults. Per-field differing modes, start models and spectral controls are restricted by the existing parser. restartCatalog domain: path (image) signature, reader weighting 'natural' 'natural'; weighting → weighting Partial Every CASA weighting accepted: natural, uniform, superuniform (uniform over a density summed in a box of npixels, or 3), radial (weight times uv distance), briggs, briggsabs (robust^2 and 2 noise^2, CASA rmode abs) and briggsbwtaper; briggsbwtaper with MFS refused as CASA does. Superuniform and radial are never per-channel densities, as in SynthesisImagerVi2::weight. Cube Briggs per-channel density follows BriggsCubeWeightor's cell orientation (negated u and v). Per-field density (mosweight) follows VisImagingWeight's and BriggsCubeWeightor's multiField. Outlier fields under density weighting remain refused. griddersCatalog domain: briggs, briggsabs, briggsbwtaper, natural, radial, superuniform, uniform signature, reader, cloud-continuation robust 0.5 0.5; robust → robust Implemented Copied to request. griddersCatalog domain: float signature, reader noise '1.0Jy' '1.0Jy'; noise → noise Implemented Read for weighting=briggsabs only, as a flux density in Jy; robust 0 with noise 0 refused in every mode (CASA refuses it for cubes and weighs continuum visibilities infinite). Ignored by the other weightings. Active from tclean contract 34. griddersCatalog domain: string signature, reader npixels 0 0; npixels → npixels Implemented Read as SynthesisImagerVi2::weight reads it: superuniform's box half-width (3 when zero or less), a continuum uniform/Briggs density grid of npixels x npixels cells over the image's uv extent, and a cube per-channel density's box (BriggsCubeWeightor superUniformBox); ignored by natural and radial. Negative values for uniform/Briggs and any non-zero value with briggsbwtaper are refused, as CASA fails or images nothing. Active from tclean contract 34. griddersCatalog domain: integer signature, reader uvtaper [''] ['']; uvtaper → uvtaper Partial Unit-bearing circular/elliptical angles or lambda/klambda; one/two/three entries. Missing-unit values are refused instead of reproducing CASA's radians-versus-documented-lambda behavior (#970). griddersCatalog domain: list[string], length 0..3; scalar allowed signature, reader, additions niter 0 0; niter → niter Implemented Copied to the total reported minor-cycle iteration limit. Owner-approved contract31 defaults the native extra Hogbom accounting mode to casa-inclusive, matching CASA's extra physical component at a positive cycle limit. Explicit strict remains available; scientific verification is recorded separately. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader, compensated-current gain 0.1 0.1; gain → gain Implemented Copied to request. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader threshold 0.0 0.0; threshold → threshold Implemented Copied; request interprets quantity in Jy/beam; return record echoes original number/text for dirty runs. deconvolutionCatalog domain: quantity; Constraints: [{"kind": "non_empty"}] signature, reader nsigma 0.0 0.0; nsigma → nsigma Implemented Copied; request requires non-negative value. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader cycleniter -1 -1; cycleniter → minor_cycle_length Implemented CASA correction: <=0 or >niter becomes niter (at least 1); maps to minor_cycle_length. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader cyclefactor 1.0 1.0; cyclefactor → cyclefactor Implemented Copied to request. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader minpsffraction 0.05 0.05; minpsffraction → minpsffraction Implemented Copied to request. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader maxpsffraction 0.8 0.8; maxpsffraction → maxpsffraction Implemented Copied to request. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader interactive False False; interactive → interactive Default only Read and ignored by request; non-default catalog-refused (issue 980), since interactive viewer path is unsupported. deconvolutionCatalog domain: bool; Non-default refused when always (#980) signature, reader, interactive-decision nmajor -1 -1; nmajor → nmajor -> ReconstructionControls.maximum_major_cycles (-1 -> None; otherwise Some(limit)); reported nmajordone includes the initial pass. Implemented -1 means unlimited; zero performs only the initial residual/major pass; positive limits count subsequent major passes. Existing controller gives global-threshold and zero-mask stops precedence.20 small standard Stokes-I MFS CLI/Python pairs verify products and exact iteration/major/stop counts; other mode combinations and full return parity are separate behavioral obligations. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader, nmajor-zero fullsummary False False; fullsummary → fullsummary Partial Long-form keys exist, but missing measurements and per-plane values are NaN. Return shape alone is not return-value equivalence. returnsCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, returns, scalars-empty-mask usemask 'user' 'user'; usemask → usemask Partial user and auto-multithresh pass; pb refused (issue 823); controls whether user mask is read. auto-multithresh follows SDMaskHandler::autoMaskByMultiThreshold plane by plane, every channel and Stokes plane of its own: the threshold mask pruned, smoothed and cut, the inherited mask grown through the low-noise threshold, and the negative mask; a cube is masked in tclean's serial channel blocks, each smoothed by the common beam of its planes' PSF beams, every plane thresholded by the image's PSF sidelobe level, and a channel's planes stop together (skipChannels); a plane with no data keeps its mask. CASA takes the automatic mask's statistics and peak inside pb > pblimit where the image has a primary beam (SDMaskHandler::autoMask); casa-rs takes them over every valid pixel, so an image reaching below that response can differ at a mask's edge (issue 980). deconvolutionCatalog domain: auto-multithresh, pb, user signature, reader mask '' ''; mask → mask_box or mask_image Partial One mask image, or CRTF pixel boxes and circles, inline or in a region file, each optionally limited to a spectral range=[...] in frequency or pixels (CASA's channel rounding; a region whose range misses the image is left out). A range over part of a cube masks its channels only, a plane per channel. Bounds clip to the image and outside/empty-region unions mean zero support, not full-plane support. 38 small paired rows pass across CPU64/CPU32/Metal32 and public Python; explicit empty-file + fresh numbering preserves old products and adds no components. Absent masks still permit normal cleaning. A mask image is expanded to the image's planes as SDMaskHandler::expandMask does (a continuum Stokes I mask to every plane, a continuum mask of the image's Stokes planes to every channel, a cube Stokes I mask to every Stokes plane) and refused where CASA refuses; regridding a mask along frequency or Stokes (copyMask) is refused (issue 980). Fractional/world/general CRTF, multiple images, new masks on occupied default-restart outputs and broader mask/mode combinations remain unfinished. deconvolutionCatalog domain: list[string], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, approved-comparisons-restart, scalars-empty-mask, mask-boxes pbmask 0.0 0.0; pbmask → pbmask Default only Read and ignored; non-default catalog-refused (issue 980): a primary-beam limit of user and automatic masks, and usemask='pb' (issue 823), needs the primary beam at every mask boundary. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float; Non-default refused when always (#1061) signature, reader sidelobethreshold 3.0 3.0; sidelobethreshold → sidelobethreshold Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader noisethreshold 5.0 5.0; noisethreshold → noisethreshold Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader lownoisethreshold 1.5 1.5; lownoisethreshold → lownoisethreshold Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader negativethreshold 0.0 0.0; negativethreshold → negativethreshold Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader smoothfactor 1.0 1.0; smoothfactor → smoothfactor Implemented Contract 37: auto-multithresh smooths each new, grown and negative mask by smoothfactor PSF beams before its cut (SDMaskHandler::convolveMask). With usemask=auto-multithresh and niter>0 a value of zero or less is refused, as CASA's GaussianBeam refuses it; elsewhere it is read and unused, as in CASA. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader minbeamfrac 0.3 0.3; minbeamfrac → minbeamfrac Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader cutthreshold 0.01 0.01; cutthreshold → cutthreshold Implemented Contract 37: each smoothed auto-multithresh mask keeps the pixels above cutthreshold times its peak; a negative value keeps none, as makeMaskByPerChanThreshold cuts below a negative level; 0.2 or more warns at the first update, as CASA does. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader growiterations 75 75; growiterations → growiterations Implemented Copied as auto-multithresh parameters; presence is still read even outside that mode. deconvolutionCatalog domain: integer signature, reader dogrowprune True True; dogrowprune → dogrowprune Implemented Contract 37: after the first cycle auto-multithresh grows the inherited mask by binary dilation through the low-noise threshold (growiterations); with dogrowprune and minbeamfrac>0 the grown mask is pruned before its smoothing and cut (SDMaskHandler::autoMaskByMultiThreshold). deconvolutionCatalog domain: bool signature, reader minpercentchange -1.0 -1.0; minpercentchange → minpercentchange Implemented Contract 37: a noise-thresholded auto-multithresh plane stops evolving once its mask is empty, or once the cycle threshold is the global threshold and its mask changed by nothing or by less than minpercentchange percent; a negative value disables the change rule (SDMaskHandler::skipChannels). deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader verbose False False; verbose → verbose Implemented Contract 37: each auto-multithresh update logs CASA's automask summary row (printAutomaskSummary) through tracing; it changes no product. deconvolutionCatalog domain: bool signature, reader fastnoise True True; fastnoise → fastnoise Implemented Contract 37: False estimates the noise of nsigma and auto-multithresh as calcRobustImageStatistics does: casacore's Chauvenet statistics (z from the sample count, five iterations) of the valid pixels when the plane has no mask or its mask fills the plane, else the classical median and MAD outside the mask. The first estimate sees no mask; a stopped auto-multithresh plane records zero noise, so nsigma no longer stops it, as in CASA. True takes the classical statistics of every valid pixel. With usemask=user, no mask and nsigma, CASA 6.7.6.14 leaves an empty mask and cleans nothing; casa-rs cleans the whole image (docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md). deconvolutionCatalog domain: bool signature, reader restart True True; restart → restart Partial Contract 36: True continues on an earlier run's products at imagename on the same grid, as SIImageStore opens them: the model (every Taylor term, cube channel and Stokes plane; a mosaic's flat-noise model made physical with the weights the run forms, every Taylor term with term 0's) starts the solve, an existing binary CLEAN mask is reused plane by plane when no mask is given, and calcpsf/calcres=False read the PSF, sums of weights and residual. False keeps contract32's single-main numbering. Refused (#944, #980): outlier fields, another deconvolver family's products, a new user mask or auto-multithresh over an existing CLEAN mask when cleaning, embedded model/mask pixel masks and tabulated spectral axes. Preserving prior image histories remains the owner-agreed deviation. restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, lifecycle, restart-native-current, approved-comparisons-restart, numbering-preview, numbering-activation, continuation-20261102 savemodel 'none' 'none'; savemodel → savemodel Partial Copied. modelcolumn writes MODEL_DATA; request checks a solved or start model exists. virtual saves the final model as CASA's virtual model (casa_ms::virtual_model): the selection's fields'/windows' models are cleared first (VisModelData::clearModel), then the standard gridder's GridFT record (MultiTermFTNew over GridFT for mtmfs) and its FT_MODEL grid image are filed, incrementally, under SOURCE (rows and a known source) or MAIN keywords as CASA 6.7.6.14 files them; CASA predicts from them what it predicts from its own. A model of no flux saves nothing. Other gridders, polarizations than I, facets and outlier fields are refused (issue 823). returnsCatalog domain: modelcolumn, none, virtual signature, reader, virtual-model calcres True True; calcres → calcres Partial Contract 36: False runs no major cycle before the first minor cycle and cleans the residual an earlier run left at imagename, read with its sums of weights as the unnormalized normal state (task_tclean.py; not counted in nmajordone). With no residual and niter=0 the run makes the PSF alone in a PSF-only pass (psf, sumwt, pb). niter=0 with savemodel predicts the read model (predictModel) and leaves the residual as read. Refused: niter>0 with no earlier residual, and mosaic, A-projection, facets or outliers (#980). restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, continuation-20261102 calcpsf True True; calcpsf → calcpsf Partial Contract 36: False reads the PSF and sums of weights an earlier run left (each channel and Stokes plane's, or a Taylor family's 2*nterms-1 moments) in place of gridding them; the restoring beam is fitted on the PSF read and the primary beam formed as before. Refused: no earlier PSF or .sumwt, and mosaic, A-projection, facets or outliers (#980). restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, continuation-20261102 psfcutoff 0.35 0.35; psfcutoff → psfcutoff Implemented Copied; request requires positive value. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader parallel False False; parallel → parallel Partial Native local worker resource policy, not CASA MPI launch/partition semantics. Ordinary output equivalence and resource bounds require separate evidence; distributed behavior is unfinished. accuracyCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, adopted-defaults

docs.title: tclean interacting modes and task behavior
Selection and multi-MS inputs
docs.text:
Partial — vis, field, spw, timerange, uvrange, antenna, scan, observation, intent, datacolumn and selectdata (#54).

IDs/ranges, names/simple patterns, mixed field lists, SPW/channel text, intent and UV limits are routed natively. Sixteen field cases compare exact physical MAIN row order or refusal with CASA, including flagged and padded FIELD metadata. Since the main imaging cutover was integrated (3016f1b), FIELD selection resolves over the observation catalogue's FIELD rows on MSv2 and MSv4 alike; on the production traversal the field cases of the CASA row oracle (IDs, names, glob, mixed, range) and both refusals read exactly CASA's physical MAIN rows. Production T1 compares ID/name selections with selectdata=False on the single native route. Scan and observation selection is active from tclean contract 33 (owner decision 2026-11-02): on that path scan 1, scan 3 and observation 0 read exactly CASA's rows, and T1 images each numeric selection as its equivalent FIELD selection with either selectdata value and refuses CASA's refused forms without writing images. Through the public Python task, 13 science cases and 23 CASA grammar cases pass against CASA on CPU64, CPU32 and Metal32 (108/108). CODE/numeric-name fallback, advanced field forms, richer scan/observation grammar, remain unfinished; a vis list images as one observation from contract 38, as CASA's tclean does (awproject with several MeasurementSets is refused, #980); antenna and timerange are active from contract 34 (timerange on MeasurementSets only). Image-science comparisons for selected real datasets, flags, channel membership and data-column fallback remain separate required evidence.

Evidence: reader, representative, field-selection, cloud-continuation, scan-observation-activation, vis-list-20261102.

docs.title: Restart, product persistence and recalculation
docs.text:
Partial — imagename, restart, startmodel, calcres, calcpsf, restoration; main and outlier fields (#944).

Contract 36 continues every spectral mode, Taylor family and Stokes set of the main image and activates calcres/calcpsf (CASA test-case matrix at 4fe0e56: 11/48 restart/calcres/calcpsf cases pass, from 1/48 counting the 74a3b85 run's CASA refusals as environment failures; the rest are blocked by other gaps or an f32 scalar floor). Earlier: paired CASA 6.7.6.14 small standard Stokes-I MFS defaults pass (18 native 10->0->10 rows, 6 persisted nontrivial-mask cases, 6 CASA-to-native and 2 native-to-CASA continuations). Embedded model/mask pixel masks, tabulated spectral grids, new explicit/auto masks over occupied masks when cleaning, outliers, and reads under mosaic/A-projection/facets remain unfinished; concurrency at one prefix unassessed. CASA mutates prior logtables whereas native preserves them (owner-agreed). New-image history completeness remains unfinished. This is not general persistence or full metadata acceptance.

Evidence: reader, lifecycle, restart-native-current, approved-comparisons-restart, scalars-empty-mask, numbering-preview, numbering-activation, continuation-20261102.

docs.title: Cube axes, reference frequencies and moving sources
docs.text:
Partial — specmode, spw, start, width, nchan, reffreq, restfreq, outframe, veltype, interpolation and perchanweightdensity.

Cube channel-count mapping exists, but selected-channel-derived defaults are refused; a cube over several selected windows lays its axis over their channels merged as CASA's MSTransformRegridder::combineSpwsCore merges them, grids every window's rows onto it, and with nchan=-1 counts a channel grid's planes over the merged band as regridChanBounds does (#980); MFS outframe (LSRK/BARY/TOPO, header only, gridding stays LSRK as in CASA) and restfreq lists (first active, the others listed in the header) are read; MFS REST outframe, blank restfreq entries and cubic interpolation remain restricted. Moving-source cubesource needs its own representative oracle (#714). MVC removal is a separate prior owner decision, not a passing moving-source comparison. The moving-MFS spectral envelope now uses CASA FIELD-origin direction semantics; six fixed/moving CPU64/CPU32/GPU32 comparisons pass recorded WCS values, and the previous 3.5 Hz increment mismatch is repaired at its unchanged tolerance. This does not complete moving-PB or cubesource acceptance. The ordinary MFS default SOURCE rest-frequency label is now repaired; five fresh mosaic/AW weight families and small restart metadata checks match. DOPPLER-backed SOURCE lookup and multiple SOURCE key groups with stored wildcards are explicitly unfinished, not approved deviations. The MFS header's first visibility field is the least (ARRAY_ID, DATA_DESC_ID, FIELD_ID) of the selected samples, CASA's buffer order: the MSv2 adapter states each partition's array and the survey reads the rows' arrays for a partition holding several (3bdf6fa, after Astra's review found the merge had dropped ARRAY_ID); a T1 run with opposing arrays records CASA's choice. An MSv4 has no arrays. The moving-MFS increment oracle on the catalogue path gives CASA's 125020996.11132812 Hz exactly (8b0fe44).

Evidence: reader, representative, mvc-decision, taylor-pb-mfs, approved-comparisons-restart, cloud-continuation.

docs.title: Gridder, weighting and beam combinations
docs.text:
Partial — standard/W/mosaic/AW, rectangular geometry, facets, normtype, beam terms and density weighting.

Rectangular standard/W/mosaic and uvtaper were implemented in #970. AW remains square/equal-cell and MFS-only; it reads tclean's aterm, psterm, wbawp, conjbeams and any positive wprojplanes (#980), and an imported CASA cache must already exist: where cfcache names a missing directory CASA fills it, casa-rs refuses (aw_cf_source=native-evla generates its own). Odd cells an older CASA wrote (test_mosaic_mtmfs's staged caches) are read about CASA's convOrigin, shape/2+1; on those cases the PSF agrees to 1e-7 but CASA's weight image is 0.8% above casa-rs's in scale, and CASA's second call into the same image leaves weight.tt1 and weight.tt2 undivided by sumwt; both are open (#980). Mosaic per-field density weighting (mosweight) is implemented, continuum and a cube's per-channel density (BriggsCubeWeightor multiField, #818); W/AW facets and additional gridders/weightings remain incomplete. Native CF generation is verified separately from CASA cache oracles. The native write_pb default is True. Homogeneous ALMA-labelled 7m arrays select ACA; legacy VLA PB now covers all named bands and NVSS frequency gaps. Fresh ordinary-default W/Hogbom20 CPU64/CPU32 runs pass all seven products, with PB NRMS zero. One ALMA mosaic field imaged at its own centre agrees with CASA to 1e-7 with sumwt exact, uniform and Briggs; at its neighbour's centre it differs (uniform PSF 2.6e-2), and an evidence-only build that grids the density at GridFT's rotation and looks it up at the MeasurementSet uvw, as CASA does, matches all 130,032 of CASA's (row, channel) weights to 4.2e-10 (docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md). Three fields together at the test's centre: uniform PSF 9.3e-3, Briggs 5.6e-4. An EVLA mosaic cube differs even for one field at its own centre, with or without mosweight (PSF 3.6e-3), unattributed (#789). Native: T0 per-field cube density law, T1 sumwt additivity over fields, and the density pass's counting law with every field's cube.

docs.title: Simulation programme: CASA's sm, simobserve, simanalyze and simalma in Rust
docs.text: Truth class: normative plan Date: 2026-10-20 Work issue: #841, which keeps the phase checklist and status Status: accepted by the owner on 2026-10-20.

docs.title: 1. Goal and requirements
docs.text:
Make CASA simulation scripts run on casa-rs with only their imports changed, and run them dramatically faster:

  • the simulator tool (sm), with every user-facing method under CASA's name, signature and effective default;
  • the simobserve, simanalyze and simalma tasks, with CASA's parameters and defaults.

Requirements:

  • ADR-0017, ADR-0018 and ADR-0019 apply. All computation is in Rust, including the parts CASA writes in Python (task_simobserve.py, task_simanalyze.py, task_simalma.py, simutil.py); Python only presents CASA's interface.
  • Agreement with CASA follows AGENTS.md. The MS has CASA's columns, subtables and keywords, apart from decision 6; predicted visibilities agree to about 1e-3 normalized RMS; noise and corruptions are statistically equivalent, not bit-identical. casacore C++ reads the MS, proved by an interop test.
  • Performance is the point. Prediction uses Metal where it pays; geometry, prediction, corruption and writing use multiple workers; results do not depend on the worker count or the backend. Every benchmark reports wall time, single-worker (W1) user CPU and peak RSS, so parallelism cannot mask serial cost. The targets are in §5.
  • Memory is bounded. Peak resident memory stays under a declared budget whatever the number of rows, channels or fields, proved by a counting-law test. Work streams in time and channel chunks sized from the budget, and Metal device buffers count against it. The MS write session stays bounded (ADR-0008).
  • The MS write path may be optimized; what is on disk may not change. The same storage managers, tile formats and table metadata, guarded by the casacore C++ interop tests. The simulator writes every row in the layout casa-rs's other MS writers share, not NewMSSimulator's.

docs.title: 2. Status
docs.text: Phases 1 to 5 are merged, except 5e (simobserve graphics), which is now part of #1025. By the owner's priority of 2026-10-31 (#841), the new tasks of Phase 6 wait until the existing conversions reach behavioral equivalence with CASA; their design and dependencies stand (§6). Phase 7 follows.

docs.title: 3. Owner decisions (accepted 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
1. Namespace. CASA tool classes are in casars.tools under casatools' names, tasks in casars.tasks; there are no casatools or casatasks alias packages (ADR-0019).
  2. The simobserve surface is CASA's. The old family generator is the developer binary synthetic-ms, outside the catalog.
  3. casa-simulation is an application-layer crate in ADR-0016's dependency policy. simulation.rs, simulation_task.rs and casa-simulation-synthesis are deleted at the end (Phase 7).
  4. ATM is ported to Rust as casa-atmosphere.
  5. TIME honours the requested UTC. CASA computes its geometry at the requested time + (TAI − UTC); the divergence is recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md. A parity run requests a start later by TAI − UTC at the reference epoch and compares rows at equal stored TIME.
  6. DATA only, unless a later step needs MODEL_DATA. MODEL_DATA is created only when something needs it, and CORRECTED_DATA is not written. casa-rs's imager falls back from datacolumn='corrected' to DATA, as CASA's tclean does.

docs.title: Deferred, single-pass execution
docs.text: The session records observe, predict and corrupt as a plan and, at close/done, materializes the MS in one streamed pass (geometry, prediction, corruption and the write for each chunk), published at close as ADR-0008 staging requires. The plan is a fold: each predict and corrupt applies to the scans observed before it, and a predict that is not incremental replaces every step before it. A call that needs data on disk forces the pending pass. Corrupting an existing MS (openfromms + corrupt) patches it in place through the bounded selected-row mutation path, in chunks aligned to the DATA tile.

docs.title: Prediction
docs.text: Prediction goes through the imaging operator, so simulation and imaging share one forward model, and through casa-imaging-runtime's worker teams, Metal backends and budget (HostResources, ResourcePolicy): the simulator builds no second budget or worker model. Total power is image-plane sampling of the model convolved with the primary beam, in casa-imaging-singledish.

docs.title: Random numbers
docs.text: A counter-based generator keys each draw by seed, row, channel, correlation and real/imaginary part, so noise is bitwise identical for any worker count, chunking or backend. It is not CASA's MLCG stream.

docs.title: CASA quirks
docs.text: CASA quirks that shape outputs users compare are matched (default limits, SIGMA and WEIGHT left at their geometric values after corrupt, noise scaling, fBM normalization, scan numbering, autocorrelation defaults). casa-rs diverges only for crashes, undefined behaviour or data corruption, such as setmosaicfield's integer division; every divergence is recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md.

docs.title: 5. Performance and I/O targets
docs.text:
Each benchmark is timed for CASA, the old simulator, and casa-rs on CPU and on Metal. CASA's time is measured in-process, per call, excluding Python start-up.

Mode Target Analytic and component-list prediction No slower than July's record (#257) on the same case; the CASA multiple measured on a case where CASA runs ≥ 60 s. Image-model prediction, CPU ≥ 10× CASA on the same input, with W1 user CPU reported. Image-model prediction, Metal I/O-bound: meets the I/O target below; the CASA multiple reported. I/O-bound passes (geometry only, noise only, write only) Judged against the device's ceiling, not against CASA.

No-regression rule. On every case, the new simulator is no slower than the old one, within 5%; a trade-off needs owner approval.

I/O target. The sustained MAIN-table rate (bytes on disk over the wall time from the first row to publication, including the final sync), on a dataset at least twice the size of RAM with the page cache purged, is at least 70% of the same volume's raw sequential-write ceiling for the write-only case and at least 50% end to end with Metal prediction (tools/simulation/bench_sustained_io.py). Phase 1 met both on the external NVMe drive (owner decision, 2026-10-22, #855). The 1 GiB internal-disk case stays as a quick, cache-resident check.

Benchmark cases. ALMA (about 43 antennas, 1 h of 10 s integrations, 256 channels, a 1024² image model); VLA of similar size; one MFS model plane degridded at 256 frequencies; analytic and component-list models; write only.

docs.title: 6. Phases
docs.text: Phases 1 to 5 are on #841. What remains:

docs.title: Phase 6: simanalyze and simalma
docs.text:
Scope (planned 2026-10-27; the split is on #841). - Both tasks, ported to Rust (ADR-0018) from CASA 6.7.6's installed task_simanalyze.py and task_simalma.py, with the simutil and sdbeamutil parts they use: imtclean, convimage, statim, cellsize, ismstp, primaryBeamArcsec and TheoreticalBeam. - simanalyze: finds the project's MeasurementSets and sky model; grids total power with tsdimaging; concatenates several interferometric MeasurementSets and images them through the imager, with tclean's arguments as imtclean builds them; feathers; and analyses the convolved model, the difference, the fidelity and the statistics. - simalma: runs simobserve, simanalyze, concat and feather. Its own logic chooses the configurations and allocates the time; it lays out the total-power pointings, scales the total power, and makes the primary-beam-weighted feather. - The Python surfaces mimic CASA's exactly from the start (#931).

Owner decisions (2026-10-27). - The single-dish gridder is in its own library crate, casa-imaging-singledish (#938), which holds the kernels, the image-plane gridder and simobserve's total-power predictor (the gridder's adjoint). Single-dish image-plane gridding is its own operator family, outside ADR-0016's four interferometric kernel sets. - tsdimaging and concat read and write through casa-observation (#937, #938, #939), not through casa-ms's older access paths.

Decided in planning. Each part records these in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md when it implements them. - Total-power intensity scaling: each task keeps its own formula, which differ by 8.7%. A part departs from one only if it measures that formula to be physically wrong. - simalma's TypeError for configuration names without "cycleN" (task_simalma.py:523) is fixed. - The user's modelimage is not changed in place; CASA's master branch has removed those lines. - No .tclean.last is written (#931: no Last profiles from Python). - Products do not depend on graphics. In CASA, simalma's combine figure deletes simanalyze's flat images. - Sky-model discovery takes candidates in sorted order, not in glob order. - Acceptance avoids simanalyze's feather of total power with interferometer data, which is not primary-beam weighted. CASA skips its own test of that path because feather fails. The simanalyze part decides it by the better-physics rule; simalma's weighted feather is the candidate.

Parts, one PR each. 6a (image analysis in casa-images), 6b (imager startmodel, uvtaper, non-square imsize, optimum size), 6c (the casa-imaging-singledish core) and 6f (simanalyze's analysis) are merged.

Part Content Waits for 6d tsdimaging on casa-observation (#938 part 2) #931 2a and 3 6e concat core on casa-observation (#939) #931 2a and 3 6g simanalyze: discovery, imaging, total power, concat, feather; its host and Python surface 6d, 6e, #931 3 6h simalma 6g 6i Graphics for both, on 5e's plot document 5e (#1025)

Acceptance. - regression/sim_multi_arrays_and_TP. It runs simobserve for 12 m, 7 m and total power, then simanalyze twice. - The oracle is CASA 6.7.6-14's products, regenerated by a committed recipe. The references in the test data are from an older CASA: 6.7.6-14 differs from them by 4–7% NRMS in DATA. - Compared by NRMS: the MeasurementSets (DATA within 1e-6, as in Phase 5), the total-power image, and the images and difference images. - regression/simalma_12m_ACA_combination. CASA's test checks only that 14 PNGs and 5 MeasurementSets exist. Acceptance instead compares every product with CASA 6.7.6-14's: the MeasurementSets, the concatenation included; the total-power image, each configuration's image and the concatenation's; the feathered image, the differences and the fidelities. The PNGs come after 6i. - Timing rows for both cases, against CASA. The multi-array case takes about 30 s in CASA 6.7.6-14 on the Mac mini.

docs.title: Phase 7: retire the old code
docs.text:
Scope. - Delete simulation.rs, simulation_task.rs and casa-simulation-synthesis, shrinking the file-length allowlist. - Move the imaging T1 fixtures and the perf benches to the new API. - Update the capability matrix and the docs.

Acceptance. No caller of the old API remains, and just quick is green.

docs.title: CASA Tutorial Parity
docs.text:
Truth class: current descriptive Last reality check: 2026-11-02 Verification: just docs-check

The CASA Guide "First Look" tutorials are checked section by section by the declarative runner in scripts/tutorial_parity. Its twelve version-1 section manifests (scripts/tutorial_parity/sections/) cover First Look at Image Analysis (imhead, imstat, immoments, exportfits) and First Look at Imaging (from listobs and the uv-coverage plots through cleaning and primary-beam correction). Each section runs on three surfaces, CASA, the command line and Python, and compares their products.

docs.title: Runtime contract
docs.text:
• CASA_RS_TUTORIAL_DATA_ROOT is the only tutorial-data root; it holds the pack paths the manifests declare.
  • CASA_RS_CASA_PYTHON selects the optional CASA oracle interpreter.
  • Native Python is found by scripts/resolve-python.sh and counts only when it can import the installed casars._core extension.
  • Task and parameter names are allowlisted by the schema. Workers accept only JSON requests produced from validated manifests, never Python or shell fragments.
  • A missing CASA, native Python, network or dataset is recorded as typed unavailable evidence, never as a success or a fallback to another surface.
  • Plot sections compare text point manifests; casa-rs does not render PNG plots.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Validate the manifests and list the sections, without external resources:

python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py validate --all
python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py run --dry-run --all

Run one section (omit --surface for all three):

python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py run \
  --section alma-first-look-image-analysis:01-imhead-continuum-header \
  --surface casa --surface cli --surface python

Evidence, review records and the section's Markdown and HTML documentation are written atomically under the pack paths the manifest declares. The runner's tests run with scripts/test-perf-tools.sh.
